1.1: A vision of Isaiah, the sonne of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem: in the dayes of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah Kings of Judah.
1.2: Hear, O heavens, and hearken, O earth: for the Lord hath sayde, I have nourished and brought up children, but they have rebelled against me.
1.3: The oxe knoweth his owner, and the ass his masters crib: but Israel hath not knowen: my people hath not understand.
1.4: Ah, sinful nation, a people laden with iniquitie: a seed of the wicked, corrupt children: they have forsaken the Lord: they have provoked the holy one of Israel to anger: they are gone backewarde.
1.5: Wherefore should ye be smitten any more? for ye fall away more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is heauie.
1.6: From the sole of the foot unto the head, there is nothing whole therein, but wounds, and swelling, and sores full of corruption: they have not been wrapped, nor bound up, nor mollified with oyle.
1.7: Your land is waste: your cities are burnt with fire: strangers deuoure your land in your presence, and it is desolate like the overthrow of strangers.
1.8: And the daughter of Zion shall remain like a cotage in a vineyard, like a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and like a besieged citie.
1.9: Except the Lord of hostes had reserved unto us, even a small remnant: we should have been as Sodom, and should have been like unto Gomorah.
1.10: Hear the word of the Lord, O princes of Sodom: hearken unto the Law of our God, O people of Gomorah.
1.11: What have I to doe with the multitude of your sacrifices, sayth the Lord? I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and of the fat of fed beasts: and I desire not the blood of bullocks, nor of lambs, nor of goates.
1.12: When ye come to appear before me, who required this of your hands to tread in my courts?
1.13: Bring no more oblations, in vain: incense is an abomination unto me: I can not suffer your new moones, nor Sabbaths, nor solemn dayes (it is iniquitie) nor solemn assemblies.
1.14: My soul hateth your new moones and your appointed feastes: they are a burden unto me: I am weary to bear them.
1.15: And when you shall stretch out your hands, I wil hide mine eyes from you: and though ye make many prayers, I wil not hear: for your hands are full of blood.
1.16: Wash you, make you clean: take away the evil of your workes from before mine eyes: cease to doe evil.
1.17: Learn to doe well: seek iudgement, relieve the oppressed: judge the fatherless and defend the widow.
1.18: Come now, and let us reason together, sayth the Lord: though your sinnes were as crimsin, they shalbe made white as snow: though they were red like skarlet, they shalbe as wool.
1.19: If ye consent and obey, ye shall eat the good things of the land.
1.20: But if ye refuse and be rebellious, ye shalbe deuoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
1.21: How is the faithful citie become an harlot? it was full of iudgement, and justice lodged therein, but now they are murtherers.
1.22: Thy silver is become dross: thy wine is mixt with water.
1.23: Thy Princes are rebellious and companions of theeues: every one loveth giftes, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doeth the widowes cause come before them.
1.24: Therefore sayth the Lord God of hostes, the mightie one of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies.
1.25: Then I will turn mine hand upon thee, and burn out thy dross, till it be pure, and take away all thy tinne.
1.26: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellers as at the beginning: afterward shalt thou be called a citie of righteousnes, and a faithful citie.
1.27: Zion shall be redeemed in iudgement, and they that return in her, in justice.
1.28: And the destruction of the transgressers and of the sinners shalbe together: and they that forsake the Lord, shalbe consumed.
1.29: For they shalbe confounded for the okes, which ye have desired, and ye shall be ashamed of the gardens, that ye have chosen.
1.30: For ye shalbe as an oke, whose leaf fadeth: and as a garden that hath no water.
1.31: And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker thereof, as a spark: and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

2.1: The word that Isaiah the sonne of Amoz saw upon Judah and Jerusalem.
2.2: It shall be in the last dayes, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shalbe prepared in the top of the mountaines, and shall be exalted above the hilles, and all nations shall flow unto it.
2.3: And many people shall go, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Iaakob, and hee will teach us his wayes, and we will walk in his paths: for the Law shall go foorth of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem,
2.4: And he shall judge among the nations, and rebuke many people: they shall break their swords also into mattocks, and their speares into siethes: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn to fight any more.
2.5: O house of Iaakob, come ye, and let us walk in the Law of the Lord.
2.6: Surely thou hast forsaken thy people, the house of Iaakob, because they are full of the East maners, and are sorcerers as the Philistims, and abound with strange children.
2.7: Their land also was full of silver and gold, and there was none end of their treasures: and their land was full of horses, and their charets were infinite.
2.8: Their land also was full of idols: they worshipped the work of their own hands, which their own fingers have made.
2.9: And a man bowed himself, and a man humbled himself: therefore spare them not.
2.10: Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust from before the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his maiestie.
2.11: The hie look of man shall be humbled, and the loftiness of men shalbe abased, and the Lord onely shall be exalted in that day.
2.12: For the day of the Lord of hostes is upon all the proud and hautie, and upon all that is exalted: and it shalbe made low.
2.13: Even upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are hie and exalted, and upon all the okes of Bashan,
2.14: And upon all the hie mountaines, and upon all the hilles that are lifted up,
2.15: And upon every hie tower, and upon every strong wall,
2.16: And upon all the shippes of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant pictures.
2.17: And the hautinesse of men shalbe brought low, and the loftiness of men shalbe abased, and the Lord shall onely be exalted in that day.
2.18: And the idoles will he utterly destroy.
2.19: Then they shall goe into the holes of the rockes, and into the caves of the earth, from before the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his maiestie, when he shall arise to destroy the earth.
2.20: At that day shall man cast away his silver idoles, and his golden idoles (which they had made themselves to worship them) to the mowles and to the backes,
2.21: To goe into the holes of the rockes, and into the toppes of the ragged rockes from before the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his maiestie, when he shall rise to destroy the earth.
2.22: Cease you from the man whose breath is in his nostrels: for wherein is he to be esteemed?

3.1: For lo, the Lord God of hostes will take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the strength: even all the stay of bread, and all the stay of water,
3.2: The strong man, and the man of war, the judge and the prophet, the prudent and the aged,
3.3: The captain of fiftie, and the honourable, and the counseller, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent man.
3.4: And I will appoint children to bee their princes, and babes shall rule over them.
3.5: The people shalbe oppressed one of another, and every one by his neighbour: the children shall presume against the ancient, and the vile against the honourable.
3.6: When every one shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, and say, Thou hast clothing: thou shalt bee our prince, and let this fall be under thine hand.
3.7: In that day hee shall swear, saying, I cannot bee an helper: for there is no bread in mine house, nor clothing: therefore make me no prince of the people.
3.8: Doubtless Jerusalem is fallen, and Judah is fallen down, because their tongue and workes are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his glory.
3.9: The trial of their countenance testifieth against them, yea, they declare their sinnes as Sodom, they hide them not. Wo be unto their soules: for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.
3.10: Say ye, Surely it shalbe well with the just: for they shall eat the fruit of their workes.
3.11: Woe be to the wicked, it shalbe evil with him: for the reward of his handes shalbe given him.
3.12: Children are extortioners of my people, and women have rule over them: O my people, they that lead thee, cause thee to ere, and destroy the way of thy paths.
3.13: The Lord standeth up to plead, yea, hee standeth to judge the people.
3.14: The Lord shall enter into iudgement with the Ancients of his people and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard: the spoyle of the poor is in your houses.
3.15: What have ye to do, that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor, saith the Lord, even the Lord of hoasts?
3.16: The Lord also saith, Because the daughters of Zion are hautie, and walk with stretched out neckes, and with wandering eyes, walking and minsing as they goe, and making a tinkeling with their feet,
3.17: Therefore shall the Lord make the heades of the daughters of Zion bald, and the Lord shall discover their secret partes.
3.18: In that day shall the Lord take away the ornament of the slippers, and the calles, and the round tyres,
3.19: The sweet balles, and the brasselets, and the bonnets,
3.20: The tyres of the head, and the sloppes, and the head bandes, and the tablets, and the earings,
3.22: The costly apparell and the vailes, and the wimples, and the crisping pinnes,
3.23: And the glasses and the fine linen, and the hoodes, and the launes.
3.24: And in stead of sweet sauour, there shall be stink, and in stead of a girdle, a rent, and in stead of dressing of the hear, baldness, and in stead of a stomacher, a girding of sackecloth, and burning in stead of beautie.
3.25: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy strength in the battell.
3.26: Then shall her gates mourn and lament, and she, being desolate, shall sit upon the ground.

4.1: And in that day shall seven women take hold of one man, saying, Wee will eat our own bread, and we wil wear our own garments: onely let us bee called by thy name, and take away our reproche.
4.2: In that day shall the budde of the Lord bee beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shalbe excellent and pleasant for them that are escaped of Israel.
4.3: Then hee that shalbe left in Zion, and hee that shall remain in Jerusalem, shalbe called holy, and every one shalbe written among the living in Jerusalem,
4.4: When the Lord shall wash the filthines of the daughters of Zion, and purge the blood of Jerusalem out of the middes thereof by the spirit of iudgement, and by the spirit of burning.
4.5: And the Lord shall create upon every place of mount Zion, and upon the assemblies thereof, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence.
4.6: And a covering shalbe for a shadow in the day for the heat, and a place of refuge and a covert for the storm and for the rain.

5.1: Now will I sing to my beloved a song of my beloved to his vineyard, My beloved had a vineyard in a very fruitefull hill,
5.2: And hee hedged it, and gathered out the stones of it, and he planted it with the best plants, and hee built a towre in the middes thereof, and made a wine press therein: then hee looked that it should bring foorth grapes: but it brought foorth wild grapes.
5.3: Now therefore, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me, and my vineyard.
5.4: What could I have done any more to my vineyard that I have not done unto it? why have I looked that it should bring foorth grapes, and it bringeth foorth wild grapes?
5.5: And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up: I will break the wall thereof, and it shall be troden down:
5.6: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be cut, nor digged, but briers, and thornes shall grow up: I will also command the cloudes that they rain no rain upon it.
5.7: Surely the vineyard of the Lord of hostes is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his pleasant plant, and hee looked for iudgement, but behold oppression: for righteousness, but behold a crying.
5.8: Woe unto them that ioyne house to house, and lay field to field, till there bee no place, that ye may be placed by your selves in the mids of the earth.
5.9: This is in mine cares, saith the Lord of hostes. Surely many houses shall be desolate, even great, and fair without inhabitant.
5.10: For ten acres of vines shall yelde one bath, and the seed of an homer shall yelde an ephah.
5.11: Wo unto them, that rise up early to follow drunkennes, and to them that continue until night, till the wine doe inflame them.
5.12: And the harp and viol, timbrel, and pipe, and wine are in their feastes: but they regard not the work of the Lord, neither consider the work of his handes.
5.13: Therefore my people is gone into captiuitie, because they had no knowledge, and the glorie thereof are men famished, and the multitude thereof is dried up with thirst.
5.14: Therefore hell hath inlarged it self, and hath opened his mouth, without measure, and their glorie, and their multitude, and their pomp, and hee that reioyceth among them, shall descend into it.
5.15: And man shalbe brought down, and man shalbe humbled, even the eyes of the proud shalbe humbled.
5.16: And the Lord of hostes shalbe exalted in iudgement, and the holy God shalbe sanctified in justice.
5.17: Then shall the lambes feed after their maner, and the strangers shall eat the desolate places of the fat.
5.18: Woe unto them, that draw iniquitie with cordes of vanitie, and sinne, as with cart ropes:
5.19: Which say, Let him make speed: let him hasten his work, that wee may see it: and let the counsel of the holy one of Israel draw neere and come, that we may know it.
5.20: Woe unto them that speak good of evil, and evil of good, which put darkenes for light, and light for darkenes, that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for sowre.
5.21: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight.
5.22: Wo unto them that are mightie to drink wine, and to them that are strong to powre in strong drink:
5.23: Which iustifie the wicked for a reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him.
5.24: Therefore as the flame of fire deuoureth the stubble, and as the chaff is cosumed of the flame: so their root shalbe as rottenness, and their bud shall rise up like dust, because they have cast off the Law of the Lord of hostes, and contemned the word of the holy one of Israel.
5.25: Therefore is the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, and hee hath stretched out his hand upon them, and hath smitten them that the mountaines did tremble: and their carkases were torn in the middes of the streetes, and for all this his wrath was not turned away, but his hand was stretched out still.
5.26: And he will lift up a sign unto the nations a far, and wil hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and behold, they shall come hastily with speed.
5.27: None shall faint nor fall among them: none shall slumber nor sleep, neither shall the girdle of his loynes be loosed, nor the latchet of his shooes be broken:
5.28: Whose arrowes shall be sharp, and all his bowes bent: his horse hoofes shall be thought like flint, and his wheeles like a whirlewinde.
5.29: His roaring shalbe like a lyon, and he shall roar like lyons whelpes: they shall roar, and lay hold of the pray: they shall take it away, and none shall deliver it.
5.30: And in that day they shall roar upon them, as the roaring of the sea: and if they look unto the earth, behold darkenesse, and sorowe, and the light shalbe darkened in their skie.

6.1: In the yeere of the death of King Uzziah, I saw also the Lord sitting upon an high throne, and lifted up, and the lower partes thereof filled the Temple.
6.2: The Seraphims stood upon it: every one had six wings: with twain he covered his face, and with twain hee covered his feet, and with twain he did flie.
6.3: And one cryed to another, and sayde, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hostes: the whole world is full of his glory.
6.4: And the lintles of the door cheekes moved at the voyce of him that cryed, and the house was filled with smoke.
6.5: Then I sayd, Wo is me: for I am undone, because I am a man of polluted lips, and I dwell in the middes of a people of polluted lips: for mine eyes have seen the King and Lord of hostes.
6.6: Then flew one of the Seraphims unto me with an hot cole in his hand, which he had taken from the altar with the tongs:
6.7: And he touched my mouth, and sayd, Loe, this hath touched thy lips, and thine iniquitie shall be taken away, and thy sinne shalbe purged.
6.8: Also I heard the voyce of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send? and who shall goe for us? Then I sayd, Here am I, send me.
6.9: And he sayd, Goe, and say unto this people, Ye shall hear in deed, but ye shall not understand: ye shall plainely see, and not perceive.
6.10: Make the heart of this people fatte, make their eares heauie, and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their eares, and understand with their hearts, and convert, and he heal them.
6.11: Then sayd I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,
6.12: And the Lord have removed men far away, and there be a great desolation in the mids of the land.
6.13: But yet in it shalbe a tenth, and shall return, and shalbe eaten up as an elme or an oke, which have a substance in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

7.1: And in the dayes of Ahaz, the sonne of Jotham, the sonne of Uzziah king of Judah, Rezin the King of Aram came up, and Pekah the sonne of Remaliah King of Israel, to Jerusalem to fight against it, but he could not overcome it.
7.2: And it was told the house of David, saying, Aram is ioyned with Ephraim: therefore his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest are moved by the wind.
7.3: Then sayde the Lord unto Isaiah, Goe foorth now to meet Ahaz (thou and Sheariashub thy sonne) at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the path of the fullers field,
7.4: And say unto him, Take heed, and be still: fear not, neither be faint hearted for the two tailes of these smoking firebrands, for the furious wrath of Rezin and of Aram, and of Remaliahs sonne:
7.5: Because Aram hath taken wicked counsel against thee, and Ephraim, and Remaliahs sonne, saying,
7.6: Let us goe up against Judah, and let us waken them up, and make a breach therein for us, and set a King in the mids thereof, even the sonne of Tabeal.
7.7: Thus sayth the Lord God, It shall not stand, neither shall it be.
7.8: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin: and within five and threescore yeere, Ephraim shalbe destroyed from being a people.
7.9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliahs sonne. If ye beleeue not, surely ye shall not be established.
7.10: And the Lord spake again unto Ahaz, saying,
7.11: Ask a sign for thee of the Lord thy God: ask it, either in the depth beneath or in the height above.
7.12: But Ahaz sayd, I wil not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord.
7.13: Then he sayd, Hear you now, O house of David, Is it a small thing for you to grieve men, that ye will also grieve my God?
7.14: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a sonne, and she shall call his name Immanu-el.
7.15: Butter and hony shall he eat, till he have knowledge to refuse the evil, and to chuse the good.
7.16: For afore the child shall have knowledge to eschew the evil, and to chuse the good, the land, that thou abhorrest, shalbe forsaken of both her Kings.
7.17: The Lord shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy fathers house (the dayes that have not come from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah) even the King of Asshur.
7.18: And in that day shall the Lord hiss for the flie that is at the uttermost part of the floods of Egypt, and for the bee which is in the land of Asshur,
7.19: And they shall come and shall light all in the desolate valleys, and in the holes of the rockes, and upon all thorny places, and upon all bushy places.
7.20: In that day shall the Lord shave with a rasor that is hired, even by them beyond the River, by the King of Asshur, the head and the hear of the feet, and it shall consume the beard.
7.21: And in the same day shall a man nourish a yong kow, and two sheep.
7.22: And for the abundance of milk, that they shall give, hee shall eat butter: for butter and hony shall every one eat, which is left within the land.
7.23: And at the same day every place, wherein shalbe a thousand vines, shalbe at a thousand pieces of silver: so it shalbe for the briers and for the thornes.
7.24: With arrowes and with bow shall one come thither: because all the land shall be briers and thornes.
7.25: But on all the mountaines, which shalbe digged with the mattock, there shall not come thither the fear of briers and thornes: but they shalbe for the sending out of bullocks, and for the treading of sheep.

8.1: Moreover, the Lord sayd unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a mans penne, Make speed to the spoyle: haste to the pray.
8.2: Then I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the Priest, and Zechariah the sonne of Jeberechiah.
8.3: After, I came unto the Prophetess, which conceived, and bare a sonne. Then sayd the Lord to me, Call his name, Mahershalalhash-baz.
8.4: For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, he shall take away the riches of Damascus and the spoyle of Samaria, before the King of Asshur.
8.5: And the Lord spake yet again unto me, saying,
8.6: Because this people hath refused the waters of Shiloah that runne softly, and reioyce with Rezin, and the sonne of Remaliah,
8.7: Now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the River mightie and great, even the King of Asshur with all his glory, and he shall come up upon all their rivers, and goe over all their banks,
8.8: And shall break into Judah, and shall overflow and pass through, and shall come up to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanu-el.
8.9: Gather together on heapes, O ye people, and ye shalbe broken in pieces, and hearken all ye of far countreys: gird your selves, and you shalbe broken in pieces: gird your selves, and you shalbe broken in pieces.
8.10: Take counsel together, yet it shall be brought to nought: pronounce a decree, yet shall it not stand: for God is with us.
8.11: For the Lord spake thus to me in taking of mine hand, and taught me, that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying,
8.12: Say ye not, A confederacie to all them, to whom this people sayth a confederacie, neither fear you their fear, nor be afrayd of them.
8.13: Sanctifie the Lord of hostes, and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread,
8.14: And he shalbe as a Sanctuarie: but as a stumbling stone, and as a rock to fall upon, to both the houses of Israel, and as a snare and as a net to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
8.15: And many among them shall stumble, and shall fall and shalbe broken and shalbe snared and shalbe taken.
8.16: Bind up the testimonie: seal up the Law among my disciples.
8.17: Therefore I will wait upon the Lord that hath hid his face from the house of Iaakob, and I wil look for him.
8.18: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me, are as signes and as wonders in Israel, by the Lord of hostes, which dwelleth in mount Zion.
8.19: And when they shall say unto you, Enquire at them that have a spirit of divination, and at the soothsayers, which whisper and murmur, Should not a people enquire at their God? from the living to the dead?
8.20: To the Law, and to the testimonie, if they speak not according to this word: it is because there is no light in them.
8.21: Then he that is afflicted and famished, shall go to and from in it: and when he shalbe hungry, he shall even freat himself, and curse his King and his gods, and shall look upward.
8.22: And when he shall look to the earth, behold trouble, and darkenes, vexation and anguish, and he is driven to darkenes.

9.1: Yet the darkenesse shall not be according to the affliction that it had when at the first hee touched lightly the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, nor afteward when he was more grieuous by the way of the sea beyond Iorden in Galile of the Gentiles.
9.2: The people that walked in darkenes have seen a great light: they that dwelled in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.
9.3: Thou hast multiplied the nation, and not increased their ioye: they have reioyced before thee according to the ioye in harvest, and as men reioyce when they deuide a spoyle.
9.4: For the yoke of their burthen, and the staff of their shoulder and the rod of their oppressour hast thou broken as in the day of Midian.
9.5: Surely every battell of the warriour is with noyse, and with tumbling of garments in blood: but this shall be with burning and deuouring of fire.
9.6: For unto us a child is borne, and unto us a Sonne is given: and the gouernement is upon his shoulder, and he shall call his name Wonderful, Counseller, The mightie God, The everlasting Father, The prince of peace,
9.7: The increase of his gouernement and peace shall have none end: he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to stablish it with iudgement and with justice, from hencefoorth, even for ever: the zeal of the Lord of hostes will perform this.
9.8: The Lord hath sent a word into Iaakob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.
9.9: And all the people shall know, even Ephraim, and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in the pride and presumption of the heart,
9.10: The brickes are fallen, but we will build it with hewen stones: the wild figge trees are cut down, but we will change them into ceders.
9.11: Nevertheless the Lord will raise up the adversaries of Rezin against him, and ioyne his enemies together.
9.12: Aram before and the Philistims behind, and they shall deuoure Israel with open mouth: yet for all this his wrath is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
9.13: For the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, neither doe they seek the Lord of hostes.
9.14: Therefore will the Lord cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush in one day.
9.15: The ancient and the honorable man, he is the head: and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.
9.16: For the leaders of the people cause them to ere: and they that are led by them are deuoured.
9.17: Therefore shall the Lord have no pleasure in their yong men, neither will he have compassion of their fatherless and of their widowes: for every one is an hypocrite and wicked, and every mouth speaketh follie: yet for all this his wrath is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out stil.
9.18: For wickedness burneth as a fire: it deuoureth the briers and the thornes and will kindle in the thick places of the forest: and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke.
9.19: By the wrath of the Lord of hostes shall the land be darkened, and the people shall be as the meat of ye fire: no man shall spare his brother.
9.20: And he shall snatch at the right hand, and be hungrie: and he shall eat on the left hand, and shall not be satisfied: every one shall eat ye flesh of his own arm.
9.21: Manasseh, Ephraim: and Ephraim Manasseh, and they both shall be against Judah yet for all this his wrath is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

10.1: Woe unto them that decree wicked decrees, and write grieuous things,
10.2: To keep back ye poor from iudgement, and to take away the iudgement of the poor of my people, that widowes may be their pray, and that they may spoyle the fatherless.
10.3: What will ye doe now in the day of visitation, and of destruction, which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glorie?
10.4: Without me every one shall fall among them that are bound, and they shall fall down among the slayne: yet for all this his wrath is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
10.5: O Asshur, the rod of my wrath: and the staff in their hands is mine indignation.
10.6: I will send him to a dissembling nation, and I will give him a charge against the people of my wrath to take the spoyle and to take the pray, and to tread them under feet like the mire in the street.
10.7: But he thinketh not so, neither doeth his heart esteem it so: but he imagineth to destroy and to cut off not a few nations.
10.8: For he sayeth, Are not my princes altogether Kings?
10.9: Is not Calno as Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria as Damascus?
10.10: Like as mine hand hath found the kingdomes of the idoles, seeing their idoles were above Jerusalem, and above Samaria:
10.11: Shall not I, as I have done to Samaria, and to the idoles thereof, so doe to Jerusalem and to the idoles thereof?
10.12: But when the Lord hath accomplished all his work upon mount Zion and Jerusalem, I will visit the fruit of the proud heart of the King of Asshur, and his glorious and proud lookes,
10.13: Because he said, By ye power of mine own hand have I done it, and by my wisdom, because I am wise: therefore I have remooued the borders of the people, and have spoyled their treasures, and have pulled down the inhabitants like a valiant man.
10.14: And mine hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people, and as one gathereth egges that are left, so have I gathered all the earth: and there was none to mooue the wing or to open the mouth, or to whisper.
10.15: Shall the axe boast it self against him that heweth therewith? or shall the saw exalt it self against him that moveth it? as if the rod should lift up it self against him that taketh it up, or the staff should exalt it self, as it were no wood.
10.16: Therefore shall the Lord God of hostes send amog his fat men, leannes, and under his glorie he shall kindle a burning, like the burning of fire.
10.17: And the light of Israel shalbe as a fire, and the Holy one thereof as a flame, and it shall burn, and deuoure his thornes and his briers in one day:
10.18: And shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful fieldes both soul and flesh: and he shalbe as ye fainting of a standard bearer.
10.19: And the rest of the trees of his forest shalbe few, that a child may tell them.
10.20: And at that day shall the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Iaakob, stay no more upon him that smote them, but shall stay upon ye Lord, ye Holy one of Israel in trueth.
10.21: The remnant shall return, even the remnant of Iaakob unto the mightie God.
10.22: For though thy people, O Israel, be as the sand of the sea, yet shall the remnant of them return. The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.
10.23: For the Lord God of hostes shall make the consumption, even determined, in the middes of all the land.
10.24: Therefore thus saith ye Lord God of hostes, O my people, that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of Asshur: he shall smite thee with a rod, and shall lift up his staff against thee after the maner of Egypt:
10.25: But yet a very litle time, and the wrath shall be consumed, and mine anger in their destruction.
10.26: And ye Lord of hostes shall raise up a scourge for him, according to the plague of Midian in the rock Oreb: and as his staff was upon the Sea, so he will lift it up after the maner of Egypt.
10.27: And at that day shall his burden be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck: and the yoke shalbe destroied because of the anoynting.
10.28: He is come to Aiath: he is passed into Migron: at Michmash shall he lay up his armour.
10.29: They have gone over the foorde: they lodged in the lodging at Geba: Ramah is afraid: Gibeah of Saul is fled away.
10.30: Lift up thy voyce, O daughter Gallim, cause Laish to hear, O poor Anathoth.
10.31: Madmenah is removed: the inhabitants of Gebim have gathered themselves together.
10.32: Yet there is a time that he will stay at Nob: he shall lift up his hand toward the mount of the daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
10.33: Behold, the Lord God of hostes shall cut off the bough with fear, and they of high stature shalbe cut off, and the hie shalbe humbled.
10.34: And he shall cut away the thick places of the forest with yron, and Lebanon shall have a mightie fall.

11.1: But there shall come a rod foorth of the stock of Ishai, and a grass shall grow out of his rootes.
11.2: And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the Spirit of wisedome and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge, and of the fear of the Lord,
11.3: And shall make him prudent in the fear of the Lord: for he shall not judge after the sight of his eies, neither reprove by ye hearing of his eares.
11.4: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and with equitie shall he reprooue for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lippes shall he slay the wicked.
11.5: And justice shall be ye girdle of his loynes, and faithfulness the girdle of his reines.
11.6: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie with the kid, and the calf, and the lyon, and the fat beast together, and a litle child shall lead them.
11.7: And the kow and the bear shall feed: their yong ones shall lie together: and the lyon shall eat straw like the bullock.
11.8: And the sucking child shall play upon the hole of the asp, and the wained child shall put his hand upon the cockatrice hole.
11.9: Then shall none hurt nor destroy in all the mountain of mine holines: for the earth shalbe full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters that cover the sea.
11.10: And in that day the root of Ishai, which shall stand up for a sign unto the people, the nations shall seek unto it, and his rest shall be glorious.
11.11: And in the same day shall the Lord stretch out his hand again the second time, to possess the remnant of his people, (which shalbe left) of Asshur, and of Egypt, and of Pathros, and of Ethiopia, and of Elam, and of Shinear, and of Hamath, and of the yles of the sea.
11.12: And he shall set up a sign to the nations, and assemble the dispersed of Israel, and gather the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the world.
11.13: The hatred also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shalbe cut off: Ephraim shall not enuie Judah, neither shall Judah vex Ephraim:
11.14: But they shall flee upon the shoulders of the Philistims toward the West: they shall spoyle them of the East together: Edom and Moab shall be the stretching out of their hands, and the children of Ammon in their obedience.
11.15: The Lord also shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptians sea, and with his mightie wind shall lift up his hand over the river, and shall smite him in his seven streames, and cause men to walk therein with shooes.
11.16: And there shalbe a path to the remnant of his people, which are left of Asshur, like as it was unto Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

12.1: And thou shalt say in that day, O Lord, I will prayse thee: though thou wast angrie with me, thy wrath is turned away, and thou comfortest me.
12.2: Behold, God is my salvation: I will trust, and will not fear: for ye Lord God is my strength and song: he also is become my salvation.
12.3: Therefore with joy shall ye draw waters out of the welles of salvation.
12.4: And ye shall say in that day, Prayse the Lord: call upon his Name: declare his workes among the people: make mention of them, for his Name is exalted.
12.5: Sing unto the Lord, for he hath done excellent things: this is knowen in all the world.
12.6: Cry out, and shout, O inhabitant of Zion: for great is ye holy one of Israel in the middes of thee.

13.1: The burden of Babel, which Isaiah the sonne of Amoz did see.
13.2: Lift up a standard upon the hie mountain: lift up the voyce unto them: wagge the hand, that they may goe into the gates of the nobles.
13.3: I have commanded them, that I have sanctified: and I have called ye mightie to my wrath, and them that reioyce in my glorie.
13.4: The noyse of a multitude is in the mountaines, like a great people: a tumultuous voyce of the kingdomes of the nations gathered together: the Lord of hostes nombreth the host of the battell.
13.5: They come from a far countrey, from the end of the heaven: even the Lord with the weapons of his wrath to destroy the whole land.
13.6: Howl you, for the day of the Lord is at hand: it shall come as a destroier from the Almightie.
13.7: Therefore shall all hands be weakened, and all mens hearts shall melt,
13.8: And they shalbe afraid: anguish and sorowe shall take them, and they shall have pain, as a woman that travaileth: every one shall be amased at his neighbour, and their faces shalbe like flames of fire.
13.9: Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger to lay the land wast: and he shall destroy the sinners out of it.
13.10: For the starres of heaven and the planets thereof shall not give their light: the sunne shalbe darkened in his going foorth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.
13.11: And I will visit the wickednes upon the world, and their iniquitie upon the wicked, and I wil cause the arrogancie of the proud to cease, and will cast down the pride of tyrants.
13.12: I will make a man more precious then fine gold, even a man above the wedge of gold of Ophir.
13.13: Therefore I will shake the heaven, and the earth shall remooue out of her place in the wrath of the Lord of hostes, and in the day of his fierce anger.
13.14: And it shall be as a chased doe, and as a sheep that no man taketh up. every man shall turn to his own people, and flee eche one to his own land.
13.15: Every one that is found, shall be striken through: and whosoever ioyneth himself, shall fal by the sword.
13.16: Their children also shall be broken in pieces before their eyes: their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished.
13.17: Behold, I will stirre up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver, nor be desirous of gold.
13.18: With bowes also shall they destroy ye children, and shall have no compassion upon the fruit of the womb, and their eies shall not spare the children.
13.19: And Babel the glorie of kingdomes, the beautie and pride of the Chaldeans, shall be as the destruction of God in Sodom and Gomorah.
13.20: It shall not bee inhabited for ever, neither shall it be dwelled in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch his tents there, neither shall the shepheardes make their foldes there.
13.21: But Ziim shall lodge there, and their houses shall be ful of Ohim: Ostriches shall dwel there, and the Satyrs shall dance there.
13.22: And Iim shall crie in their palaces, and dragons in their pleasant palaces: and the time thereof is readie to come, and the daies thereof shall not be prolonged.

14.1: For the Lord wil have compassion of Iaakob, and wil yet chuse Israel, and cause them to rest in their own land: and the stranger shall ioyne him self unto them, and they shall cleave to the house of Iaakob.
14.2: And the people shall receive them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord, for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them prisoners, whose captives they were, and have rule over their oppressours.
14.3: And in that day when the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the sore bodage, wherein thou didest serve,
14.4: Then shalt thou take up this proverb against the King of Babel, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased? and the gold thirsty Babel rested?
14.5: The Lord hath broken the rod of the wicked, and the scepter of the rulers:
14.6: Which smote the people in anger with a continual plague, and ruled the nations in wrath: if any were persecuted, he did not let.
14.7: The whole world is at rest and is quiet: they sing for ioye.
14.8: Also the fire trees reioyced of thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no hewer came up against us.
14.9: Hel beneath is mooued for thee to meet thee at thy coming, raising up the dead for thee, even all the princes of the earth, and hath raised from their thrones all the Kinges of the nations.
14.10: All they shall crie, and saie unto thee, Art thou become weak also as we? art thou become like unto us?
14.11: Thy pomp is brought down to ye grave, and the sound of thy violes: the worm is spred under thee, and the wormes cover thee.
14.12: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, sonne of the morning? and cutte down to the ground, which didest cast lottes upon the nations?
14.13: Yet thou saidest in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, and exalt my throne above beside the starres of God: I will sitte also upon the mount of the Congregation in the sides of the North.
14.14: I wil ascend above ye height of the cloudes, and I will be like the most high.
14.15: But thou shalt bee brought down to the grave, to the sides of the pit.
14.16: They that see thee, shall look upon thee and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, and that did shake the kingdomes?
14.17: He made the world as a wilderness, and destroied the cities thereof, and opened not the house of his prisoners.
14.18: All the Kings of the nations, even they all sleep in glorie, every one in his own house.
14.19: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch: like the raiment of those that are slain, and thrust thorowe with a sword, which goe down to the stones of the pit, as a carkeise troden under feet.
14.20: Thou shalt not be ioyned with them in the grave, because thou hast destroied thine own land, and slain thy people: the seed of the wicked shall not be renoumed for ever.
14.21: Prepare a slaughter for his children, for the iniquitie of their fathers: let them not rise up nor possess the land, nor fil the face of the world with enemies.
14.22: For I wil rise up against them (sayth the Lord of hostes) and will cut off from Babel the name and the remnant and the sonne, and the nephew, sayth the Lord:
14.23: And I wil make it a possession to ye hedgehogge, and pooles of water, and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
14.24: The Lord of hostes hath sworn, saying, Surely like as I have purposed, so shall it come to pass, and as I have consulted, it shall stand:
14.25: That I will break to pieces Asshur in my land, and upon my mountaines will I tread him under foot: so that his yoke shall depart from them, and his burden shall be taken from off their shoulder.
14.26: This is the counsel that is consulted upon the whole world, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations,
14.27: Because the Lord of hostes hath determined it, and who shall disanull it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it away?
14.28: In the yeere that King Ahaz died, was this burden.
14.29: Reioyce not, (thou whole Palestina) because the rod of him that did beat thee, is broken for out of the serpents root shall come forth a cockatrise, and the fruit therof shalbe a firy flying serpent.
14.30: For the first borne of the poor shall be fed, and the needie shall lie down in safetie: and I will kill thy root with famine, and it shall slay thy remnant.
14.31: Howl, O gate, crie, O citie: thou whole land of Palestina art dissolved, for there shall come from the North a smoke, and none shalbe alone, at his time appointed.
14.32: What shall then one answer the messengers of the Gentiles? That the Lord hath stablished Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.

15.1: The burden of Moab. Surely Ar of Moab was destroied, and brought to silece in a night: surely Kir of Moab was destroied, and brought to silence in a night.
15.2: He shall goe up to the temple, and to Dibon to the hie places to weep: for Nebo and for Medeba shall Moab howl: upon all their heades shalbe baldness, and every beard shaven.
15.3: In their streetes shall they bee gilded with sackecloth: on the toppes of their houses, and in their streetes every one shall howl, and come down with weeping.
15.4: And Heshbon shall crie, and Elealeh: their voyce shall bee heard unto Jahaz: therefore the warriers of Moab shall showt: the soul of every one shall lament in him self.
15.5: Mine heart shall crie for Moab: his fugitiues shall flee unto Zoar, an heifer of three yere old: for they shall goe up with weeping by the mounting up of Luhith: and by the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a crie of destruction.
15.6: For the waters of Nimrim shall be dried up: therefore the grass is withered, the herbes consumed, and there was no green herb.
15.7: Therefore what every man hath left, and their substance shall they bear to the brook of the willowes.
15.8: For the crie went round about the borders of Moab: and the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the skriking thereof unto Beer Elim,
15.9: Because the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring more upon Dimon, even lyons upon him that escapeth of Moab, and to the remnant of the land.

16.1: Send yee a lamb to the ruler of the world from the rock of the wilderness, unto the mountain of the daughter Zion.
16.2: For it shall be as a bird that flieth, and a nest forsaken: the daughters of Moab shall be at the foordes of Arnon.
16.3: Gather a cousel, execute iudgement: make thy shadow as the night in the midday: hide them that are chased out: bewray not him that is fled.
16.4: Let my banished dwell with thee: Moab be thou their covert from the face of the destroyer: for the extortioner shall end: the destroyer shalbe consumed, and the oppressour shall cease out of the land.
16.5: And in mercy shall the throne be prepared, and hee shall sit upon it in stedfastness, in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking iudgement, and hasting justice.
16.6: We have heard of the pride of Moab, (he is very proud) even his pride, and his arrogancie, and his indignation, but his lies shall not be so.
16.7: Therefore shall Moab howl unto Moab: every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kirhareseth shall ye mourn, yet they shalbe striken.
16.8: For ye vineyards of Heshbon are cut down, and the vine of Sibmah: the lordes of the heathen have broken the principal vines thereof: they are come unto Jaazer: they wandred in the wilderness: her goodly branches stretched out them selves, and went over the sea.
16.9: Therefore will I weep with the weeping of Jaazer, and of the vine of Sibmah, O Heshbon: and Elealeh, I will make thee drunk with my teares, because upon thy sommer fruits, and upon thy harvest a showting is fallen.
16.10: And gladnes is taken away, and joy out of the plentiful field: and in the vineyardes shall be no singing nor shouting for joy: the treader shall not tread wine in the wine presses: I have caused the reioycing to cease.
16.11: Wherefore, my bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab, and mine inward partes for Ker-haresh.
16.12: And when it shall appear that Moab shall be wearie of his hie places, then shall hee come to his temple to praie, but he shall not prevail.
16.13: This is the word that the Lord hath spoken against Moab since that time.
16.14: And now the Lord hath spoken, saying, In three yeres, as the yeeres of a hireling, and the glorie of Moab shall be contemned in all the great multitude, and the remnant shalbe very small and feeble.

17.1: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a citie, for it shall be a ruinous heap.
17.2: The cities of Aroer shall be forsaken: they shall be for the flockes: for they shall lye there, and none shall make them afraid.
17.3: The munition also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Aram shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, sayeth the Lord of hostes.
17.4: And in that day the glorie of Iaakob shall be impoverished, and the fatnes of his flesh shalbe made lean.
17.5: And it shalbe as when the harvest man gathereth the corn, and reapeth the eares with his arm, and he shall be as he that gathereth the eares in the valley of Rephaim.
17.6: Yet a gathering of grapes shall be left in it, as the shaking of an olive tree, two or three beries are in the top of the vpmost boughes, and four or five in the hie branches of the fruit thereof, sayeth the Lord God of Israel.
17.7: At that day shall a man look to his maker, and his eyes shall look to the holy one of Israel.
17.8: And hee shall not look to the altars, the workes of his own hands, neither shall he look to those thinges, which his own fingers have made, as groves and images.
17.9: In that day shall the cities of their strength be as the forsaking of boughes and branches, which they did forsake, because of the children of Israel, and there shall be desolation.
17.10: Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not remembred the God of thy strength, therefore shalt thou set pleasant plantes, and shalt graff strange vine branches:
17.11: In the day shalt thou make thy plant to grow, and in the morning shalt thou make thy seed to florish: but the harvest shall be gone in the day of possession, and there shalbe desperate sorrow.
17.12: Ah, the multitude of many people, they shall make a sound like the noyse of the sea: for the noyse of the people shall make a sound like the noyse of mightie waters.
17.13: The people shall make a sound like the noise of many waters: but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shalbe chased as the chaff of the mountaines before the wind, and as a rolling thing before the whirlewinde.
17.14: And loe, in the evening there is trouble: but afore the morning it is gone. This is the portion of them that spoyle us, and the lot of them that rob us.

18.1: Oh, the land shadowing with winges, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
18.2: Sending ambassadours by the Sea, even in vessels of reedes upon the waters, saying, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation that is scattered abroad, and spoyled, unto a terrible people from their beginning even hitherto: a nation by litle and litle, even troden under foot, whose land the floods have spoyled.
18.3: Al ye the inhabitants of ye world and dwellers in the earth, shall see when he setteth up a sign in the mountaines, and when he bloweth the trumpet, ye shall hear.
18.4: For so the Lord said unto me, I will rest and behold in my tabernacle, as the heat drying up the rayne, and as a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
18.5: For afore the harvest when the flour is finished, and the fruit is riping in the flour, then he shall cut down the branches with hookes, and shall take away, and cut off the boughes:
18.6: They shall be left together unto the foules of the mountaines, and to the beastes of the earth: for the fowl shall sommer upon it, and every beast of the earth shall winter upon it.
18.7: At that time shall a present be brought unto the Lord of hostes, (a people that is scattered abroad, and spoyled, and of a terrible people from their beginning hitherto, a nation, by litle and litle even troden under foot, whose land the rivers have spoyled) to the place of the Name of the Lord of hostes, even the mount Zion.

19.1: The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt, and the idoles of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the middes of her.
19.2: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: so every one shall fight against his brother, and every one against his neighbour, citie against citie, and kingdom against kingdom.
19.3: And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the middes of her, and I will destroy their counsel, and they shall seek at the idoles, and at the sorcerers, and at them that have spirits of divination, and at the southsayers.
19.4: And I will deliver the Egyptians into the hand of the cruel Lordes, and a mightie King shall rule over them, sayth the Lord God of hostes.
19.5: Then the waters of the sea shall fail, and the rivers shall be dryed up, and wasted.
19.6: And the rivers shall goe far away: the rivers of defence shalbe emptied and dryed up: the reedes and flagges shall be cut down.
19.7: The grass in the river, and at the head of the rivers, and all that groweth by the river, shall wither, and be driven away, and be no more.
19.8: The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the river, shall lament, and they that spread their nette upon the waters, shall be weakened.
19.9: Moreover, they that work in flax of divers sortes, shall be confounded, and they that weave nettes.
19.10: For their nettes shalbe broken, and all they, that make pondes, shalbe heauie in heart.
19.11: Surely the princes of Zoan are fooles: the counsel of the wise counselers of Pharaoh is become foolish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the sonne of the wise? I am the sonne of the ancient Kings?
19.12: Where are now thy wise men, that they may tell thee, or may know what the Lord of hostes hath determined against Egypt?
19.13: The princes of Zoan are become fooles: the princes of Noph are deceived, they have deceived Egypt, even the corners of the tribes thereof.
19.14: The Lord hath mingled among them the spirit of errours: and they have caused Egypt to ere in every work thereof, as a drunken man erreth in his vomit.
19.15: Neither shall there be any work in Egypt, which the head may doe, nor the tayle, ye branch nor the rush.
19.16: In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: for it shall be afraid and fear because of the moouing of the hand of the Lord of hostes, which he shaketh over it.
19.17: And the land of Judah shall be a fear unto Egypt: every one that maketh mention of it, shalbe afraid thereat, because of ye counsel of the Lord of hostes, which he hath determined upon it.
19.18: In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and shall swear by the Lord of hostes. one shall be called the citie of destruction.
19.19: In that day shall the altar of the Lord be in the middes of the land of Egypt, and a pillar by the border thereof unto the Lord.
19.20: And it shall be for a sign and for a witnes unto the Lord of hostes in the land of Egypt: for they shall crie unto the Lord, because of the oppressers, and he shall send them a Sauiour and a great man, and shall deliver them.
19.21: And the Lord shall be knowen of the Egyptians, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day, and doe sacrifice and oblation, and shall vow vowes unto the Lord, and perform them.
19.22: So ye Lord shall smite Egypt, he shall smite and heal it: for he shall return unto ye Lord, and he shall be intreated of them and shall heal them.
19.23: In that day shall there be a path from Egypt to Asshur, and Asshur shall come into Egypt, and Egypt into Asshur: so the Egyptians shall worship with Asshur.
19.24: In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and Asshur, even a blessing in the middes of the land.
19.25: For the Lord of hostes shall bless it, saying, Blessed be my people Egypt and Asshur, the work of mine hands, and Israel mine inheritance.

20.1: In the yeere that Tartan came to Ashdod, (when Sargon King of Asshur sent him) and had fought against Ashdod, and taken it,
20.2: At the same time spake the Lord by ye hand of Isaiah the sonne of Amoz, saying, Goe, and loose the sackecloth from thy loynes, and put off thy shooe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.
20.3: And the Lord said, Like as my servant Isaiah hath walked naked, and barefoot three yeeres, as a sign and wonder upon Egypt, and Ethiopia,
20.4: So shall the King of Asshur take away the captiuitie of Egypt, and the captiuitie of Ethiopia, both yong men and old men, naked and barefoot, with their buttockes vncouered, to the shame of Egypt.
20.5: And they shall fear, and be ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.
20.6: Then shall the inhabitant of this yle say in that day, Behold, such is our expectation, whither we fledde for help to be delivered from the King of Asshur, and how shall we be delivered?

21.1: The burden of the desert Sea. As the whirlewindes in the South use to pass from the wilderness, so shall it come from the horrible land.
21.2: A grieuous vision was shewed unto me, The transgressour against a transgressour, and the destroyer against a destroyer. Goe up Elam, besiege Media: I have caused all the mourning thereof to cease.
21.3: Therefore are my loynes filled with sorow: sorowes have taken me as the sorowes of a woman that trauayleth: I was bowed down when I heard it, and I was amased when I saw it.
21.4: Mine heart failed: fearefulnesse troubled me: the night of my pleasures hath he turned into fear unto me.
21.5: Prepare thou the table: watch in the watch towre: eat, drink: arise, ye princes, anoynt the shield.
21.6: For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Go, set a watchman, to tell what he seeth.
21.7: And he saw a charet with two horsemen: a charet of an ass, and a charet of a camel: and he hearkened and took diligent heed.
21.8: And he cryed, A lyon: my lord, I stand continually upon ye watch towre in the day time, and I am set in my watch every night:
21.9: And behold, this mans charet cometh with two horsemen. And he answered and said, Babel is fallen: it is fallen, and all the images of her gods hath he broken unto the ground.
21.10: O my threshing, and the corn of my floor. That which I have heard of the Lord of hostes, the God of Israel, have I shewed unto you.
21.11: The burden of Dumah. He calleth unto me out of Seir, Watchman, what was in ye night? Watchman, what was in the night?
21.12: The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night. If yee will ask, enquire: return and come.
21.13: The burden against Arabia. In the forest of Arabia shall yee tarie all night, even in the waies of Dedanim.
21.14: O inhabitants of the land of Tema, bring foorth water to meet the thirstie, and prevent him that fleeth with his bread.
21.15: For they flee from the drawen swords, even from the drawen sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grieuousnesse of war.
21.16: For thus hath the Lord sayd unto me, Yet a yeere according to the yeeres of an hireling, and all the glorie of Kedar shall fail.
21.17: And the residue of the nomber of ye strong archers of the sonnes of Kedar shall be few: for the Lord God of Israel hath spoken it.

22.1: The burden of the valley of vision. What aileth thee now that thou art wholy gone up unto the house toppes?
22.2: Thou that art full of noise, a citie full of brute, a joyous citie: thy slain men shall not bee slain with sword, nor die in battell.
22.3: All thy princes shall flee together from the bow: they shalbe bound: all that shall be found in thee, shall be bound together, which have fled from far.
22.4: Therefore said I, Turn away from me: I wil weep bitterly: labour not to comfort mee for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
22.5: For it is a day of trouble, and of ruin, and of perplexitie by the Lord God of hostes in the valley of vision, breaking down the citie: and a crying unto the mountaines.
22.6: And Elam bare the quiuer in a mans charet with horsemen, and Kir vncouered the shield.
22.7: And thy chief valleis were full of charets, and the horsemen set themselves in aray against the gate.
22.8: And hee discovered the covering of Judah: and thou didest look in that day to the armour of the house of the forest.
22.9: And ye have seen the breaches of the citie of David: for they were many, and ye gathered the waters of the lower pool.
22.10: And yee nombred the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses have yee broken down to fortifie the wall,
22.11: And have also made a ditch between the two walles, for the waters of the old pool, and have not looked unto the maker thereof, neither had respect unto him that formed it of old.
22.12: And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call unto weeping and mourning, and to baldnes and girding with sackecloth.
22.13: And behold, joy and gladnes, slaying oxen and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine, eating and drinking: for to morowe we shall die.
22.14: And it was declared in ye eares of the Lord of hostes. Surely this iniquitie shall not be purged from you, til ye die, saith the Lord God of hostes.
22.15: Thus sayeth the Lord God of hostes, Goe, get thee to that treasurer, to Shebna, the steward of the house, and say,
22.16: What haste thou to doe here? and whom hast thou here? that thou shouldest here hew thee out a sepulchre, as he that heweth out his sepulchre in an hie place, or that graveth an habitation for him self in a rock?
22.17: Behold, the Lord wil carie thee away with a great captiuitie, and will surely cover thee.
22.18: He wil surely roll and turn thee like a bal in a large countrey: there shalt thou die, and there the charets of thy glory shalbe the shame of thy lordes house.
22.19: And I wil drive thee from thy station, and out of thy dwelling will he destroy thee.
22.20: And in that day will I call my servant Eliakim the sonne of Hilkiah,
22.21: And with thy garments will I clothe him, and with thy girdle will I strengthen him: thy power also will I commit into his hand, and hee shalbe a father of the inhabitats of Jerusalem, and of the house of Judah.
22.22: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder: so hee shall open, and no man shall shut: and he shall shut, and no man shall open.
22.23: And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place, and hee shall be for the throne of glorie to his fathers house.
22.24: And they shall hang upon him all the glorie of his fathers house, even of the nephewes and posteritie all small vessels, from the vessels of the cuppes, even to all the instruments of musike.
22.25: In that day, sayeth the Lord of hostes, shall the nail, that is fastned in the sure place, depart and shall be broken, and fall: and the burden, that was upon it, shall bee cut off: for the Lord hath spoken it.

23.1: The burden of Tyrus. Howl, yee shippes of Tarshish: for it is destroied, so that there is none house: none shall come from the land of Chittim: it is reueiled unto them.
23.2: Be still, yee that dwell in the yles: the marchantes of Zidon, and such as pass over the sea, have replenished thee.
23.3: The seed of Nilus growing by the abundance of waters, and the harvest of the river was her reuenues, and she was a mart of the nations.
23.4: Be ashamed, thou Zidon: for the sea hath spoken, even the strength of the sea, saying, I have not travailed, nor brought forth children, neither nourished yong men, nor brought up virgins.
23.5: When the fame cometh to the Egyptians, they shall be sorie, concerning the rumour of Tyrus.
23.6: Goe you over to Tarshish: howl, yee that dwell in the yles.
23.7: Is not this that your glorious citie? her antiquitie is of ancient daies: her own feet shall lead her afarre off to be a soiourner.
23.8: Who hath decreed this against Tyrus (that crowneth men) whose marchantes are princes? whose chapmen are the nobles of the world?
23.9: The Lord of hostes hath decreed this, to stain the pride of all glorie, and to bring to contempt all them that be glorious in the earth.
23.10: Pass through thy land like a flood to the daughter of Tarshish: there is no more strength.
23.11: He stretched out his hand upon the sea: he shook the kingdomes: the Lord hath given a commandement concerning the place of marchandise, to destroy the power thereof.
23.12: And he said, Thou shalt no more reioyce when thou art oppressed: O virgin daughter of Zidon: rise up, goe over unto Chittim: yet there thou shalt have no rest.
23.13: Behold the land of the Caldeans: this was no people: Asshur founded it by the inhabitantes of the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof: they raised the palaces thereof and hee brought it to ruin.
23.14: Howl yee shippes of Tarshish, for your strength is destroyed.
23.15: And in that day shall Tyrus bee forgotten seuentie yeeres, (according to the yeeres of one King) at the end of seuentie yeeres shall Tyrus sing as an harlot.
23.16: Take an harp and go about the citie: (thou harlot thou hast been forgotten) make sweet melodie, sing moe songes that thou maiest be remembred.
23.17: And at the end of seuentie yeres shall the Lord visit Tyrus, and she shall return to her wages, and shall commit fornication with all the kingdomes of the earth, that are in the world.
23.18: Yet her occupying and her wages shall bee holy unto the Lord: it shall not be laied up nor kept in store, but her marchandise shalbe for them that dwell before the Lord, to eat sufficiently, and to have durable clothing.

24.1: Behold, the Lord maketh the earth emptie, and hee maketh it waste: hee turneth it upside down, and scattereth abrode the inhabitants thereof.
24.2: And there shalbe like people, like Priest, and like seruaunt, like master, like maid, like mistress, like bier, like seller, like lender, like borower, like giver, like taker to vsurie.
24.3: The earth shalbe clean emptied, and utterly spoiled: for the Lord hath spoken this word.
24.4: The earth lamenteth and fadeth away: the world is feeble and decaied: the proud people of the earth are weakened.
24.5: The earth also deceiveth, because of the inhabitantes thereof: for they transgressed the lawes: they changed the ordinances, and brake the everlasting covenant.
24.6: Therefore hath the curse deuoured the earth, and the inhabitantes thereof are desolate. Wherefore the inhabitants of the land are burned up, and few men are left.
24.7: The wine faileth, the vine hath no might: all that were of merie heart, doe mourn.
24.8: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth: the noyse of them that reioyce, endeth: the ioye of the harp ceaseth.
24.9: They shall not drink wine with mirth: strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.
24.10: The citie of vanitie is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in.
24.11: There is a crying for wine in the streetes: al joy is darkened: the mirth of the world is gone away.
24.12: In the citie is left desolation, and the gate is smitten with destruction.
24.13: Surely thus shall it bee in the middes of the earth, among the people, as the shaking of an olive tree, and as the grapes when the vintage is ended.
24.14: They shall lift up their voyce: they shall shout for the magnificence of the Lord: they shall reioyce from the sea.
24.15: Wherefore praise yee the Lord in the valleis, even the Name of the Lord God of Israel, in the yles of the sea.
24.16: From the uttermost part of the earth wee have heard praises, even glory to the just, and I sayd, My leanesse, my leanesse, woe is mee: the transgressours have offended: yea, the transgressours have grieuously offended.
24.17: Fear, and the pitte, and the snare are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth.
24.18: And hee that fleeth from the noyse of the fear, shall fall into the pit: and he that cometh up out of the pit, shall be taken in the snare: for the windowes from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth doe shake.
24.19: The earth is utterly broken down: the earth is clean dissolved: the earth is mooued exceedingly.
24.20: The earth shall reel to and from like a drunken man, and shall be remooued like a tent, and the iniquitie thereof shall be heauie upon it: so that it shall fall, and rise no more.
24.21: And in that day shall the Lord visit the host above that is on hie, even the Kinges of the world that are upon the earth.
24.22: And they shall be gathered together, as the prisoners in the pit: and they shall be shut up in the prison, and after many daies shall they be visited.
24.23: Then the moon shall be abashed, and the sunne ashamed, when the Lord of hostes shall reign in mount Zion and in Jerusalem: and glory shalbe before his ancient men.

25.1: O Lord, thou art my God: I will exalt thee, I will prayse thy Name: for thou hast done wonderful things, according to the counsels of old, with a stable trueth.
25.2: For thou hast made of a citie an heap, of a strong citie, a ruin: even the palace of strangers of a citie, it shall never be built.
25.3: Therefore shall the mightie people give glory unto thee: the citie of the strong nations shall fear thee.
25.4: For thou hast been a strength unto the poor, even a strength to the needie in his trouble, a refuge against the tempest, a shadow against the heat: for the blast of the mightie is like a storm against the wall.
25.5: Thou shalt bring down the noyse of the strangers, as the heat in a drie place: he wil bring down the song of the mightie, as the heat in the shadow of a cloud.
25.6: And in this mountain shall the Lord of hostes make unto all people a feast of fat thinges, even a feast of fined wines, and of fat thinges full of marow, of wines fined and purified.
25.7: And he will destroy in this mountain the covering that covereth all people, and the vail that is spread upon all nations.
25.8: He wil destroy death for ever: and the Lord God wil wipe away the teares from all faces, and the rebuke of his people will he take away out of all the earth: for the Lord hath spoken it.
25.9: And in that day shall men say, Loe, this is our God: we have waited for him, and he wil save us. This is the Lord, we have waited for him: we will reioyce and be ioyfull in his salvation.
25.10: For in this mountain shall the hand of the Lord rest, and Moab shalbe threshed under him, even as straw is threshed in Madmenah.
25.11: And he shall stretch out his hand in the middes of them (as he that swimmeth, stretcheth them out to swimme) and with the strength of his handes shall he bring down their pride.
25.12: The defence also of the height of thy walles shall he bring down and lay low, and cast them to the ground, even unto the dust.

26.1: In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah, We have a strong citie: salvation shall God set for walles and bulwarkes.
26.2: Open ye the gates that the righteous nation, which keepeth the trueth, may enter in.
26.3: By an assured purpose wilt thou preserve perfite peace, because they trusted in thee.
26.4: Trust in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord God is strength for evermore.
26.5: For hee will bring down them that dwell on hie: the hie citie he will abase: even unto the ground wil he cast it down, and bring it unto dust.
26.6: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steppes of the needie.
26.7: The way of the just is righteousness: thou wilt make equal the righteous path of the just.
26.8: Also we, O Lord, have waited for thee in the way of thy iudgemets: the desire of our soul is to thy Name, and to the remembrance of thee.
26.9: With my soul have I desired thee in the night, and with my spirit within mee will I seek thee in the morning: for seeing thy iudgements are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn righteousness.
26.10: Let mercie bee shewed to the wicked, yet hee will not learn righteousness: in the land of vprightnesse will he do wickedly, and will not behold the maiestie of the Lord.
26.11: O Lord, they will not behold thine hie hand: but they shall see it, and bee confounded with the zeal of the people, and the fire of thine enemies shall deuoure them.
26.12: Lord, unto us thou wilt ordeine peace: for thou also hast wrought all our workes for us.
26.13: O Lord our God, other lords beside thee, have ruled us, but we will remember thee onely, and thy Name.
26.14: The dead shall not live, neither shall the dead arise, because thou hast visited and scattered them, and destroyed all their memorie.
26.15: Thou hast increased the nation, O Lord: thou hast increased the nation: thou art made glorious: thou hast enlarged all the coastes of the earth.
26.16: Lord, in trouble have they visited thee: they powred out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.
26.17: Like as a woman with child, that draweth neere to the travail, is in sorow, and cryeth in her paines, so have we been in thy sight, O Lord.
26.18: We have coceiued, we have borne in pain, as though we should have brought forth wind: there was no help in the earth, neither did the inhabitants of the world fall.
26.19: Thy dead men shall live: even with my body shall they rise. Awake, and sing, ye that dwel in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbes, and the earth shall cast out the dead.
26.20: Come, my people: enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doores after thee: hide thy self for a very litle while, until the indignation pass over.
26.21: For lo, the Lord cometh out of his place, to visit the iniquitie of the inhabitants of the earth upon them: and the earth shall disclose her blood, and shall no more hide her slain.

27.1: In that day the Lord with his sore and great and mightie sword shall visit Liuiathan, that pearcing serpent, even Liuiathan, that crooked serpent, and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.
27.2: In that day sing of the vineyard of redde wine.
27.3: I the Lord doe keep it: I will water it every moment: least any assaile it, I will keep it night and day.
27.4: Anger is not in mee: who would set the briers and the thornes against me in battel? I would go through them, I would burn them together.
27.5: Or will he feel my strength, that he may make peace with me, and be at one with me?
27.6: Hereafter, Iaakob shall take root: Israel shall florish and grow, and the world shall be filled with fruit.
27.7: Hath hee smitten him as hee smote those that smote him? or is hee slain according to the slaughter of them that were slain by him?
27.8: In measure in the branches thereof wilt thou contend with it, when he bloweth with his rough wind in the day of the East wind.
27.9: By this therefore shall the iniquitie of Iaakob be purged, and this is all the fruit, the taking away of his sinne: whe he shall make all the stones of the altars, as chalke stones broken in pieces, that the groves and images may not stand up.
27.10: Yet the defenced citie shalbe desolate, and the habitation shalbe forsaken, and left like a wildernes. There shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie, and consume the branches thereof.
27.11: When the boughes of it are drie, they shalbe broken: the women come, and set them on fire: for it is a people of none vnderstading: therefore hee that made them, shall not have compassion of them, and he that formed them, shall have no mercie on them.
27.12: And in that day shall the Lord thresh from the chanell of the River unto the river of Egypt, and ye shalbe gathered, one by one, O children of Israel.
27.13: In that day also shall the great trumpet be blowen, and they shall come, which perished in the land of Asshur: and they that were chased into the land of Egypt, and they shall worship the Lord in the holy Mount at Jerusalem.

28.1: Woe to the crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim: for his glorious beautie shall be a fading flowre, which is upon the head of the valley of them that be fat, and are overcome with wine.
28.2: Behold, the Lord hath a mightie and strong host, like a tempest of hail, and a whirlewinde that overthroweth, like a tempest of mightie waters that overflow, which throw to the ground mightily.
28.3: They shall be troden under foot, even the crown and the pride of the drunkards of Ephraim.
28.4: For his glorious beautie shall be a fading flour, which is upon the head of the valley of them that be fatte, and as the hastie fruit afore sommer, which when hee that looketh upon it, seeth it, while it is in his hand, he eateth it.
28.5: In that day shall the Lord of hostes be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beautie unto the residue of his people:
28.6: And for a spirit of iudgement to him that sitteth in iudgement, and for strength unto them that turn away the battell to the gate.
28.7: But they have erred because of wine, and are out of the way by strong drink: the priest and the prophet have erred by strong drink: they are swallowed up with wine: they have gone astray through strong drink: they fail in vision: they stumble in iudgement.
28.8: For all their tables are full of filthy vomiting: no place is clean.
28.9: Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the thinges that hee heareth? them that are weyned from the milk, and drawen from the breastes.
28.10: For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept, line unto line, line unto line, there a litle, and there a litle.
28.11: For with a stammering tongue and with a strange language shall he speak unto this people.
28.12: Unto whom hee said, This is the rest: give rest to him that is weary: and this is the refreshing, but they would not hear.
28.13: Therefore shall the word of the Lord be unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept, line unto line, line unto line, there a litle and there a litle, that they may goe, and fall backward, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.
28.14: Wherefore, hear the word of the Lord, ye scornefull men that rule this people, which is at Jerusalem.
28.15: Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement: though a scourge runne over, and pass through, it shall not come at us: for we have made falshood our refuge, and under vanitie are we hid,
28.16: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I will lay in Zion a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation. Hee that beleeueth, shall not make haste.
28.17: Iudgement also will I lay to the rule, and righteousness to the balance, and the hail shall sweep away the vain confidence, and the waters shall overflow the secret place.
28.18: And your covenant with death shalbe disanulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand: when a scourge shall runne over and pass through, then shall ye be trode down by it.
28.19: When it passeth over, it shall take you away: for it shall pass through every morning in the day, and in the night, and there shalbe onely fear to make you to understand the hearing.
28.20: For the bed is streight that it can not suffice, and the covering narowe that one can not wrappe himself.
28.21: For the Lord shall stand as in mount Perazim: hee shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strage work, and bring to pass his act, his strange act.
28.22: Now therefore be no mockers, least your bondes increase: for I have heard of the Lord of hostes a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth.
28.23: Hearken ye, and hear my voyce: hearken ye, and hear my speach.
28.24: Doeth the plow man plow all the day, to sow? doeth he open, and break the clots of his ground?
28.25: When he hath made it plain, wil he not then sow the fitches, and sow cummin, and cast in wheat by measure, and the appointed barly and rye in their place?
28.26: For his God doeth instruct him to have discretion, and doeth teach him.
28.27: For fitches shall not be threshed with a threshing instrument, neither shall a cart wheel be turned about upon the cummin: but ye fitches are beaten out with a staff, and cummin with a rod.
