28.28: Bread corn when it is threshed, hee doeth not alway thresh it, neither doeth the wheel of his cart still make a noyse, neither will he break it with the teeth thereof.
28.29: This also cometh from the Lord of hostes, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in workes.

29.1: Ah altar, altar of the citie that David dwelt in: add yere unto yere: let them kill lambs.
29.2: But I wil bring the altar into distress, and there shalbe heauines and sorowe, and it shall be unto me like an altar.
29.3: And I wil besiege thee as a circle, and fight against thee on a mount, and will cast up ramparts against thee.
29.4: So shalt thou be humbled, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speach shalbe as out of the dust: thy voyce also shall be out of the ground like him that hath a spirit of divination, and thy talking shall whisper out of the dust.
29.5: Moreover, the multitude of thy strangers shalbe like small dust, and the multitude of strong men shalbe as chaff that passeth away, and it shall be in a moment, even suddenly.
29.6: Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hostes with thunder, and shaking, and a great noyse, a whirlewinde, and a tempest, and a flame of a deuouring fire.
29.7: And the multitude of all the nations that fight against the altar, shalbe as a dream or vision by night: even all they that make the war against it, and strong holdes against it, and lay siege unto it.
29.8: And it shalbe like as an hungry man dreameth, and behold, he eateth: and when he awaketh, his soul is emptie: or like as a thirsty man dreameth, and loe, he is drinking, and when he awaketh, behold, he is faint, and his soul longeth: so shall the multitude of all nations be that fight against mount Zion.
29.9: Stay your selves, and wonder: they are blind, and make you blind: they are drunken but not with wine: they stagger, but not by strong drink.
29.10: For the Lord hath covered you with a spirit of slumber, and hath shut up your eyes: the Prophets, and your chief Seers hath he covered.
29.11: And the vision of them all is become unto you, as the wordes of a book that is sealed up, which they deliver to one that can read, saying, Read this, I pray thee. Then shall he say, I can not: for it is sealed.
29.12: And the book is given unto him that can not read, saying, Read this, I pray thee. And he shall say, I can not read.
29.13: Therefore the Lord sayd, Because this people come neere unto me with their mouth, and honour me with their lips, but have remooued their heart far from me, and their fear toward me was taught by the precept of men,
29.14: Therefore behold, I wil again doe a marueilous work in this people, even a marueilous work, and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shalbe hid.
29.15: Wo unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord: for their workes are in darkenes, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?
29.16: Your turning of deuises shall it not be esteemed as the potters clay? for shall the work say of him that made it, Hee made me not? or the thing formed, say of him that facioned it, He had none understanding?
29.17: Is it not yet but a litle while, and Lebanon shall be turned into Carmel? and Carmel shall be counted as a forest?
29.18: And in that day shall the deaf hear the wordes of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscuritie, and out of darkenesse.
29.19: The meek in the Lord shall receive ioye again, and the poor men shall reioyce in the holy one of Israel.
29.20: For the cruel man shall cease, and the scornefull shalbe consumed: and all that hasted to iniquitie, shalbe cut off:
29.21: Which made a man to sinne in ye word, and took him in a snare: which reproved them in the gate, and made the just to fall without cause.
29.22: Therefore thus sayth the Lord unto the house of Iaakob, even hee that redeemed Abraham, Iaakob shall not now be confounded, neither now shall his face be pale.
29.23: But when he seeth his children, the work of mine hands, in the mids of him, they shall sanctifie my Name, and sanctifie the holy one of Iaakob, and shall fear the God of Israel.
29.24: Then they that erred in spirit, shall have understanding, and they that murmured, shall learn doctrine.

30.1: Wo to the rebellious children, sayth the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me, and cover with a covering, but not by my spirit, that they may lay sinne upon sinne:
30.2: Which walk forth to goe down into Egypt (and have not asked at my mouth) to strengthen them selves with the strength of Pharaoh, and trust in the shadow of Egypt.
30.3: But the strength of Pharaoh shalbe your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.
30.4: For his princes were at Zoan, and his Ambassadours came unto Hanes.
30.5: They shalbe all ashamed of the people that cannot profit them, nor help nor doe them good, but shalbe a shame and also a reproche.
30.6: The burden of the beasts of the South, in a land of trouble and anguish, from whence shall come the yong and old lyon, the viper and fierie flying serpent against them that shall bear their riches upon the shoulders of the coltes, and their treasures upon the bounches of the camels, to a people that cannot profit.
30.7: For the Egyptians are vanitie, and they shall help in vain. Therefore have I cried unto her, Their strength is to sit still.
30.8: Now go, and write it before them in a table, and note it in a book that it may be for the last day for ever and ever:
30.9: That it is a rebellious people, lying children, and children that would not hear the law of the Lord.
30.10: Which say unto the Seers, See not: and to the Prophets, Prophecie not unto us right things: but speak flattering things unto us: prophecie errours.
30.11: Depart out of the way: go aside out of the path: cause the holy one of Israel to cease from us.
30.12: Therefoe thus saith the holy one of Israel, Because you have cast off this word, and trust in violence, and wickednes, and stay thereupon,
30.13: Therefore this iniquitie shalbe unto you as a breach that falleth, or a swelling in an hie wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly in a moment.
30.14: And the breaking thereof is like the breaking of a potters pot, which is broken without pitie, and in the breaking thereof is not found a sheard to take fire out of the hearth, or to take water out of the pit.
30.15: For thus sayd the Lord God, the Holy one of Israel, In rest and quietnes shall ye be saved: in quietnes and in confidence shall be your strength, but ye would not.
30.16: For ye have sayd, No, but we wil flee away upon horses. Therefore shall ye flee. We will ride upon the swiftest. Therefore shall your persecuters be swifter.
30.17: A thousand as one shall flee at the rebuke of one: at the rebuke of five shall ye flee, till ye be left as a ship mast upon the top of a mountain, and as a beaken upon an hill.
30.18: Yet therefore will the Lord wait, that he may have mercy upon you, and therefore wil he be exalted, that hee may have compassion upon you: for the Lord is the God of iudgement. Blessed are all they that wait for him.
30.19: Surely a people shall dwell in Zion, and in Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he wil certainly have mercy upon thee at the voyce of thy cry: when he heareth thee, he wil answer thee.
30.20: And when the Lord hath given you the bread of aduersitie, and the water of affliction, thy rain shalbe no more kept back, but thine eyes shall see thy rain.
30.21: And thine eares shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when thou turnest to the right hand, and when thou turnest to the left.
30.22: And ye shall pollute the covering of the images of silver, and the rich ornament of thine images of gold, and cast them away as a menstruous cloth, and thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.
30.23: Then shall hee give rain unto thy seed, when thou shalt sow the ground, and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shalbe fat and as oyle: in that day shall thy cattell be fed in large pastures.
30.24: The oxen also and the yong asses, that till the ground, shall eat clean provender, which is winowed with the shoouel and with the fanne.
30.25: And upon every hie mountain, and upon every hie hill shall there be rivers and streames of waters, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers shall fall.
30.26: Moreover, the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sunne, and the light of the sunne shalbe seven fold, and like the light of seven dayes in the day that the Lord shall bind up the breach of his people, and heal the stroke of their wound.
30.27: Behold, the Name of the Lord cometh from far, his face is burning, and the burden thereof is heavy: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a deuouring fire.
30.28: And his spirit is as a river that overfloweth up to the neck: it deuideth asunder, to fanne the nations with the fanne of vanitie, and there shall be a bridle to cause them to ere in the chawes of the people.
30.29: But there shall be a song unto you as in the night, when solemn feast is kept: and gladnes of heart, as he that cometh with a pipe to goe unto the mount of the Lord, to the mightie one of Israel.
30.30: And the Lord shall cause his glorious voyce to be heard, and shall declare the lighting down of his arm with the anger of his countenance, and flame of a deuouring fire, with scattering and tempest, and hailestones.
30.31: For with the voyce of the Lord shall Asshur be destroyed, which smote with the rod.
30.32: And in every place that ye staff shall pass, it shall cleave fast, which the Lord shall lay upon him with tabrets and harpes: and with battels, and lifting up of hands shall he fight against it.
30.33: For Tophet is prepared of old: it is even prepared for the King: hee hath made it deep and large: the burning thereof is fire and much wood: the breath of the Lord, like a river of brimstone, doeth kindle it.

31.1: Woe unto them that goe down into Egypt for help, and stay upon horses, and trust in charets, because they are many, and in horsemen, because they be very strong: but they look not unto the holy one of Israel, nor seek unto the Lord.
31.2: But he yet is wisest: therefore he wil bring evil, and not turn back his word, but he will arise against the house of the wicked, and against the help of them that work vanitie.
31.3: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit: and when the Lord shall stretch out his hand, the helper shall fall, and hee that is holpen shall fall, and they shall altogether fail.
31.4: For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me, As the lyon or lyons whelp roareth upon his pray, against whom if a multitude of shepheards be called, hee will not be afraid at their voyce, neither will humble him self at their noise: so shall the Lord of hostes come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.
31.5: As birds that flie, so shall the Lord of hostes defend Jerusalem by defending and delivering, by passing through and preseruing it.
31.6: O ye children of Israel, turn again, in as much as ye are sunken deep in rebellion.
31.7: For in that day every man shall cast out his idoles of silver, and his idoles of gold, which your handes have made you, even a sinne.
31.8: Then shall Asshur fall by the sword, not of man, neither shall the sword of man deuoure him, and hee shall flee from the sword, and his yong men shall faint.
31.9: And he shall go for fear to his towre, and his princes shall be afraid of the standart, sayeth the Lord, whose fire is in Zion, and his fornace in Jerusalem.

32.1: Behold, a King shall reign in justice, and the princes shall rule in iudgement.
32.2: And that man shall bee as an hiding place from the wind, and as a refuge for the tempest: as rivers of water in a drie place, and as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
32.3: The eyes of the seeing shall not be shut, and the eares of them that hear, shall hearken.
32.4: And the heart of the foolish shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stutters shalbe ready to speak distinctly.
32.5: A nigard shall no more be called liberal, nor the churl rich.
32.6: But the nigarde will speak of nigardnesse, and his heart will work iniquitie, and do wickedly, and speak falsely against the Lord, to make emptie the hungrie soul, and to cause the drink of the thirstie to fail.
32.7: For the weapons of the churl are wicked: hee deviseth wicked counsels, to vndoe the poor with lying words: and to speak against the poor in iudgement.
32.8: But the liberal man will devise of liberal things, and he will continue his liberalitie.
32.9: Rise up, ye women that are at ease: hear my voyce, ye careless daughters: hearken to my wordes.
32.10: Yee women, that are careless, shall be in fear above a yeere in dayes: for the vintage shall fail, and the gatherings shall come no more.
32.11: Yee women, that are at ease, be astonied: fear, O yee careless women: put off the clothes: make bare, and gird sackcloth upon the loynes.
32.12: Men shall lament for the teates, even for the pleasant fieldes, and for the fruitefull vine.
32.13: Upon the land of my people shall grow thornes and briers: yea, upon all the houses of ioye in the citie of reioysing,
32.14: Because the palace shalbe forsaken, and the noise of the citie shalbe left: the towre and fortress shalbe dennes for ever, and the delite of wild asses, and a pasture for flockes,
32.15: Until the Spirit be powred upon us from above, and the wildernes become a fruitful field, and the plenteous field be counted as a forest.
32.16: And iudgement shall dwel in the desert, and justice shall remain in the fruitful field.
32.17: And the work of justice shall bee peace, even the work of justice and quietness, and assurance for ever.
32.18: And my people shall dwell in the tabernacle of peace, and in sure dwellings, and in safe resting places.
32.19: When it haileth, it shall fall on the forest, and the citie shall be set in the low place.
32.20: Blessed are ye that sow upon all waters, and drive thither the feet of the oxe and the ass.

33.1: Woe to thee that spoylest, and wast not spoyled: and doest wickedly, and they did not wickedly against thee: when thou shalt cease to spoyle, thou shalt be spoyled: when thou shalt make an end of doing wickedly, they shall doe wickedly against thee.
33.2: O Lord, have mercie upon us, wee have waited for thee: be thou, which waste their arm in the morning, our help also in time of trouble.
33.3: At the noise of the tumult, the people fled: at thine exalting the nations were scattered.
33.4: And your spoyle shall be gathered like the gathering of caterpillers: and he shall go against him like the leaping of grashoppers.
33.5: The Lord is exalted: for hee dwelleth on hie: he hath filled Zion with iudgement and justice.
33.6: And there shall be stabilitie of thy times, strength, salvation, wisdom and knowledge: for the fear of the Lord shalbe his treasure.
33.7: Behold, their messengers shall cry without, and ye ambassadours of peace shall weep bitterly.
33.8: The pathes are waste: the wayfaring man ceaseth: hee hath broken the covenant: hee hath contemned the cities: he regarded no man.
33.9: The earth mourneth and fainteth: Lebanon is ashamed, and hewen down: Sharon is like a wildernes, and Bashan is shaken and Carmel.
33.10: Now will I arise, saith the Lord: now will I be exalted, now will I lift up my self.
33.11: Ye shall conceive chaff, and bring forth stubble: the fire of your breath shall deuoure you.
33.12: And the people shall be as the burning of lime: and as the thornes cut up, shall they be burnt in the fire.
33.13: Hear, yee that are far off, what I have done, and ye that are neere, know my power.
33.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid: a fear is come upon the hypocrites: who among us shall dwel with the deuouring fire? who among us shall dwell with the everlasting burnings?
33.15: Hee that walketh in justice, and speaketh righteous things, refusing gain of oppression, shaking his handes from taking of gifts, stopping his eares from hearing of blood, and shutting his eyes from seeing evil.
33.16: He shall dwell on hie: his defence shall be the munitions of rockes: bread shalbe given him, and his waters shalbe sure.
33.17: Thine eyes shall see the King in his glory: they shall behold the land far off.
33.18: Thine heart shall meditate fear, Where is the scribe? where is the receiver? where is hee that counted the towres?
33.19: Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a dark speache, that thou canst not perceive, and of a stammering tongue that thou canst not vnderstande.
33.20: Look upon Zion the citie of our solemn feastes: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a Tabernacle that can not be remooued: and the stakes thereof can never be taken away, neither shall any of the cordes thereof be broken.
33.21: For surely there the mightie Lord will be unto us, as a place of floods and broad rivers, whereby shall pass no shippe with oares, neither shall great shippe pass thereby.
33.22: For the Lord is our Judge, the Lord is our law giver: the Lord is our King, he will save us.
33.23: Thy cordes are loosed: they could not well strengthen their mast, neither could they spread the sail: then shall the pray be deuided for a great spoil: yea, the lame shall take away the pray.
33.24: And none inhabitant shall say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein, shall have their iniquitie forgiven.

34.1: Come neere, ye nations and hear, and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear and all that is therein, the world and al that proceedeth thereof.
34.2: For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his wrath upon all their armies: hee hath destroyed them and delivered them to the slaughter.
34.3: And their slain shalbe cast out, and their stincke shall come up out of their bodies, and the mountaines shalbe melted with their blood.
34.4: And all the host of heaven shalbe dissolved, and the heavens shall be folden like a book: and all their hostes shall fall as the leaf falleth from the vine, and as it falleth from the figtree.
34.5: For my sword shalbe drunken in the heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Edom, even upon the people of my curse to iudgement.
34.6: The sword of the Lord is filled with blood: it is made fat with the fat and with the blood of the lambes and the goates, with the fat of the kidneis of the rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
34.7: And the vnicorne shall come down with them and the heiffers with the bulles, and their land shalbe drunken with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.
34.8: For it is the day of the Lordes vengeance, and the yeere of recompence for the iudgement of Zion.
34.9: And the rivers thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shalbe burning pitch.
34.10: It shall not be quenched night nor day: the smoke thereof shall goe up evermore: it shall be desolate from generation to generation: none shall pass through it for ever.
34.11: But the pelican and the hedgehog shall possess it, and the great owl, and the raven shall dwel in it, and he shall stretch out upon it the line of vanitie, and the stones of emptiness.
34.12: The nobles thereof shall call to the kingdom, and there shalbe none, and all the princes thereof shalbe as nothing.
34.13: And it shall bring foorth thornes in the palaces thereof, nettles and thistles in the strong holdes thereof, and it shall be an habitation for dragons, and a court for ostriches.
34.14: There shall meet also Ziim and Iim, and the Satyr shall cry to his fellow, and the shricheowle shall rest there, and shall find for her self a quiet dwelling.
34.15: There shall the owl make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather them under her shadow: there shall the vultures also bee gathered, every one with her make.
34.16: Seek in the book of the Lord, and read: none of these shall fayle, none shall want her make: for his mouth hath commanded, and his very Spirit hath gathered them.
34.17: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath deuided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever: from generation to generation shall they dwell in it.

35.1: The desert and the wildernes shall reioyce: and the waste ground shalbe glad and florish as the rose.
35.2: It shall florish abundantly and shall greatly reioyce also and ioye: the glory of Lebanon shalbe given unto it: the beautie of Carmel, and of Sharon, they shall see the glory of the Lord, and the excellencie of our God.
35.3: Strengthen the weak handes, and comfort the feeble knees.
35.4: Say unto them that are fearefull, Bee you strong, fear not: behold, your God cometh with vengeance: even God with a recompense, he will come and save you.
35.5: Then shall the eyes of the blind be lightened, and the eares of the deaf be opened.
35.6: Then shall ye lame man leap as an hart, and the dumme mans tongue shall sing: for in the wildernes shall waters break out, and rivers in ye desert.
35.7: And the dry ground shalbe as a pool, and the thirstie (as springs of water in the habitation of dragons: where they lay) shall be a place for reedes and rushes.
35.8: And there shalbe a path and a way, and the way shalbe called holy: the polluted shall not pass by it: for he shalbe with them, and walk in the way, and the fooles shall not ere.
35.9: There shall be no lyon, nor noysome beastes shall ascend by it, neither shall they be found there, that the redeemed may walk.
35.10: Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with prayse: and everlasting joy shall bee upon their heads: they shall obteine ioye and gladness, and sorow and mourning shall flee away.

36.1: Now in the fourteenth yeere of King Hezekiah, Saneherib King of Asshur came up against al the strong cities of Judah, and took them.
36.2: And the King of Asshur sent Rabshakeh from Lachish toward Jerusalem unto King Hezekiah, with a great host, and he stood by ye conduit of the upper pool in the path of the fullers field.
36.3: Then came foorth unto him Eliakim the sonne of Hilkiah the steward of the house, and Shebna the chanceler, and Joah the sonne of Asaph the recorder.
36.4: And Rabshakeh sayde unto them, Tell you Hezekiah, I pray you, Thus sayth the great King, the King of Asshur, What confidence is this, wherein thou trustest?
36.5: I say, Surely I have eloquence, but counsel and strength are for the war: on whom then doest thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?
36.6: Loe, thou trustest in this broken staff of reed on Egypt, whereupon if a man lean, it will goe into his hand, and pearce it: so is Pharaoh King of Egypt, unto all that trust in him.
36.7: But if thou say to me, We trust in the Lord our God. Is not that he, whose hie places and whose altars Hezekiah took down, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?
36.8: Now therefore give hostages to my lord the King of Asshur, and I wil give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.
36.9: For how canst thou despise any captain of the least of my lordes servants? and put thy trust on Egypt for charets and for horsemen?
36.10: And am I now come up without the Lord to this land to destroy it? The Lord sayd unto me, Goe up against this land and destroy it.
36.11: Then sayd Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, to thy servants in the Aramites language, (for we understand it) and talk not with us in the Iewes tongue, in the audience of the people that are on the wall.
36.12: Then said Rabshakeh, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee to speak these wordes, and not to the men that sit on the wall? that they may eat their own doung, and drink their own piss with you?
36.13: So Rabshakeh stood, and cryed with a loud voyce in the Iewes language, and sayd, Hear the wordes of the great King, of the King of Asshur.
36.14: Thus saith the King, Let not Hezekiah deceive you: for he shall not be able to deliver you.
36.15: Neither let Hezekiah make you to trust in the Lord, saying, The Lord will surely deliver us: this citie shall not be given over into the hand of the King of Asshur.
36.16: Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus sayth the King of Asshur, Make appointment with me, and come out to me, that every man may eat of his own vine, and every man of his own fig tree, and drink every man the water of his own well,
36.17: Till I come and bring you to a land like your own land, even a land of wheat, and wine, a land of bread and vineyardes,
36.18: Least Hezekiah deceive you, saying, The Lord wil deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the King of Asshur?
36.19: Where is the god of Hamath, and of Arpad? where is the god of Sepharvaim? or how have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?
36.20: Who is hee among all the gods of these lands, that hath delivered their countrey out of mine hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of mine hand?
36.21: Then they kept silence, and answered him not a word: for the Kings commandement was, saying, Answer him not.
36.22: Then came Eliakim the sonne of Hilkiah the steward of the house, and Shebna the chanceller, and Joah the sonne of Asaph the recorder, unto Hezekiah with rent clothes, and told him the wordes of Rabshakeh.

37.1: And when the King Hezekiah heard it, he rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth and came into the House of the Lord.
37.2: And he sent Eliakim the steward of the house, aud Shebna the chanceller, with the Elders of the Priestes, clothed in sackcloth unto Isaiah the Prophet, the sonne of Amoz.
37.3: And they sayd unto him, Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of tribulation and of rebuke and blasphemie: for the children are come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring foorth.
37.4: If so be the Lord thy God hath heard the wordes of Rabshakeh, whom the King of Asshur his master hath sent to rail on the living God, and to reproch him with wordes which the Lord thy God hath heard, then lift thou up thy prayer for the remnant that are left.
37.5: So the servants of the King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
37.6: And Isaiah sayde unto them, Thus say unto your master, Thus saith the Lord, Be not afrayd of the wordes that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Asshur have blasphemed me.
37.7: Behold, I wil send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a noyse, and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.
37.8: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the King of Asshur fighting against Libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.
37.9: He heard also men say of Tirhakah, King of Ethiopia, Behold, he is come out to fight against thee: and when he heard it, he sent other messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
37.10: Thus shall ye speak to Hezekiah King of Judah, saying, Let not thy God deceive thee, in whom thou trustest, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the King of Asshur.
37.11: Behold, thou hast heard what the Kings of Asshur have done to all lands in destroying them, and shalt thou be delivered?
37.12: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed? as Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden, which were at Telassar?
37.13: Where is the King of Hamath, and the King of Arpad, and the King of the citie of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivah?
37.14: So Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers and read it, and he went up into the House of the Lord, and Hezekiah spread it before the Lord.
37.15: And Hezekiah prayed unto the Lord, saying,
37.16: O Lord of hostes, God of Israel, which dwellest between the Cherubims, thou art very God alone over all the kingdomes of the earth: thou hast made the heaven and the earth.
37.17: Encline thine ear, O Lord, and hear: open thine eyes, O Lord, and see, and hear all the wordes of Saneherib, who hath sent to blaspheme the living God.
37.18: Trueth it is, O Lord, that the Kings of Asshur have destroyed all lands, and their countrey,
37.19: And have cast their gods in ye fire: for they were no gods, but the work of mans hands, even wood or stone: therefore they destroyed them.
37.20: Now therefore, O Lord our God, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdomes of the earth may know, that thou onely art the Lord.
37.21: Then Isaiah the sonne of Amoz sent unto Hezekiah, saying, Thus sayth the Lord God of Israel, Because thou hast prayed unto me, concerning Saneherib king of Asshur,
37.22: This is the word that the Lord hath spoken against him, the virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn: the daughter of Jerusalem, hath shaken her head at thee.
37.23: Whom hast thou railed on and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voyce, and lifted up thine eyes on hie? even against the holy one of Israel.
37.24: By thy servants hast thou railed on the Lord, and sayd, By the multitude of my charets I am come up to the top of the mountaines to the sides of Lebanon, and will cut down the hie cedars thereof, and the fair fire trees thereof, and I will goe up to the heightes of his top and to the forest of his fruitful places.
37.25: I have digged and drunk the waters, and with the plant of my feet have I dryed all the rivers closed in.
37.26: Hast thou not heard how I have of old time made it, and have formed it long ago? and should I now bring it, that it should be destroyed, and layde on ruinous heapes, as cities defensed?
37.27: Whose inhabitants have small power, and are afrayd and confounded: they are like the grass of the field and green herb, or grass on the house tops, or corn blassed afore it be growen.
37.28: But I know thy dwelling, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy fury against me.
37.29: Because thou ragest against me, and thy tumult is come unto mine eares, therefore will I put mine hook in thy nostrels, and my bridle in thy lips, and wil bring thee back again the same way thou camest.
37.30: And this shalbe a sign unto thee, O Hezekiah, Thou shalt eat this yeere such as groweth of it self: and the second yeere, such things as grow without sowing: and in the third yeere, sow ye and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit thereof.
37.31: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah, shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
37.32: For out of Jerusalem shall goe a remnant, and they that escape out of mount Zion: the zeal of the Lord of hostes shall doe this.
37.33: Therefore thus sayth the Lord, concerning the King of Asshur, He shall not enter into this citie, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a mount against it.
37.34: By the same way that he came, he shall return, and not come into this citie, saith the Lord.
37.35: For I will defend this citie to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant Dauids sake.
37.36: Then the Angel of the Lord went out, and smote in the camp of Asshur an hundreth, fourescore, and five thousand: so when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.
37.37: So Saneherib king of Asshur departed, and went away and returned and dwelt at Nineveh.
37.38: And as he was in the temple worshipping of Nisroch his god, Adramelech and Sharezer his sonnes slew him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat: and Esarhaddon his sonne reigned in his stead.

38.1: About that time was Hezekiah sick unto the death, and the Prophet Isaiah sonne of Amoz came unto him, and sayd unto him, Thus sayth the Lord, Put thine house in an order, for thou shalt dye, and not live.
38.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, and prayed to the Lord,
38.3: And said, I beseech thee, Lord, remember now how I have walked before thee in trueth, and with a perfite heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight: and Hezekiah wept sore.
38.4: Then came the word of the Lord to Isaiah, saying,
38.5: Goe, and say unto Hezekiah, Thus saith the Lord God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, and seen thy teares: behold, I will add unto thy dayes fifteen yeeres.
38.6: And I will deliver thee out of the hand of the King of Asshur, and this citie: for I will defend this citie.
38.7: And this sign shalt thou have of ye Lord, that ye Lord will do this thing that he hath spoken,
38.8: Behold, I will bring again the shadow of the degrees (whereby it is gone down in the dial of Ahaz by the sunne) ten degrees backeward: so the sunne returned by tenne degrees, by the which degrees it was gone down.
38.9: The writing of Hezekiah King of Judah, when he had been sick, and was recovered of his sickenesse.
38.10: I said in the cutting off of my dayes, I shall goe to the gates of the grave: I am deprived of the residue of my yeeres.
38.11: I said, I shall not see the Lord, even the Lord in the land of the living: I shall see man no more among the inhabitants of the world.
38.12: Mine habitation is departed, and is removed from me, like a shepheards tent: I have cut off like a weaver my life: he will cut me off from the height: from day to night, thou wilt make an end of me.
38.13: I rekoned to the morning: but he brake all my bones, like a lion: from day to night wilt thou make an end of me.
38.14: Like a crane or a swallow, so did I chatter: I did mourn as a dove: mine eies were lift up on high: O Lord, it hath oppressed me, comfort me.
38.15: What shall I say? for he hath said it to me, and he hath done it: I shall walk weakely all my yeeres in the bitterness of my soul.
38.16: O Lord, to them that ouerliue them, and to all that are in them, the life of my spirit shalbe knowen, that thou causedst me to sleep and hast given life to me.
38.17: Behold, for felicitie I had bitter grief, but it was thy pleasure to deliver my soul from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sinnes behind thy back.
38.18: For the grave cannot confess thee: death cannot praise thee: they that goe down into the pit, cannot hope for thy trueth.
38.19: But the living, the living, he shall confess thee, as I doe this day: the father to the children shall declare thy trueth.
38.20: The Lord was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my song, all the dayes of our life in the House of the Lord.
38.21: Then said Isaiah, Take a lump of dry figs and lay it upon the boyle, and he shall recover.
38.22: Also Hezekiah had said, What is ye sign, that I shall goe up into the House of the Lord?

39.1: At the same time, Merodach Baladan, the sonne of Baladan, King of Babel, sent letters, and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.
39.2: And Hezekiah was glad of them, and shewed them the house of the treasures, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his kingdom that Hezekiah shewed them not.
39.3: Then came Isaiah the Prophet unto King Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they to thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far countrey unto me, from Babel.
39.4: Then said he, What have they seen in thine house? And Hezekiah answered, All that is in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures, that I have not shewed them.
39.5: And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord of hostes,
39.6: Behold, the dayes come, that all that is in thine house, and which thy fathers have layed up in store until this day, shall be caried to Babel: nothing shall be left, sayeth the Lord.
39.7: And of thy sonnes, that shall proceed out of thee, and which thou shalt beget, shall they take away, and they shall be eunuches in the palace of the King of Babel.
39.8: Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, The word of the Lord is good, which thou hast spoken: and he said, Yet let there be peace, and trueth in my dayes.

40.1: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, will your God say.
40.2: Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warrefare is accomplished, that her iniquitie is pardoned: for she hath received of the Lords hand double for all her sinnes.
40.3: A voyce cryeth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord: make streight in the desert a path for our God.
40.4: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shalbe streight, and the rough places plain.
40.5: And the glory of the Lord shalbe reueiled, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
40.6: A voyce said, Crie. And he said, What shall I crie? All flesh is grass, and all the grace thereof is as the flour of the field.
40.7: The grass withereth, the flour fadeth, because the Spirit of the Lord bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass.
40.8: The grass withereth, the flour fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
40.9: O Zion, that bringest good tidings, get thee up into the hie mountain: O Jerusalem, that bringest good tidings, lift up thy voyce with strength: lift it up, be not afraid: say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God.
40.10: Behold, the Lord God will come with power, and his arm shall rule for him: behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him,
40.11: He shall feed his flock like a shepheard: he shall gather the lambes with his arm, and cary them in his bosom, and shall guide them with young.
40.12: Who hath measured the waters in his fist? and counted heaven with the spanne, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure? and weighed ye mountaines in a weight, and the hilles in a balance?
40.13: Who hath instructed ye Spirit of the Lord? or was his counseler or taught him?
40.14: Of whom took he counsel, and who instructed him and taught him in the way of iudgement? or taught him knowledge, and shewed unto him the way of understanding?
40.15: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the dust of the balance: behold, he taketh away the yles as a litle dust.
40.16: And Lebanon is not sufficient for fire, nor the beastes thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.
40.17: All nations before him are as nothing, and they are counted to him, less then nothing, and vanitie.
40.18: To whom then wil ye liken God? or what similitude will ye set up unto him?
40.19: The workeman melteth an image, or the goldsmith beateth it out in gold, or the goldesmith maketh silver plates.
40.20: Doeth not the poor chuse out a tree that will not rot, for an oblation? he seeketh also unto him a cunning workeman, to prepare an image, that shall not be moved.
40.21: Know ye nothing? have ye not heard it? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understand it by the foundation of the earth?
40.22: He sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grashoppers, hee stretcheth out ye heavens, as a curtain, and spreadeth them out, as a tent to dwell in.
40.23: He bringeth the princes to nothing, and maketh the judges of the earth, as vanitie,
40.24: As though they were not plated, as though they were not sowen, as though their stock took no root in the earth: for he did even blow upon them, and they withered, and the whirlewinde will take them away as stubble.
40.25: To whom now will ye liken me, that I should be like him, saith the Holy one?
40.26: Lift up your eyes on hie, and behold who hath created these things, and bringeth out their armies by nomber, and calleth them all by names? by the greatness of his power and mightie strength nothing faileth.
40.27: Why sayest thou, O Iaakob, and speakest O Israel, My way is hid from the Lord, and my iudgement is passed over of my God?
40.28: Knowest thou not? or hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the Lord hath created the endes of the earth? he neither fainteth, nor is wearie: there is no searching of his understanding.
40.29: But he giveth strength unto him that fainteth, and unto him that hath no strength, he encreaseth power.
40.30: Even the yong men shall faint, and be wearie, and the yong men shall stumble and fall.
40.31: But they that wait upon the Lord, shall renue their strength: they shall lift up the wings as the eagles: they shall runne, and not be wearie, and they shall walk and not faint.

41.1: Keep silence before mee, O ylands, and let the people renue their strength: let the come neere, and let them speak: let us come together into iudgement.
41.2: Who raised up justice from the East, and called him to his foot? and gave the nations before him, and subdued the Kings? he gave them as dust to his sword, and as scattered stubble unto his bow.
41.3: He pursued them, and passed safely by the way that he had not gone with his feet.
41.4: Who hath wrought and done it? he that calleth the generations from the beginning. I the Lord am the first, and with the last I am ye same.
41.5: The yles saw it, and did fear, and the ends of the earth were abashed, drew neere, and came.
41.6: Every man helped his neighbour, and said to his brother, Be strong.
41.7: So the workeman comforted the founder, and he that smote with ye hammer, him that smote by course, saying, It is ready for the sodering, and he fastened it with nayles that it should not be mooued.
41.8: But thou, Israel, art my servant, and thou Iaakob, whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.
41.9: For I have taken thee from the endes of the earth, and called thee before the chief thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant: I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.
41.10: Fear thou not, for I am with thee: be not afraid, for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee, and help thee, and will susteine thee with the right hand of my justice.
41.11: Behold, all they that provoke thee, shalbe ashamed, and confounded: they shalbe as nothing, and they that strive with thee, shall perish.
41.12: Thou shalt seek them and shalt not find them: to wit, the men of thy strife, for they shall be as nothing, and the men that war against thee, as a thing of nought.
41.13: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not, I wil help thee.
41.14: Fear not, thou worm, Iaakob, and ye men of Israel: I wil help thee, sayth the Lord and thy redeemer the holy one of Israel.
41.15: Behold, I wil make thee a roller, and a new threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountaines, and bring them to pouder, and shalt make the hilles as chaff.
41.16: Thou shalt fanne them, and the wind shall carie them away, and the whirlewinde shall scatter them: and thou shalt reioyce in the Lord, and shalt glory in the holy one of Israel.
41.17: When the poor and the needy seek water, and there is none (their tongue faileth for thirst: I the Lord will hear them: I the God of Israel will not forsake them)
41.18: I will open rivers in the toppes of the hils, and fountaines in the middes of the valleis: I will make the wilderness as a pool of water, and the waste land as springs of water.
41.19: I will set in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrrh tree, and the pine tree, and I will set in the wilderness the fire tree, the elme and the box tree together.
41.20: Therefore let them see and know, and let them consider and vnderstande together that the hand of the Lord hath done this, and the holy one of Israel hath created it.
41.21: Stand to your cause, saith the Lord: bring forth your strong reasons, saith ye King of Iaakob.
41.22: Let them bring foorth, and let them tell us what shall come: let them shew the former things what they be, that wee may consider them, and know the latter end of them: either declare us things for to come.
41.23: Shew the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods: yea, doe good or doe evil, that we may declare it, and behold it together.
41.24: Behold, ye are of no value, and your making is of naught: man hath chosen an abomination by them.
41.25: I have raised up from the North, and he shall come: from the East sunne shall he cal upon my Name, and shall come upon princes as upon clay, and as the potter treadeth myre under the foot.
41.26: Who hath declared from the beginning, that we may know? or before time, that we may say, He is righteous? Surely there is none that sheweth: surely there is none that declareth: surely there is none that heareth your wordes.
41.27: I am the first, that saieth to Zion, Behold, behold them: and I will give to Jerusalem one that shall bring good tidings.
41.28: But when I beheld, there was none, and when I inquired of them, there was no counsellor, and when I demaunded of them, they answered not a woorde.
41.29: Behold, they are all vanitie: their work is of nothing, their images are wind and confusion.

42.1: Behold, my seruaunt: I will stay upon him: mine elect, in whom my soul deliteth: I have put my Spirit upon him: he shall bring forth iudgement to the Gentiles.
42.2: He shall not crie, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.
42.3: A bruised reed shall hee not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring foorth iudgement in trueth.
42.4: He shall not fail nor be discouraged till he have set iudgement in the earth: and the yles shall wait for his law.
42.5: Thus sayeth God the Lord (he that created the heavens and spred them abroad: he that stretched foorth the earth, and the buddes thereof: he that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein)
42.6: I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and I will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, and for a light of the Gentiles,
42.7: That thou maist open the eyes of the blind, and bring out the prisoners from the prison: and them that sitte in darkenesse, out of the prison house.
42.8: I am the Lord, this is my Name, and my glory wil I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.
42.9: Behold, the former thinges are come to pass, and new things doe I declare: before they come foorth, I tell you of them.
42.10: Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth: yee that goe down to the sea, and all that is therein: the yles and the inhabitants thereof.
42.11: Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voyce, the townes that Kedar doeth inhabit: let the inhabitants of the rocks sing: let them shout from the toppe of the mountaines.
42.12: Let them give glorie unto the Lord, and declare his praise in the ylands.
42.13: The Lord shall go forth as a gyant: he shall stirre up his courage like a man of war: he shall shout and crie, and shall prevail against his enemies.
42.14: I have a long time holden my peace: I have been still and refrained my self: now will I crie like a travailing woman: I will destroy and deuoure at once.
42.15: I will make waste mountaines, and hilles, and drie up all their herbes, and I will make the floods ylands, and I will drie up the pooles.
42.16: And I will bring the blind by a way, that they knew not, and lead them by paths that they have not knowen: I will make darkenesse light before them, and crooked thinges straight. These thinges will I doe unto them, and not forsake them.
42.17: They shall be turned back: they shall be greatly ashamed, that trust in graven images, and say to the molten images, Yee are our gods.
42.18: Hear, ye deaf: and ye blind, regard, that ye may see.
42.19: Who is blind but my seruaunt? or deaf as my messenger, that I sent? who is blind as the perfit, and blind as the Lordes servant?
42.20: Seeing many things, but thou keepest them not? opening the eares, but he heareth not?
42.21: The Lord is willing for his righteousness sake that he may magnifie the Law, and exalt it.
42.22: But this people is robbed and spoiled, and shalbe all snared in dungeons, and they shalbe hid in prison houses: they shall be for a pray, and none shall deliver: a spoil, and none shall say, Restore.
42.23: Who among you shall hearken to this, and take heed, and hear for afterwardes?
42.24: Who gave Iaakob for a spoyle, and Israel to the robbers? Did not ye Lord, because we have sinned against him? for they would not walk in his waies, neither be obedient unto his Law.
42.25: Therefore hee hath powred upon him his fierce wrath, and the strength of battell: and it set him on fire round about, and he knew not, and it burned him up, yet he considered not.

43.1: But now thus sayeth the Lord, that created thee, O Iaakob: and hee that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee: I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine.
43.2: When thou passest through the waters, I wil be with thee, and through the floods, that they doe not overflow thee. When thou walkest through the very fire, thou shalt not be burnt, neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
43.3: For I am the Lord thy God, the holy one of Israel, thy Sauiour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia, and Seba for thee.
43.4: Because thou wast precious in my sight, and thou wast honourable, and I loved thee, therefore will I give man for thee, and people for thy sake.
43.5: Fear not, for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the East, and gather thee from the West.
43.6: I will say to the North, Give: and to the South, Keep not back: bring my sonnes from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
43.7: Every one shall be called by my Name: for I created him for my glorie, formed him and made him.
43.8: I will bring foorth the blind people, and they shall have eyes, and the deaf, and they shall have eares.
43.9: Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this and shew us former things? let them bring foorth their witnesses, that they may be justified: but let them hear, and say, It is truth.
43.10: You are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant, whom I have chosen: therefore yee shall know and beleeue me and yee shall understand that I am: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.
43.11: I, even I am the Lord, and beside me there is no Sauiour.
43.12: I have declared, and I have saved, and I have shewed, when there was no strange god among you: therefore you are my witnesses, sayeth the Lord, that I am God.
43.13: Yea, before the day was, I am, and there is none that can deliver out of mine hand: I will doe it, and who shall let it?
43.14: Thus sayeth the Lord your redeemer, the holy one of Israel, For your sake I have sent to Babel, and brought it down: they are all fugitiues, and the Chaldeans crie in the shippes.
43.15: I am the Lord your holy one, the creator of Israel, your King.
43.16: Thus sayeth the Lord which maketh a way in the Sea, and a path in the mighty waters.
43.17: When hee bringeth out the charet and horse, the armie and the power lie together, and shall not rise: they are extinct, and quenched as tow.
43.18: Remember yee not the former things, neither regard the things of old.
43.19: Behold, I do a new thing: now shall it come foorth: shall you not know it? I wil even make a way in the desert, and floods in the wilderness.
43.20: The wild beastes shall honour mee, the dragons and the ostriches, because I gave water in the desert, and floods in the wilderness to give drink to my people, even to mine elect.
43.21: This people have I formed for my self: they shall shew foorth my praise.
43.22: And thou hast not called upon mee, O Iaakob, but thou hast wearied me, O Israel.
43.23: Thou hast not brought me the sheep of thy burnt offrings, neither hast thou honoured me with thy sacrifices. I have not caused thee to serve with an offring, nor wearied thee with incense.
43.24: Thou boughtest mee no sweet sauour with money, neither hast thou made mee drunk with the fatte of thy sacrifices, but thou hast made mee to serve with thy sinnes, and wearied mee with thine iniquities.
43.25: I, even I am he that putteth away thine iniquities for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sinnes.
43.26: Put me in remembrance: let us be judged together: count thou that thou maist be justified.
43.27: Thy first father hath sinned, and thy teachers have transgressed against me.
43.28: Therefore I have prophaned the rulers of the Sanctuarie, and have made Iaakob a curse, and Israel a reproche.

44.1: Yet now hear, O Iaakob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
44.2: Thus sayeth the Lord, that made thee, and formed thee from the womb: he wil help thee. Fear not, O Iaakob, my seruaunt, and thou righteous, whom I have chosen.
44.3: For I will powre water upon the thirstie, and floods upon the drie ground: I will powre my Spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thy buddes.
44.4: And they shall grow as among the grass, and as the willowes by the rivers of waters.
44.5: One shall say, I am the Lordes: another shalbe called by the name of Iaakob: and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and name himself by the name of Israel.
44.6: Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel and his redeemer, the Lord of hostes, I am the first, and I am the last, and without me is there no God.
44.7: And who is like me, that shall call, and shall declare it, and set it in order before me, since I appointed the ancient people? and what is at hand, and what things are to come? let them shew unto them.
44.8: Fear ye not, neither be afraid: have not I told thee of old, and have declared it? you are even my witnesses, whether there be a God beside me, and that there is no God that I know not.
44.9: All they that make an image, are vanitie, and their delectable things shall nothing profit: and they are their own witnesses, that they see not nor know: therefore they shalbe confounded.
44.10: Who hath made a god, or molten an image, that is profitable for nothing?
44.11: Behold, all that are of the fellowship thereof, shall be confounded: for the workemen themselves are men: let them all be gathered together, and stand up, yet they shall fear, and be confounded together.
44.12: The smith taketh an instrument, and worketh in the coles, and facioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with the strength of his armes: yea, he is an hungred, and his strength faileth: he drinketh no water, and is faint.
44.13: The carpenter stretcheth out a line: he facioneth it with a red thread, he planeth it, and he purtreyeth it with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, and according to the beautie of a man that it may remain in an house.
44.14: He will hew him down cedars, and take the pine tree and the oke, and taketh courage among the trees of the forest: he planteth a fire tree, and the rain doeth nourish it.
44.15: And man burneth thereof: for he will take thereof and warm himself: he also kindleth it and baketh bread, yet he maketh a god, and worshippeth it: he maketh it an idol and boweth unto it.
44.16: He burneth the half thereof even in the fire, and upon the half thereof he eateth flesh: he rosteth the roste and is satisfied: also he warmeth himself and sayth, Aha, I am warm, I have been at the fire.
44.17: And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his idol: he boweth unto it, and worshippeth and prayeth unto it, and sayeth, Deliver me: for thou art my god.
44.18: They have not knowen, nor understand: for God hath shut their eyes that they cannot see, and their heartes, that they cannot understand.
44.19: And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burnt half of it, even in the fire, and have baked bread also upon the coles thereof: I have rosted flesh, and eaten it, and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I bow to the stock of a tree?
44.20: He feedeth of ashes: a seduced heart hath deceived him, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lye in my right hand?
44.21: Remember these (O Iaakob and Israel) for thou art my servant: I have formed thee: thou art my servant: O Israel forget me not.
44.22: I have put away thy transgressions like a cloud, and thy sinnes, as a mist: turn unto me, for I have redeemed thee.
44.23: Reioyce, ye heavens: for the Lord hath done it: shout, ye lower partes of the earth: brast foorth into prayses, ye mountaines, O forest and every tree therein: for the Lord hath redeemed Iaakob and will be glorified in Israel.
44.24: Thus sayeth the Lord thy redeemer and he that formed thee from the womb, I am the Lord, that made all things, that spred out the heavens alone, and stretched out the earth by my self.
44.25: I destroy the tokens of ye southsayers, and make them that coniecture, fooles, and turn the wise men backward, and make their knowledge foolishness.
44.26: He confirmeth the word of his servant and performeth the counsel of his messengers, saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt bee inhabited: and to the cities of Judah, Yee shall be built up, and I will repayre the decayed places thereof.
44.27: He saith to the deep, Be dry and I will dry up thy floods.
44.28: He saith to Cyrus, Thou art my shepheard: and he shall perform all my desire: saying also to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built: and to the Temple, Thy foundation shall be surely layed.

45.1: Thus sayeth the Lord unto Cyrus his anointed, whose right hand I have holden to subdue nations before him: therefore will I weaken the loynes of Kings and open the doores before him, and the gates shall not be shut:
45.2: I will goe before thee and make the crooked streight: I will break the brasen doores, and burst the yron barres.
45.3: And I will give thee the treasures of darkenesse, and the things hid in secret places, that thou maist know that I am the Lord which call thee by thy name, even the God of Israel.
45.4: For Iaakob my servants sake, and Israel mine elect, I will even call thee by thy name and name thee, though thou hast not knowen me.
45.5: I am the Lord and there is none other: there is no God besides me: I girded thee though thou hast not knowen me,
45.6: That they may know from the rising of the sunne and from the West, that there is none besides me. I am the Lord, and there is none other.
45.7: I form the light and create darkenes: I make peace and create evil: I the Lord doe all these things.
45.8: Ye heavens, send the dew from above, and let the cloudes droppe down righteousness: let the earth open, and let salvation and justice grow foorth: let it bring them foorth together: I the Lord have created him.
45.9: Woe be unto him that striveth with his maker, the potsherd with the potsherds of the earth: shall the clay say to him that facioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, It hath none hands?
45.10: Woe unto him that sayeth to his father, What hast thou begotten? or to his mother, What hast thou brought foorth?
45.11: Thus saith the Lord, the holy one of Israel, and his maker, Ask me of things to come concerning my sonnes, and concerning the workes of mine hands: command you me.
45.12: I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, whose hands have spred out the heavens, I have even commanded all their armie.
45.13: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his wayes: he shall build my citie, and he shall let goe my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the Lord of hostes.
45.14: Thus sayth the Lord, The labour of Egypt, and the marchandise of Ethiopia, and of the Sabeans, men of stature shall come unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall follow thee, and shall goe in chaines: they shall fall down before thee, and make supplication unto thee, saying, Surely God is in thee, and there is none other God besides.
45.15: Verely thou, O God, hidest thy self, O God, the Sauiour of Israel.
45.16: All they shalbe ashamed and also confounded: they shall goe to confusion together, that are the makers of images.
45.17: But Israel shall be saved in the Lord, with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.
45.18: For thus saith the Lord (that created heaven, God himself, that formed the earth, and made it: he that prepared it, he created it not in vain: he formed it to be inhabited) I am the Lord, and there is none other.
45.19: I have not spoken in secret, neither in a place of darkenes in the earth: I said not in vain unto the seed of Iaakob, Seek you me: I the Lord doe speak righteousness, and declare righteous things.
45.20: Assemble your selves, and come: draw neere together, ye abiect of the Gentiles: they have no knowledge, that set up the wood of their idol, and pray unto a god, that cannot save them.
45.21: Tell ye and bring them, and let them take counsel together, who hath declared this from the beginning? or hath told it of old? Have not I the Lord? and there is none other God beside me, a just God, and a Sauiour: there is none beside me.
45.22: Look unto me, and ye shall be saved: all the endes of the earth shall be saved: for I am God, and there is none other.
45.23: I have sworn by my self: the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That every knee shall bow unto me, and every tongue shall swear by me.
45.24: Surely he shall say, In the Lord have I righteousness and strength: he shall come unto him, and all that provoke him, shall be ashamed.
45.25: The whole seed of Israel shall be justified, and glorie in the Lord.

46.1: Bel is bowed down: Nebo is fallen: their idoles were upon the beastes, and upon the cattell: they which did bear you, were laden with a wearie burden.
46.2: They are bowed down, and fallen together: for they could not rid them of the burden, and their soul is gone into captiuitie.
46.3: Hear ye me, O house of Iaakob, and all that remain of the house of Israel, which are borne of me from the womb, and brought up of me from the birth.
46.4: Therefore unto old age, I the same, even I will bear you until the hoar heares: I have made you: I will also bear you, and I will cary you and I will deliver you.
46.5: To whom will ye make me like or make me equal, or copare me, that I should be like him?
46.6: They draw gold out of the bagge and weigh silver in the balance, and hire a goldsmith to make a god of it, and they bow down, and worship it.
46.7: They bear it upon the shoulders: they carie him and set him in his place: so doeth he stand, and cannot remove from his place. Though one crie unto him, yet can he not answer, nor deliver him out of his tribulation.
46.8: Remember this, and be ashamed: bring it again to mind, O you transgressers.
46.9: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none other God, and there is nothing like me,
46.10: Which declare the last thing from the beginning: and from of old, the things that were not done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will doe whatsoever I will.
46.11: I call a bird from the East, and the man of my counsel from far: as I have spoken, so will I bring it to pass: I have purposed it, and I will doe it.
46.12: Hear me, ye stubburne hearted, that are far from justice.
46.13: I bring neere my justice: it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarie: for I wil give salvation in Zion, and my glory unto Israel.

47.1: Come down and sit in the dust: O virgin, daughter Babel, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, Tender and delicate.
47.2: Take the mill stones, and grind meal: loose thy lockes: make bare the feet: vncouer the legge, and pass through the floods.
47.3: Thy filthiness shall be discovered, and thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.
47.4: Our redeemer, the Lord of hostes is his Name, the holy one of Israel.
47.5: Sit still, and get thee into darkenesse, O daughter of the Chaldeas: for thou shalt no more be called, The ladie of kingdomes.
47.6: I was wroth with my people: I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine had: thou diddest shew them no mercy, but thou didest lay thy very heavy yoke upon the ancient.
47.7: And thou saidest, I shall be a ladie for ever, so that thou diddest not set thy mind to these things, neither diddest thou remember ye latter end therof.
47.8: Therefore now hear, thou that art given to pleasures, and dwellest careless, She sayeth in her heart, I am and none els: I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall know the loss of children.
47.9: But these two thinges shall come to thee suddenly on one day, the loss of children and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection, for the multitude of thy divinations, and for the great abundance of thine inchanters.
47.10: For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast sayd, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, they have caused thee to rebel, and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none els.
47.11: Therefore shall evil come upon thee, and thou shalt not know the morning thereof: destruction shall fal upon thee, which thou shalt not be able to put away: destruction shall come upon thee suddenly, or thou beware.
47.12: Stand now among thine inchanters, and in the multitude of thy southsaiers (with whom thou hast wearied thy self from thy youth) if so be thou maist have profit, or if so be thou maist have strength.
47.13: Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels: let now the astrologers, the star gasers, and prognosticatours stand up, and save thee from these things, that shall come upon thee.
47.14: Behold, they shall be as stubble: the fire shall burn them: they shall not deliver their own lives from the power of the flame: there shalbe no coles to warm at, nor light to sit by.
47.15: Thus shall they serve thee, with whom thou hast wearied thee, even thy marchants from thy youth: every one shall wander to his own quarter: none shall save thee.

48.1: Hear yee this, O house of Iaakob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come out of the waters of Judah: which swear by the Name of the Lord, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness.
48.2: For they are called of the holy citie, and staie themselves upon the God of Israel, whose Name is the Lord of hostes.
48.3: I have declared ye former things of old, and they went out of my mouth, and I shewed them: I did them suddenly, and they came to pass.
48.4: Because I knew, that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an yron sinew, and thy brow brass,
48.5: Therefore I have declared it to thee of old: before it came to pass, I shewed it thee, lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my carved image, and my molten image hath commanded them.
48.6: Thou hast heard, behold all this, and wil not yee declare it? I have shewed thee new things, even now, and hid things, which thou knewest not.
48.7: They are created now, and not of old, and even before this thou heardest them not, lest thou shouldest say, Behold, I knew them.
48.8: Yet thou heardest them not, neither diddest know them, neither yet was thine ear opened of old: for I knew that thou wouldest grieuously transgress: therefore have I called thee a transgressour from the womb.
48.9: For my Names sake will I defer my wrath, and for my praise will I refrain it from thee, that I cut thee not off.
48.10: Behold, I have fined thee, but not as silver: I have chosen thee in the fornace of affliction.
48.11: For mine own sake, for mine own sake wil I doe it: for how should my Name be polluted? surely I wil not give my glory unto another.
48.12: Hear me, O Iaakob and Israel, my called, I am, I am the first, and I am the last.
48.13: Surely mine hand hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heaues: when I cal them, they stand up together.
48.14: All you, assemble your selves, and hear: which among them hath declared these thinges? The Lord hath loved him: he wil doe his will in Babel, and his arm shalbe against the Chaldeans.
48.15: I, even I have spoken it, and I have called him: I have brought him, and his way shall prosper.
48.16: Come neere unto me: hear ye this: I have not spoken it in secret from the beginning: from the time that the thing was, I was there, and now the Lord God and his Spirit hath sent me.
48.17: Thus saith the Lord thy redeemer, the Holy one of Israel, I am the Lord thy God, which teach thee to profit, and lead thee by the way, that thou shouldest goe.
48.18: Oh that thou haddest hearkened to my commandements! then had thy prosperitie been as the floude, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea.
48.19: Thy seed also had been as the sand, and the fruit of thy body like the gravel thereof: his name should not have been cut off nor destroied before me.
48.20: Goe yee out of Babel: flee yee from the Chaldeans, with a voice of joy: tel and declare this: shew it foorth to the end of the earth: say yee, The Lord hath redeemed his servant Iaakob.
48.21: And they were not thirstie: hee led them through the wilderness: hee caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them: for he clave the rock, and the water gushed out.
48.22: There is no peace, sayeth the Lord, unto the wicked.

49.1: Hear yee me, O yles, and hearken, yee people from far. The Lord hath called me from the womb, and made mention of my name from my mothers bellie.
49.2: And hee hath made my mouth like a sharp sword: under the shadow of his hand hath he hid mee, and made me a chosen shaft, and hid me in his quiuer,
49.3: And sayd unto me, Thou art my seruaunt, Israel, for I will be glorious in thee.
49.4: And I said, I have labored in vain: I have spent my strength in vain and for nothing: but my iudgement is with the Lord, and my woorke with my God.
49.5: And now sayeth the Lord, that formed me from the womb to be his seruaunt, that I may bring Iaakob again to him (though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I bee glorious in the eyes of the Lord: and my God shall be my strength)
49.6: And hee sayde, It is a small thing that thou shouldest be my seruaunt, to raise up the tribes of Iaakob, and to restore the desolations of Israel: I will also give thee for a light of the Gentiles, that thou maiest bee my salvation unto the end of the world.
49.7: Thus sayeth the Lord the redeemer of Israel, and his Holie one, to him that is despised in soul, to a nation that is abhorred, to a seruaunt of rulers, Kinges shall see, and arise, and princes shall worship, because of the Lord, that is faithful: and ye Holy one of Israel, which hath chosen thee.
49.8: Thus sayeth the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and wil give thee for a covenant of ye people, that thou maiest raise up the earth, and obtain the inheritance of the desolate heritages:
49.9: That thou maiest say to the prisoners, Goe foorth: and to them that are in darkenesse, Shew your selves: they shall feed in the waies, and their pastures shall bee in all the toppes of the hilles.
49.10: They shall not be hungrie, neither shall they be thirstie, neither shall the heat smite them, nor the sunne: for he that hath compassion on them, shall lead them: even to the springs of waters shall he drive them.
49.11: And I will make all my mountaines, as a way, and my paths shalbe exalted.
49.12: Behold, these shall come from far: and loe, these from the North and from the West, and these from the land of Sinim.
49.13: Reioyce, O heavens: and bee ioyfull, O earth: brast foorth into praise, O mountaines: for God hath comforted his people, and will have mercie upon his afflicted.
49.14: But Zion said, The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me.
49.15: Can a woman forget her child, and not have compassion on the sonne of her womb? though they should forget, yet wil I not forget thee.
49.16: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palm of mine hands: thy walles are ever in my sight.
49.17: Thy builders make haste: thy destroiers and they that made thee waste, are departed from thee.
49.18: Lift up thine eies round about and behold: all these gather themselves together and come to thee: as I live, sayeth the Lord, thou shalt surely put them all upon thee as a garment, and gird thy self with them like a bride.
49.19: For thy desolations, and thy waste places, and thy land destroied, shall surely be now narow for them that shall dwell in it, and they that did deuoure thee, shalbe far away.
49.20: The children of thy barennesse shall say again in thine eares, The place is straict for mee: give place to me that I may dwell.
49.21: Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten mee these, seeing I am baren and desolate, a captive and a wanderer to and from? and who hath nourished them? behold, I was left alone: whence are these?
49.22: Thus sayeth the Lord God, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles and set up my stadart to the people, and they shall bring thy sonnes in their armes: and thy daughters shall be caried upon their shoulders.
49.23: And Kings shalbe thy nourcing fathers, and Queenes shalbe thy nources: they shall worship thee with their faces toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.
49.24: Shall the pray be taken from the mightie? or the just captiuitie delivered?
49.25: But thus sayeth the Lord, even the captiuitie of the mightie shall be taken away: and the pray of the tyrant shall be delivered: for I wil contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children,
49.26: And will feed them that spoil thee, with their own flesh, and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the Lord am thy sauiour and thy redeemer, the mighty one of Iaakob.

50.1: Thus sayeth the Lord, Where is that bill of your mothers divorcement, whom I have cast off? or who is the creditour to whom I sold you? Behold, for your iniquities are yee sold, and because of your transgressions is your mother forsaken.
50.2: Wherefore came I, and there was no man? I called, and none answered: is mine hand so shortened, that it cannot help? or have I no power to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I drie up the Sea: I make the floods desert: their fish rotteth for want of water, and dieth for thirst.
50.3: I clothe the heavens with darkenesse, and make a sack their covering.
50.4: The Lord God hath given me a tongue of the learned, that I should know to minister a woord in time to him that is weary: he will raise me up in the morning: in the morning hee will waken mine ear to hear, as the learned.
50.5: The Lord God hath opened mine ear and I was not rebellious, neither turned I back.
50.6: I gave my back unto the smiters, and my cheekes to the nippers: I hid not my face from shame and spitting.
50.7: For the Lord God will help me, therefore shall I not bee confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.
50.8: Hee is neere that justifieth mee: who will contend with me? Let us stand together: who is mine aduersarie? let him come neere to me.
50.9: Behold, the Lord God will help me: who is he that can condemn me? loe, they shall wax old as a garment: the moth shall eat them up.
50.10: Who is among you that feareth the Lord? let him hear the voyce of his servant: hee that walketh in darkenesse, and hath no light, let him trust in the Name of the Lord, and stay upon his God.
50.11: Behold, all you kindle a fire, and are compassed about with sparkes: walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparkes that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand: ye shall lye down in sorowe.

51.1: Hear me, ye that follow after righteousnes, and ye that seek the Lord: look unto the rock, whence ye are hewen, and to the hole of the pit, whence ye are digged.
51.2: Consider Abraham your father, and Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.
51.3: Surely the Lord shall comfort Zion: he shall comfort all her desolations, and he shall make her desert like Eden, and her wildernes like the garden of the Lord: joy and gladness shalbe found therein: praise, and the voyce of singing.
51.4: Hearken ye unto me, my people, and give ear unto me, O my people: for a Law shall proceed from me, and I will bring foorth my iudgement for the light of the people.
51.5: My righteousnes is neere: my salvation goeth foorth, and mine armes shall judge the people: the yles shall wait for me, and shall trust unto mine arm.
51.6: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein, shall perish in like maner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not bee abolished.
51.7: Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my Law. Fear ye not the reproche of men, neither be ye afraid of their rebukes.
51.8: For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shalbe for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation.
51.9: Rise up, rise up, and put on strength, O arm of the Lord: rise up as in the old time in the generations of the world. Art not thou the same, that hath cutte Rahab, and wounded the dragon?
51.10: Art not thou the same, which hath dried the Sea, even the waters of the great deep, making the depth of the Sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
51.11: Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come with joy unto Zion, and everlasting joy shalbe upon their head: they shall obtain joy, and gladness: and sorow and mourning shall flee away.
51.12: I, even I am he, that comfort you. Who art thou, that thou shouldest fear a mortal man, and the sonne of man, which shalbe made as grass?
51.13: And forgettest the Lord thy maker, that hath spred out the heavens, and layde the foundations of the earth? and hast feared continually all the day, because of the rage of the oppressour, which is readie to destroy? Where is now the rage of the oppressour?
51.14: The captive hasteneth to be loosed, and that hee should not die in the pitte, nor that his bread should fail.
51.15: And I am the Lord thy God that deuided the Sea, when his waves roared: the Lord of hostes is his Name.
51.16: And I have put my wordes in thy mouth, and have defended thee in the shadow of mine hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundation of the earth, and say unto Zion, Thou art my people.
51.17: Awake, awake, and stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath: thou hast drunken the dregges of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.
51.18: There is none to guide her among all the sonnes, whom she hath brought foorth: there is none that taketh her by the hand of all the sonnes that she hath brought up.
51.19: These two thinges are come unto thee: who will lament thee? desolation and destruction and famine, and the sword: by whom shall I comfort thee?
51.20: Thy sonnes have fainted, and lye at the head of all the streetes as a wild bull in a nette, and are full of the wrath of the Lord, and rebuke of thy God.
51.21: Therefore hear now this, thou miserable and drunken, but not with wine.
51.22: Thus saith thy Lord God, even God that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cuppe of trembling, even the dregges of the cuppe of my wrath: thou shalt drink it no more.
51.23: But I will put it into their hand that spoil thee: which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that wee may goe over, and thou hast layde thy bodie as the ground, and as the street to them that went over.

52.1: Aries, arise: put on thy strength, O Zion: put on thy garments of thy beautie, O Jerusalem, the holy citie: for hencefoorth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the vncleane.
52.2: Shake thy self from the dust: arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose the bandes of thy neck, O thou captive daughter, Zion.
