52.3: For thus sayeth the Lord, Yee were sold for naught: therefore shall ye be redeemed without money.
52.4: For thus saith the Lord God, My people went down afore time into Egypt to soiourne there, and Asshur oppressed them without cause.
52.5: Now therefore what have I here, saith the Lord, that my people is taken away for naught, and they that rule over them, make them to howl, saith the Lord? and my Name all the day continually is blasphemed?
52.6: Therefore my people shall know my Name: therefore they shall know in that day, that I am he that doe speak: behold, it is I.
52.7: How beautiful upon the mountaines are the feet of him, that declareth and publisheth peace? that declareth good tidings, and publisheth salvation, saying unto Zion, Thy God reigneth?
52.8: The voyce of thy watchmen shalbe heard: they shall lift up their voyce, and shout together: for they shall see eye to eye, when the Lord shall bring again Zion.
52.9: O ye desolate places of Jerusalem, bee glad and reioyce together: for the Lord hath comforted his people: he hath redeemed Jerusalem.
52.10: The Lord hath made bare his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles, and all the endes of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.
52.11: Depart, depart ye: goe out from thence and touch no vncleane thing: goe out of the middes of her: be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the Lord.
52.12: For ye shall not goe out with haste, nor depart by fleeing away: but the Lord will goe before you, and the God of Israel will gather you together.
52.13: Behold, my servant shall prosper: he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very hie.
52.14: As many were astonied at thee (his visage was so deformed of men, and his form of the sonnes of men) so shall hee sprinkle many nations: the Kings shall shut their mouthes at him: for that which had not been told them, shall they see, and that which they had not heard, shall they vnderstande.

53.1: Who will beleeue our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord reueiled?
53.2: But hee shall grow up before him as a branch, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath neither form nor beautie: when we shall see him, there shall be no form that wee should desire him.
53.3: He is despised and reiected of men: he is a man full of sorowes and hath experience of infirmities: we hid as it were our faces from him: he was despised and we esteemed him not.
53.4: Surely hee hath borne our infirmities, and caried our sorowes: yet wee did judge him, as plagued, and smitten of God, and humbled.
53.5: But hee was wounded for our transgressions, hee was broken for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and with his stripes we are healed.
53.6: All we like sheep have gone astray: wee have turned every one to his own way, and the Lord hath layed upon him the iniquitie of us all.
53.7: Hee was oppressed and he was afflicted, yet did he not open his mouth: hee is brought as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearer is dumme, so he openeth not his mouth.
53.8: Hee was taken out from prison, and from iudgement: and who shall declare his age? for he was cut out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he plagued.
53.9: And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though hee had done no wickedness, neither was any deceit in his mouth.
53.10: Yet the Lord would break him, and make him subiect to infirmities: when hee shall make his soul an offring for sinne, he shall see his seed and shall prolong his dayes, and the will of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.
53.11: Hee shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant iustifie many: for hee shall bear their iniquities.
53.12: Therefore will I give him a portion with the great, and he shall deuide the spoyle with the strong, because hee hath powred out his soul unto death: and he was counted with the transgressers, and he bare the sinne of many, and prayed for the trespassers.

54.1: Rejoice, O barren that diddest not bear: break forth into joy and reioyce, thou that diddest not travail with child: for the desolate hath moe children then the married wife, sayeth the Lord.
54.2: Enlarge the place of thy tents, and let them spread out the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, stretch out thy cords and make fast thy stakes.
54.3: For thou shalt increase on the right hand and on the left, and thy seed shall possess the Gentiles, and dwell in the desolate cities.
54.4: Fear not: for thou shalt not be ashamed, neither shalt thou be confounded: for thou shalt not bee put to shame: yea, thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproch of thy widdowhoode any more.
54.5: For hee that made thee, is thine husband (whose Name is the Lord of hostes) and thy redeemer the Holy one of Israel, shall be called the God of the whole world.
54.6: For the Lord hath called thee, being as a woman forsaken, and afflicted in spirit, and as a yong wife when thou wast refused, sayth thy God.
54.7: For a litle while have I forsaken thee, but with great compassion will I gather thee.
54.8: For a moment, in mine anger, I hid my face from thee for a litle season, but with everlasting mercy have I had compassion on thee, sayth the Lord thy redeemer.
54.9: For this is unto me as the waters of Noah: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more goe over the earth, so have I sworn that I would not be angrie with thee, nor rebuke thee.
54.10: For the mountaines shall remove and the hilles shall fall down: but my mercy shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace fall away, saith the Lord, that hath compassion on thee.
54.11: O thou afflicted and tossed with tempest, that hast no comfort, behold, I wil lay thy stones with the carbuncle, and lay thy foundation with saphirs,
54.12: And I will make thy windowes of emeraudes, and thy gates shining stones, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.
54.13: And all thy children shalbe taught of the Lord, and much peace shalbe to thy children.
54.14: In righteousnes shalt thou be established, and be far from oppression: for thou shalt not fear it: and from fear, for it shall not come neere thee.
54.15: Behold, the enemie shall gather himself, but without me: whosoever shall gather himself in thee, against thee, shall fall.
54.16: Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coales in the fire, and him that bringeth forth an instrument for his work, and I have created the destroyer to destroy.
54.17: But all the weapons that are made against thee, shall not prosper: and every tongue that shall rise against thee in iudgement, thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the Lords servants, and their righteousness is of me, sayth the Lord.

55.1: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and ye that have no silver, come, bye and eat: come, I say, bye wine and milk without silver and without money.
55.2: Wherefore doe ye lay out silver and not for bread? and your labour without being satisfied? hearken diligently unto me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delite in fatnes.
55.3: Encline your eares, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live, and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
55.4: Behold, I gave him for a witnes to the people, for a prince and a master unto the people.
55.5: Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and a nation that knew not thee, shall runne unto thee, because of the Lord thy God, and the holy one of Israel: for hee hath glorified thee.
55.6: Seek ye the Lord while he may be found: call ye upon him while he is neere.
55.7: Let the wicked forsake his wayes, and the unrighteous his own imaginations, and return unto the Lord, and he wil have mercy upon him: and to our God, for hee is very ready to forgive.
55.8: For my thoughtes are not your thoughts, neither are your wayes my wayes, sayth the Lord.
55.9: For as ye heavens are higher then the earth, so are my wayes higher then your wayes, and my thoughtes above your thoughts.
55.10: Surely as the rain cometh down and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth and maketh it to bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread unto him that eateth,
55.11: So shall my word be, that goeth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me voyde, but it shall accomplish that which I will, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.
55.12: Therefore ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountaines and the hilles shall break foorth before you into ioye, and all the trees of the field shall clap their handes.
55.13: For thornes there shall grow fire trees: for nettles shall grow the myrrh tree, and it shalbe to the Lord for a name, and for an everlasting sign that shall not be taken away.

56.1: Thus saith the Lord, Keep iudgement and doe justice: for my salvation is at hand to come, and my righteousnes to be reueiled.
56.2: Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the sonne of man which layeth hold on it: hee that keepeth the Sabbath and polluteth it not, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil.
56.3: And let not the sonne of the stranger, which is ioyned to the Lord, speak and say, The Lord hath surely separate me from his people: neither let the Eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree.
56.4: For thus saith the Lord unto the Eunuches, that keep my Sabbaths, and chuse the thing that pleaseth me, and take hold of my covenant,
56.5: Even unto them wil I give in mine House and within my walles, a place and a name better then of the sonnes and of the daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be put out.
56.6: Also the strangers that cleave unto the Lord, to serve him, and to love the Name of the Lord, and to be his servants: every one that keepeth the Sabbath, and polluteth it not and imbraceth my covenant,
56.7: Them wil I bring also to mine holy mountain, and make them ioyfull in mine House of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar: for mine House shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
56.8: The Lord God sayth, which gathereth the scattered of Israel, Yet wil I gather to them those that are to be gathered to them.
56.9: All ye beastes of the field, come to deuoure, even all ye beastes of the forest.
56.10: Their watchmen are all blind: they have no knowledge: they are all dumme dogs: they can not bark: they lie and sleep and delite in sleeping.
56.11: And these griedy dogs can never have ynough: and these shepheards cannot understand: for they all look to their own way, every one for his advantage, and for his own purpose.
56.12: Come, I wil bring wine, and we wil fill our selves with strong drink, and to morowe shalbe as this day, and much more abundant.

57.1: The righteous perisheth, and no man considereth it in heart: and merciful men are taken away, and no man understandeth that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.
57.2: Peace shall come: they shall rest in their beds, every one that walketh before him.
57.3: But you witches children, come hither, the seed of the adulterer and of the whore.
57.4: On whom have ye iested? upon whom have ye gaped and thrust out your tongue? are not ye rebellious children, and a false seed?
57.5: Inflamed with idoles under every green tree? and sacrificing the children in the valleys under the tops of the rocks?
57.6: Thy portion is in the smooth stones of the river: they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou powred a drink offering: thou hast offered a sacrifice. Should I delite in these?
57.7: Thou hast made thy bed upon a very hie mountain: thou wentest up thither, even thither wentest thou to offer sacrifice.
57.8: Behind the doores also and postes hast thou set up thy remembrance: for thou hast discovered thy self to another then me, and wentest up, and diddest enlarge thy bed, and make a covenant between thee and them, and lovedst their bed in every place where thou sawest it.
57.9: Thou wentest to the Kings with oyle, and diddest increase thine oyntments and send thy messengers far off, and diddest humble thy self unto hell.
57.10: Thou weariedst thy self in thy manifold journeys, yet saydest thou not, There is no hope: thou hast found life by thine hand, therefore thou wast not grieved.
57.11: And whom diddest thou reverence or fear, seeing thou hast lyed unto me, and hast not remembred me, neither set thy mind thereon? is it not because I hold my peace, and that of long time? therefore thou fearest not me.
57.12: I will declare thy righteousnes and thy workes, and they shall not profit thee.
57.13: When thou cryest, let them that thou hast gathered together deliver thee: but the wind shall take them all away: vanitie shall pull them away: but he that trusteth in me, shall inherit the land, and shall possess mine holy Mountain.
57.14: And he shall say, Cast up, cast up: prepare the way: take up the stumbling blocks out of the way of my people.
57.15: For thus sayth he that is hie and excellent, he that inhabiteth the eternitie, whose Name is the Holy one, I dwell in the high and holy place: with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit to revive the spirit of the humble, and to give life to them that are of a contrite heart.
57.16: For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be alwayes wroth, for the spirit should fayle before me: and I have made the breath.
57.17: For his wicked couetousnesse I am angry with him, and have smitten him: I hid mee and was angry, yet he went away, and turned after the way of his own heart.
57.18: I have seen his wayes, and wil heal him: I wil lead him also, and restore comfort unto him, and to those that lament him.
57.19: I create the fruit of the lips, to be peace: peace unto them that are far off, and to them that are neere, sayth the Lord: for I will heal him.
57.20: But the wicked are like the raging sea, that can not rest, whose waters cast up myre and dirt.
57.21: There is no peace, sayth my God, to the wicked.

58.1: Cry aloud, spare not: lift up thy voyce like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and to the house of Iaakob, their sinnes.
58.2: Yet they seek me dayly, and will know my wayes, even as a nation that did righteously, and had not forsaken the statutes of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice: they wil draw neere unto God, saying,
58.3: Wherefore have we fasted, and thou seest it not? we have punished our selves, and thou regardest it not. Behold, in the day of your fast you will seek your will, and require all your dettes.
58.4: Behold, ye fast to strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye doe to day, to make your voyce to be heard above.
58.5: Is it such a fast that I have chosen, that a man should afflict his soul for a day, and to bow down his head, as a bull rush, and to lie down in sackecloth and ashes? wilt thou call this a fasting, or an acceptable day to the Lord?
58.6: Is not this the fasting, that I have chosen, to loose the bandes of wickednes, to take off the heauie burdens, and to let the oppressed goe free, and that ye break every yoke?
58.7: Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that wander, unto thine house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him, and hide not thy self from thine own flesh?
58.8: Then shall thy light break foorth as the morning, and thine health shall grow speedily: thy righteousnes shall goe before thee, and the glorie of the Lord shall embrace thee.
58.9: Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer: thou shalt cry and hee shall say, Here I am: if thou take away from the mids of thee the yoke, the putting foorth of the finger, and wicked speaking:
58.10: If thou powre out thy soul to the hungrie, and refresh the troubled soul: then shall thy light spring out in the darkenes, and thy darkenes shalbe as the noon day.
58.11: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfie thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watred garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
58.12: And they shalbe of thee, that shall build the old waste places: thou shalt rayse up the foundations for many generations, and thou shalt be called the repairer of the breach and the restorer of the pathes to dwell in.
58.13: If thou turn away thy foot from the Sabbath, from doing thy will on mine holy day, and call the Sabbath a delite, to consecrate it, as glorious to the Lord, and shalt honour him, not doing thine own wayes, nor seeking thine own will, nor speaking a vain word,
58.14: Then shalt thou delite in the Lord, and I wil cause thee to mount upon the hie places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Iaakob thy father: for the mouth of ye Lord hath spoken it.

59.1: Behold, the Lordes hand is not shortened, that it can not save: neither is his ear heauie, that it cannot hear.
59.2: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sinnes have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.
59.3: For your handes are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquitie: your lips have spoken lies and your tongue hath murmured iniquitie.
59.4: No man calleth for justice: no man contendeth for trueth: they trust in vanitie, and speak vain things: they conceive mischief, and bring foorth iniquitie.
59.5: They hatch cockatrice egges, and weave the spiders webbe: he that eateth of their egges, dieth, and that which is trode upon, breaketh out into a serpent.
59.6: Their webbes shall be no garment, neither shall they cover themselves with their labours: for their workes are workes of iniquitie, and the work of crueltie is in their handes.
59.7: Their feet runne to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are wicked thoughts: desolation and destruction is in their paths.
59.8: The way of peace they know not, and there is none equitie in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein, shall not know peace.
59.9: Therefore is iudgement far from us, neither doeth justice come neere unto us: we wait for light, but loe, it is darkenesse: for brightness, but we walk in darkenesse.
59.10: Wee grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as one without eyes: we stumble at the noon day as in the twilight: we are in solitarie places, as dead men.
59.11: We roar all like beares, and mourn like dooues: wee look for equitie, but there is none: for health, but it is far from us.
59.12: For our trespasses are many before thee, and our sinnes testifie against us: for our trespasses are with us, and we know our iniquities
59.13: In trespassing and lying against the Lord, and wee have departed away from our God, and have spoken of crueltie and rebellion, conceiving and uttering out of the heart false matters.
59.14: Therefore iudgement is turned backewarde, and justice standeth far off: for trueth is fallen in the street, and equitie cannot enter.
59.15: Yea, trueth faileth, and hee that refraineth from evil, maketh himself a pray: and when the Lord saw it, it displeased him, that there was no iudgement.
59.16: And when he saw that there was no man, hee wondered that none would offer him self. Therefore his arm did save it, and his righteousnes it self did sustain it.
59.17: For he put on righteousnes, as an habergeon, and an helmet of salvation upon his head, and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke.
59.18: As to make recompence, as to requite the furie of the adversaries with a recompence to his enemies: he will fully repair the ylands.
59.19: So shall they fear the Name of the Lord from the West, and his glory from the rising of the sunne: for the enemie shall come like a flood: but the Spirit of the Lord shall chase him away.
59.20: And the Redeemer shall come unto Zion, and unto them that turn from iniquitie in Iaakob, saith the Lord.
59.21: And I will make this my covenant with them, saith the Lord. My Spirit that is upon thee, and my wordes, which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of the seed of thy seed, saith the Lord, from hencefoorth even for ever.

60.1: Arise, O Jerusalem: be bright, for thy light is come, and the glorie of the Lord is risen upon thee.
60.2: For behold, darkenesse shall cover the earth, and gross darkenesse the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
60.3: And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and Kings at the brightness of thy rising up.
60.4: Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these are gathered, and come to thee: thy sonnes shall come from far, and thy daughters shalbe nourished at thy side.
60.5: Then thou shalt see and shine: thine heart shall be astonied and enlarged, because the multitude of the sea shalbe converted unto thee, and the riches of the Gentiles shall come unto thee.
60.6: The multitude of camels shall cover thee: and the dromedaries of Midian and of Ephah: all they of Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense, and shew foorth the prayses of the Lord.
60.7: All the sheep of Kedar shall be gathered unto thee: the rammes of Nebaioth shall serve thee: they shall come up to bee accepted upon mine altar: and I will beautifie the house of my glorie.
60.8: Who are these that flee like a cloud, and as the doves to their windowes?
60.9: Surely the yles shall wait for mee, and the shippes of Tarshish, as at the beginning, that they may bring thy sonnes from far, and their silver, and their gold with them, unto the Name of the Lord thy God, and to the Holy one of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.
60.10: And the sonnes of strangers shall build up thy walles, and their Kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my mercie I had compassion on thee.
60.11: Therefore thy gates shalbe open continually: neither day nor night shall they be shutte, that men may bring unto thee the riches of the Gentiles, and that their Kings may be brought.
60.12: For the nation and the kingdom, that will not serve thee, shall perish: and those nations shalbe utterly destroyed.
60.13: The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fire tree, the elme and the box tree together, to beautifie the place of my Sanctuarie: for I will glorifie the place of my feet.
60.14: The sonnes also of them that afflicted thee, shall come and bow unto thee: and all they that despised thee, shall fall down at the soles of thy feet: and they shall call thee, The citie of the Lord, Zion of the Holy one of Israel.
60.15: Where as thou hast been forsaken and hated: so that no man went by thee, I will make thee an eternal glorie, and a ioye from generation to generation.
60.16: Thou shalt also suck ye milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breastes of Kings: and thou shalt know, that I the Lord am thy Sauiour, and thy Redeemer, the mightie one of Iaakob.
60.17: For brass will I bring gold, and for yron will I bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones yron. I will also make thy gouernement peace, and thine exactours righteousness.
60.18: Violence shall no more be heard of in thy land, neither desolation, nor destruction within thy borders: but thou shalt call salvation, thy walles, and praise, thy gates.
60.19: Thou shalt have no more sunne to shine by day, neither shall the brightness of the moon shine unto thee: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and thy God, thy glorie.
60.20: Thy sunne shall never goe down, neither shall thy moon be hid: for the Lord shalbe thine everlasting light, and the dayes of thy sorowe shalbe ended.
60.21: Thy people also shalbe all righteous: they shall possess the land for ever, the grass of my planting shalbe the work of mine handes, that I may be glorified.
60.22: A litle one shall become as a thousand, and a small one as a strong nation: I the Lord wil hasten it in due time.

61.1: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon mee, therefore hath the Lord anoynted mee: hee hath sent mee to preach good tidings unto the poor, to bind up the broken hearted, to preach libertie to the captives, and to them that are bound, the opening of the prison,
61.2: To preach the acceptable yeere of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all that mourn,
61.3: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, and to give unto them beautie for ashes, the oyle of ioye for mourning, the garment of gladness for the spirit of heaviness, that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that he might be glorified.
61.4: And they shall build the old waste places, and raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the cities that were desolate and waste through many generations.
61.5: And the strangers shall stand and feed your sheep, and the sonnes of the strangers shall be your plowmen and dressers of your vines.
61.6: But ye shall be named the Priestes of the Lord, and men shall say unto you, The ministers of our God, Ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and shalbe exalted with their glorie.
61.7: For your shame you shall receive double, and for confusion they shall reioyce in their portion: for in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.
61.8: For I the Lord love iudgement and hate robberie for burnt offering, and I wil direct their work in trueth, and will make an everlasting covenant with them.
61.9: And their seed shall be knowen among the Gentiles, and their buddes among the people. All that see them, shall know them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.
61.10: I will greatly reioyce in the Lord, and my soul shall be ioyfull in my God: for he hath clothed mee with the garments of salvation, and covered me with the robe of righteousnes: hee hath decked me like a bridegrome, and as a bride tireth herself with her jewels.
61.11: For as the earth bringeth foorth her bud, and as the garden causeth to grow that which is sowen in it: so the Lord God will cause righteousness to grow and praise before all the heathen.

62.1: For Zions sake I will not hold my tongue, and for Ierusalems sake I wil not rest, until the righteousnes thereof break foorth as the light, and salvation thereof as a burning lamp.
62.2: And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all Kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.
62.3: Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.
62.4: It shall no more be sayd unto thee, Forsaken, neither shall it be said any more to thy land, Desolate, but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the Lord deliteth in thee, and thy land shall have an husband.
62.5: For as a yong man marieth a virgin, so shall thy sonnes marry thee: and as a bridegrome is glad of the bride, so shall thy God reioyce over thee.
62.6: I have set watchmen upon thy walles, O Jerusalem, which all the day and all the night continually shall not cease: ye that are mindful of the Lord, keep not silence,
62.7: And give him no rest, till hee repair and until hee set up Jerusalem the prayse of the world.
62.8: The Lord hath sworn by his right hand and by his strong arm, Surely I wil no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies, and surely the sonnes of the strangers shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured.
62.9: But they that have gathered it, shall eat it, and prayse the Lord, and the gatherers thereof shall drink it in the courtes of my Sanctuarie.
62.10: Go through, go through the gates: prepare you the way for the people: cast up, cast up the way, and gather out the stones and set up a standart for the people.
62.11: Behold, the Lord hath proclaimed unto the endes of the world: tell the daughter Zion, Behold, thy Sauiour cometh: behold, his wages is with him, and his work is before him.
62.12: And they shall call them, The holy people, the redeemed of the Lord, and thou shalt be named, A citie sought out and not forsaken.

63.1: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with red garments from Bozrah? hee is glorious in his apparel and walketh in his great strength: I speak in righteousness, and am mightie to save.
63.2: Wherefore is thine apparel red, and thy garments like him that treadeth in ye wine press?
63.3: I have troden the wine press alone, and of all people there was none with mee: for I will tread them in mine anger, and tread them under foot in my wrath, and their blood shalbe sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.
63.4: For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the yeere of my redeemed is come.
63.5: And I looked, and there was none to help, and I wondered that there was none to vpholde: therefore mine own arm helped me, and my wrath it self sustained me.
63.6: Therefore I wil tread down the people in my wrath, and make them drunken in mine indignation, and wil bring down their strength to the earth.
63.7: I wil remember the mercies of the Lord and the prayses of the Lord according unto all that the Lord hath given us, and for the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which hee hath given them according to his tender love, and according to his great mercies.
63.8: For he said, Surely they are my people, children that wil not lie: so he was their Sauiour.
63.9: In all their troubles he was troubled, and the Angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his mercie he redeemed them, and he bare them and caried them alwayes continually.
63.10: But they rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore was hee turned to be their enemie and he fought against them.
63.11: Then he remembred the old time of Moses and his people, saying, Where is hee that brought them up out of the Sea with the shepheard of his sheep? where is he that put his holy Spirit within him?
63.12: He led them by the right hand of Moses with his own glorious arm, deuiding the water before them, to make himself an everlasting Name.
63.13: Hee led them through the deep, as an horse in the wilderness, that they should not stumble,
63.14: As the beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the Lord gave them rest: so diddest thou lead thy people, to make thy self a glorious Name.
63.15: Look down from heaven, and behold from the dwelling place of thine holines, and of thy glory. Where is thy zeal and thy strength, the multitude of thy mercies, and of thy compassions? they are restrained from me.
63.16: Doutles thou art our Father: though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel know us not, yet thou, O Lord, art our Father, and our redeemer: thy Name is for ever.
63.17: O Lord, why hast thou made us to ere from thy wayes? and hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants sake, and for the tribes of thine inheritance.
63.18: The people of thine holiness have possessed it, but a litle while: for our adversaries have troden down thy Sanctuarie.
63.19: We have been as they, over whom thou never barest rule, and upon whom thy Name was not called.

64.1: Oh, that thou wouldest break the heavens, and come down, and that the mountaines might melt at thy presence!
64.2: As the melting fire burned, as the fire caused the waters to boyle, (that thou mightest declare thy Name to thy adversaries) the people did tremble at thy presence.
64.3: When thou diddest terrible things, which we looked not for, thou camest down, and the mountaines melted at thy presence.
64.4: For since the beginning of the world they have not heard nor vnderstande with the ear, neither hath ye eye seen another God beside thee, which doeth so to him that waiteth for him.
64.5: Thou diddest meet him, that reioyced in thee, and did justly: they remembred thee in thy wayes: behold, thou art angrie, for we have sinned: yet in them is continuance, and we shall be saved.
64.6: But we have all been as an vncleane thing, and all our righteousnes is as filthie cloutes, and we all doe fade like a leaf, and our iniquities like the wind have taken us away.
64.7: And there is none that calleth upon thy Name, neither that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee: for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us because of our iniquities.
64.8: But now, O Lord, thou art our Father: we are the clay, and thou art our potter, and we all are the work of thine hands.
64.9: Be not angry, O Lord, above measure, neither remember iniquitie for ever: lo, we beseech thee behold, we are all thy people.
64.10: Thine holy cities lye waste: Zion is a wildernes, and Jerusalem a desart.
64.11: The House of our Sanctuarie and of our glorie, where our fathers praysed thee, is burnt up with fire and all our pleasant things are wasted.
64.12: Wilt thou hold thy self still at these things, O Lord? wilt thou hold thy peace and afflict us above measure?

65.1: I have been sought of them that asked not: I was found of them that sought me not: I sayd, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that called not upon my Name.
65.2: I have spred out mine handes all the day unto a rebellious people, which walked in a way that was not good, even after their own imaginations:
65.3: A people that provoked me ever unto my face: that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon brickes.
65.4: Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the desarts, which eat swines flesh, and the broth of things polluted are in their vessels.
65.5: Which say, Stand apart, come not neere to me: for I am holier then thou: these are a smoke in my wrath and a fire that burneth all the day.
65.6: Behold, it is written before me: I wil not keep silence, but will render it and recompense it into their bosom.
65.7: Your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers shalbe together (sayth the Lord) which have burnt incense upon the mountaines, and blasphemed me upon the hilles: therefore wil I measure their old work into their bosom.
65.8: Thus sayth the Lord, As the wine is found in the cluster, and one sayth, Destroy it not, for a blessing is in it, so will I doe for my servants sakes, that I may not destroy them whole.
65.9: But I will bring a seed out of Iaakob, and out of Judah, that shall inherit my mountain: and mine elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there.
65.10: And Sharon shalbe a sheepefolde, and the valley of Achor shalbe a resting place for the cattell of my people, that have sought me.
65.11: But ye are they that have forsaken the Lord and forgotten mine holy Mountain, and have prepared a table for the multitude, and furnish the drink offerings unto the number.
65.12: Therefore wil I number you to the sword, and all you shall bow down to the slaughter, because I called, and ye did not answer: I spake, and ye heard not, but did evil in my sight, and did chuse that thing which I would not.
65.13: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, my servants shall eat, and ye shalbe hungrie: behold, my servants shall drink, and ye shall be thirstie: behold, my servants shall reioyce, and ye shalbe ashamed.
65.14: Behold, my servants shall sing for ioye of heart, and ye shall cry for sorow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of mind.
65.15: And ye shall leave your name as a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord God shall slay you and call his servants by another name.
65.16: He that shall bless in the earth, shall bless himself in the true God, and he that sweareth in the earth, shall swear by the true God: for the former troubles are forgotten, and shall surely hide themselves from mine eyes.
65.17: For lo, I will create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembred nor come into mind.
65.18: But be you glad and reioyce for ever in the things that I shall create: for behold, I will create Jerusalem, as a reioycing and her people as a ioye,
65.19: And I wil reioyce in Jerusalem, and ioye in my people, and the voyce of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voyce of crying.
65.20: There shall be no more there a child of yeeres, nor an old man that hath not filled his dayes: for he that shall be an hundreth yeeres old, shall dye as a yong man: but the sinner being an hundreth yeeres old shall be accursed.
65.21: And they shall build houses and inhabit them, and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.
65.22: They shall not build, and another inhabit: they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the dayes of the tree are the dayes of my people, and mine elect shall inioye in old age the work of their handes.
65.23: They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth in fear: for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their buds with them.
65.24: Yea, before they call, I will answer, and whiles they speak, I will hear.
65.25: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lyon shall eat straw like the bullock: and to the serpent dust shall be his meat. They shall no more hurt nor destroy in all mine holy Mountain, saith the Lord.

66.1: Thus saith the Lord, The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footestoole: where is that house that ye will build unto me? and where is that place of my rest?
66.2: For all these things hath mine hand made, and all these things have been, sayth the Lord: and to him will I look, even to him, that is poor, and of a contrite spirit and trembleth at my wordes.
66.3: He that killeth a bullock, is as if he slew a man: he that sacrificeth a sheep, as if he cut off a dogges neck: he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swines blood: he that remembreth incense, as if he blessed an idol: yea, they have chosen their own wayes, and their soul deliteth in their abominations.
66.4: Therefore will I chuse out their delusions, and I will bring their fear upon them, because I called, and none would answer: I spake and they would not hear: but they did evil in my sight, and chose the things which I would not.
66.5: Hear the word of the Lord, all ye that tremble at his word, Your brethren that hated you, and cast you out for my Names sake, said, Let the Lord be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed.
66.6: A voyce soundeth from the citie, even a voyce from the Temple, the voyce of the Lord, that recompenseth his enemies fully.
66.7: Before she travailed, she brought foorth: and before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child.
66.8: Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? shall ye earth be brought forth in one day? or shall a nation be borne at once? for assoone as Zion travailed, she brought foorth her children.
66.9: Shall I cause to travail, and not bring forth? shall I cause to bring forth, and shall be baren, saith thy God?
66.10: Reioyce ye with Jerusalem, and be gladde with her, all ye that love her: reioyce for joy with her, all ye that mourn for her,
66.11: That ye may suck and be satisfied with the brestes of her consolation: that ye may milk out and be delited with ye brightnes of her glorie.
66.12: For thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will extend peace over her like a flood, and the glorie of the Gentiles like a flowing stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be ioyfull upon her knees.
66.13: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you, and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
66.14: And when ye see this, your hearts shall reioyce, and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the Lord shall be knowen among his servants, and his indignation against his enemies.
66.15: For behold, the Lord will come with fire, and his charets like a whirlewinde, that he may recompence his anger with wrath, and his indignation with the flame of fire.
66.16: For the Lord will judge with fire, and with his sword all flesh, and the slain of the Lord shall be many.
66.17: They that sanctifie themselves, and purifie themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the middes eating swines flesh, and such abomination, even the mouse, shall be consumed together, sayeth the Lord.
66.18: For I will visit their workes, and their imaginations: for it shall come that I will gather all nations, and tongues, and they shall come, and see my glorie.
66.19: And I will set a sign among them, and will send those that escape of them, unto the nations of Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, and to them that draw the bow, to Tubal and Tauan, yles afarre off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glorie, and they shall declare my glorie among the Gentiles.
66.20: And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations, upon horses, and in charets, and in horse litters, and upon mules, and swift beastes, to Jerusalem mine holy Mountain, saith the Lord, as the children of Israel, offer in a clean vessell in the House of the Lord.
66.21: And I will take of them for Priestes, and for Levites, saith the Lord.
66.22: For as the new heavens, and the new earth which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name continue.
66.23: And from moneth to moneth, and from Sabbath to Sabbath shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.
66.24: And they shall goe forth, and look upon the carkases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not dye, neither shall their fire be quenched, and they shalbe an abhorring unto all flesh.

23:1:1: That is, a revelation or prophecy, which was one of the two means whereby God declared himself to his servants in old time, as Num. 12:6, and therefore the Prophets were called Seers, 1 Sam. 9:9.
Isaiah was chiefly sent to Judah and Jerusalem, but not only: for in this book are prophecies concerning other nations also.
Called also Azariah, 2 Kings 15:1, of these Kings, read 2 Kings 14-21, and 2 Chron. 25-33.
23:1:2: Because men were obstinate and insensible, he calleth to the dumb creatures, which were more prompt to obey God’s word, as Deut. 32:1.
He declareth his great mercy toward the Jews forasmuch as he chose them above all other nations to be his people and children, as Deut. 10:15.
23:1:3: The most dull and brute beasts do more acknowledge their duty toward their masters, than my people do toward me, of whom they have received benefits without comparison.
23:1:4: They were not only wicked as were their fathers, but utterly corrupt, and by their evil example infected others.
That is, him that sanctifieth Israel.
23:1:5: What availeth it to seek to amend you by punishment, seeing the more I correct you, the more ye rebel?
By naming the chief parts of the body, he signifieth that there was no part of the whole body of the Jews free from his rods.
23:1:6: Every part of the body as well the least as the chiefest, was plagued.
Their plagues were so grievous, that they were incurable, and yet they would not repent.
23:1:7: Meaning, of them that dwell far off, which because they look for no advantage of that which remaineth destroy all before them.
23:1:9: Because that he will ever have a Church to call upon his Name.
23:1:10: Ye that for your vices deserved all to be destroyed, as they of Sodom, save that God of his mercy reserved a little number, Lam. 3:22.
23:1:11: Although God commanded these sacrifices for a time, as aids and exercises of their faith: yet because the people had not faith nor repentance, God detesteth them, Ps. 50:13; Jer. 6:20; Amos 5:22; Mic. 6:7.
23:1:14: Your sacrifices offered in the new moons and feasts: he condemneth hereby hypocrites, which think to please God with ceremonies, and they themselves are void of faith and mercy.
23:1:15: He showeth that where men be given to avarice, deceit, cruelty and extortion, which is meant by blood, there God will show his anger, and not accept them, though they seem never so holy, as Isa. 59:3.
23:1:16: By this outward washing, he meaneth the spiritual: exhorting the Jews to repent and amend their lives.
23:1:17: This kind of reasoning by the second Table, the Scriptures use in many places against the hypocrites, who pretend most holiness and religion in word, but when the charity and love toward their brethren should appear, they declare that they have neither faith nor religion.
23:1:18: To know if I do accuse you without cause.
Lest sinners should pretend any rigor on God’s part, he only willeth them to be pure in heart, and he will forgive all their sins, were they never so many or great.
23:1:19: He showeth that whatsoever adversity man endureth, it ought to be attributed to his own incredulity and disobedience.
23:1:21: That is, Jerusalem, which had promised fidelity unto me, as a wife to her husband.
Given to covetousness and extortion, which he signified before by blood, verse 15.
23:1:22: Whatsoever was pure in thee before, is now corrupt, though thou have an outward show.
23:1:23: That is, they maintain the wicked and the extortioners: and not only do not punish them, but are themselves such.
23:1:24: When God will show himself merciful to his Church, he calleth himself, The Holy one of Israel, but when he hath to do with his enemies, he is called Mighty, as against whom no power is able to resist.
I will take vengeance of mine adversaries the Jews, and so satisfy my desire by punishing them. Which thing yet he doeth with a grief, because of his Covenant.
23:1:25: Lest the faithful among them should be overcome with his threatening, he addeth this consolation.
23:1:26: It is only the work of God to purify the heart of man, which thing he doeth because of his promise, made concerning the salvation of his Church.
23:1:27: By justice is meant God’s faithful promise, which is the cause of the deliverance of his Church.
23:1:28: The wicked shall not be partakers of God’s promise, Ps. 92:9.
23:1:29: That is, the trees and pleasant places, where ye commit idolatry, which was forbidden, Deut. 16:22.
23:1:31: The false god, wherein ye put your confidence, shall be consumed as easily as a piece of tow.
23:2:2: In an evident place to be seen and discerned.
The decree and ordinance of God, touching the restoration of the Church, which is chiefly meant of the time of Christ.
When the kingdom of Christ shall be enlarged by the preaching of the doctrine. Here also is declared the zeal of the children of God, when they are called.
23:2:3: Meaning, the whole doctrine of salvation.
This was accomplished, when the Gospel was first preached in Jerusalem, and from thence went through all the world.
Alluding to mount Zion, where the visible Church then was.
23:2:4: He speaketh not against the use of weapons and lawful war, but showeth how the hearts of the godly shall be affected one toward another: Which peace and love doth begin and grow in this life, but shall be perfected when we are joined with our Head Christ Jesus.
The Lord, which is Christ, shall have all power given him.
That they may acknowledge their sins, and turn to him.
He showeth the fruit of the peace, which the Gospel should bring: to wit, that men should do good one to another, whereas before they were enemies.
23:2:5: Seeing the Gentiles will be so ready, make you haste, and show them the way to worship God.
23:2:6: They altogether gave themselves to the fashions of other nations.
The Prophet seeing the small hope that the Jews would convert, complaineth to God, as though he had utterly forsaken them for their sins.
Full of the corruptions that reigned chiefly in the East parts.
23:2:7: The Prophet first condemned their superstition and idolatry: next their covetousness, and thirdly their vain trust in worldly means.
23:2:9: He noteth the nature of the idolaters, which are never satisfied in their superstitions.
Thus the Prophet spake, being inflamed with the zeal of God’s glory, and that he might fear them with God’s judgment.
23:2:11: Meaning, as soon as God shall begin to execute his judgments.
23:2:14: By high trees and mountains are meant them that are proud and lofty, and think themselves most strong in this world.
23:2:16: He condemneth their vain confidence, which they had in strongholds, and in their rich merchandise, which brought in vain pleasures, wherewith men’s minds became effeminate.
23:2:20: They shall cast them into most vile and filthy places, when they perceive that they are not able to help them.
23:2:22: Cast off your vain confidence of man, whose life is so frail, that if his nose be stopped, he is dead, and consider that you have to do with God.
23:3:1: Because they trusted in their abundance and prosperity, he showeth that they should be taken from them.
23:3:2: The temporal governor and the minister.
23:3:3: By these he meaneth that God would take away everything that was in any estimation, and wherein they had any occasion to vaunt themselves.
23:3:4: Not only in age: but in wit, manners, knowledge and strength.
23:3:5: For lack of good regiment and order.
23:3:6: He showeth that this plague shall be so horrible, that contrary to the common manner of men, which by nature are ambitious, none shall be found able or willing to be their governor.
23:3:7: Fear shall rather cause him to forswear himself, than to take such a dangerous charge upon him.
23:3:9: When God shall examine their deeds whereupon they now set an impudent face, he shall find the mark of their impiety in their forehead.
23:3:10: Be ye that are godly, assured that God will defend you in the midst of these troubles.
23:3:12: Because the wicked people were more addicted to their princes, than to the commandments of God, he showeth that he would give them such princes, by whom they should have no help, but that should be manifest tokens of his wrath, because they should be fools and effeminate.
23:3:14: Meaning, that the rulers and governors had destroyed his Church, and not preserved it, according to their duty.
23:3:15: That is, ye show all cruelty against them.
23:3:16: They delighted then in slippers that did creak, or had little plates sewed upon them, which tinkled as they went.
He meaneth the people because of the arrogancy and pride of their women, which gave themselves to all wantonness and dissolution.
As a sign, that they were not chaste.
23:3:23: In rehearsing all these things particularly, he showeth the lightness and vanity of such as cannot be content with comely apparel according to their degree.
23:3:25: Meaning, that God will not only punish the women, but their husbands which have suffered this dissoluteness, and also the commonweal, which hath not remedied it.
23:4:1: When God shall execute this vengeance, there shall not be one man found to be the head to many women, and they contrary to womanly shamefacedness, shall seek unto men, and offer themselves to any condition.
Be thou our husband, and let us be called thy wives.
For so they thought it to be without an head and husband.
23:4:2: He comforteth the Church in this desolation, which shall spring up like a bud, signifying that God’s graces should be as plentiful toward the faithful, as though they sprang out of the earth, as Isa. 45:8. Some by the bud of the Lord mean Christ.
23:4:3: He alludeth to the book of life, whereof read Exod. 32:32, meaning, God’s secret counsel, wherein his elect are predestinate to life everlasting.
23:4:4: That is, the cruelty, extortion, avarice, and all wickedness.
When things shall be redressed that were amiss.
23:4:5: He alludeth to the pillar of the cloud, Exod. 13:21, meaning, that God’s favor and protection should appear in every place.
The faithful are called the glory of God, because his image and tokens of his grace shine in them.
23:4:6: God promiseth to be the defense of his Church against all troubles and dangers.
23:5:1: The Prophet by this song doth set before the people’s eyes their ingratitude, and God’s mercy.
Meaning, that he had planted his Church in a place most plentiful and abundant.
23:5:2: In the seventh verse he declareth what they were.
He spared no diligence nor cost.
23:5:3: He maketh them judges in their own cause, forasmuch as it was evident that they were the cause of their own ruin.
23:5:5: I will take no more care for it: meaning, that he would take from them his word and ministers, and all other comforts, and send them contrary plagues.
23:5:7: Judgment and righteousness are true fruits of the fear of God, and therefore in the cruel oppression there is no religion.
23:5:8: To wit, for the poor to dwell in.
23:5:9: I have heard the complaint and cry of the poor.
23:5:10: Which containeth about ten pottels: so that every acre should but yield one pottel.
An Ephah containeth ten pottels and is in dry things as much as Bath is in liquors.
23:5:11: That spare no pain nor diligence to follow their lusts.
Which are never weary of their rioting and excessive pleasures, but use all means to provoke to the same.
23:5:12: They regard not the provident care of God over them, nor for what end he hath created them.
23:5:13: That is, shall certainly go: for so the Prophets use to speak, as though the thing which shall come to pass, were done already.
Because they would not obey the word of God.
23:5:14: Meaning, the grave shall swallow up them that shall die for hunger and thirst, and yet for all this great destruction it shall ever be satiate.
23:5:17: God comforteth the poor lambs of his Church, which had been strangers in other countries, promising that they should dwell in these places again, whereof they had been deprived by the fat and cruel tyrants.
23:5:18: Which use all allurements, occasions, and excuses to harden their conscience in sin.
23:5:19: He showeth what are the words of the wicked, when they are menaced with God’s judgments, 2 Pet. 3:4.
23:5:20: Which are not ashamed of sin, nor care for honesty, but are grown to a desperate impiety.
23:5:21: Which are contemners of all doctrine and admonition.
23:5:22: Which are never weary, but show their strength, and brag in gluttony and drunkenness.
23:5:24: Both they and their posterity, so that nothing shall be left.
23:5:25: He showeth that God had so sore punished this people, that the dumb creatures, if they had been so plagued, would have been more sensible, and therefore his plagues must continue, till they begin to feel them.
23:5:26: He will make the Babylonians to come against them at his beck, and to fight under his standard.
23:5:27: They shall be prompt and lusty to execute God’s vengeance.
The enemy shall have none impediment.
23:5:29: Whereby is declared the cruelty of the enemy.
23:5:30: The Jews shall find no succor.
23:6:1: Of his garment, or of his throne.
God showeth not himself to man in his majesty, but according as man’s capacity is able to comprehend him, that is, by visible signs, as John Baptist saw the holy Ghost in the form of a dove.
As a Judge ready to give sentence.
23:6:2: Whereby was declared that man was not able to see the brightness of God in them.
They were Angels, so called, because they were of a fiery color, to signify that they burnt in the love of God, or were light as fire to execute his will.
Signifying, that they were not able to endure the brightness of God’s glory.
Which thing declareth the prompt obedience of the Angels to execute God’s commandment.
23:6:3: His glory doth not only appear in the heavens, but through all the world, and therefore all creatures are bound, to praise him.
This oft repetition signifieth, that the Holy Angels cannot satisfy themselves in praising God, to teach us that in all our lives we should give ourselves to the continual praise of God.
23:6:4: Which things were to confirm the Prophet, that it was not the voice of man: and by the smoke was signified the blindness that should come upon the Jews.
23:6:5: He speaketh this for two causes: the one because he that was a mortal creature, and therefore had more need to glorify God than the Angels, did it not: and the other because the more near that man approacheth to God, the more doth he know his own sin and corruption.
23:6:6: Of the burnt offerings, where the fire never went out.
23:6:7: This declareth that man cannot render due obedience to God, till he have purged us.
23:6:9: Whereby is declared that for the malice of man God will not immediately take away his word, but he will cause it to be preached to their condemnation, when as they will not learn thereby to obey his will, and be saved: hereby he exhorteth the ministers to do their duty, and answereth to the wicked murmurers, that through their own malice their heart is hardened, Matt. 13:14; Acts 28:26; Rom. 11:8.
23:6:11: As he was moved with the zeal of God’s glory, so was he touched with a charitable affection toward the people.
23:6:13: Meaning, the tenth part: or as some write, it was revealed to Isaiah for the confirmation of his prophecy, that ten Kings should come before their captivity, as were from Uzziah to Zedekiah.
For the fewness they shall seem to be eaten up: yet they shall after flourish as a tree, which in winter loseth leaves, and seemeth to be dead, yet in Summer is fresh and green.
23:7:1: To wit, the second time: for in the first battle Ahaz was overcome.
23:7:2: That is, Israel, because that tribe was the greatest, Gen. 48:19.
23:7:3: That is to say, the rest shall return, which name Isaiah gave his son, to signify that the rest of the people should return out of their captivity.
23:7:4: Which have but a little smoke and shall quickly be quenched.
23:7:6: Which was an Israelite, and as seemeth, enemy to the house of David.
23:7:8: Counting from the five and twentieth year of the reign of Uzziah, at what time Amos prophesied this thing, and now Isaiah confirmeth that the Israelites should be led into perpetual captivity, which thing came to pass within 20 years after that Isaiah did this message.
23:7:11: For the confirmation of this thing that thine enemies shall be destroyed and thou preserved.
23:7:12: Not to believe God’s word without a sign, is to tempt God, but to refuse a sign when God offereth it for the aid and help of our infirmity, is to rebel against him.
23:7:13: You think you have to do with men, when ye contemn God’s messengers: but it is God against whom you bend yourselves.
23:7:14: Forasmuch as thou art unworthy, the Lord for his own promise sake will give a sign, which shall be that Christ the Savior of his Church, and the effect of all signs and miracles shall be revealed.
Or, God with us, which name can agree to none, but to him that is both God and man.
23:7:15: Meaning, that Christ is not only God, but man also, because he shall be nourished as other men until the age of discretion.
23:7:16: Not meaning Christ, but any child: for before a child can come to the years of discretion, the kings of Samaria and Syria shall be destroyed.
23:7:17: Since the time that the twelve Tribes rebelled under Rehoboam.
In whom thou hast put thy trust.
23:7:18: Meaning, the Egyptians: for by reason the country is hot and moist, it is full of flies, as Assyria is full of bees.
23:7:19: Signifying, that no place shall be free from them.
23:7:20: That is, that which is from the belly downward: meaning, that he would destroy both great and small.
23:7:21: He that before had a great number of cattle, shall be content with one cow and two sheep.
23:7:22: The number of men shall be so small, that a few beasts shall be able to nourish all abundantly.
23:7:24: As they that go to seek wild beasts among the bushes.
23:7:25: The mountains contrary to their wont, shall be tilled by such as shall flee to them for succor.
23:8:1: Meaning, after the common fashion, because all men might read it.
That thou mayest write in great letters, to the intent it may be more easily read.
23:8:2: Because the thing was of great importance, he took these two witnesses, which were of credit with the people, when he set this up upon the door of the Temple, albeit Uriah was a flattering hypocrite, 2 Kings 16:11.
23:8:3: Meaning, to his wife, and this was done in a vision.
Or, make speed to the spoil: haste to the prey.
23:8:4: That is, the army of Assyria.
Before any child be able to speak.
23:8:6: Which was a fountain at the foot of mount Zion, out of the which ran a small river through the city: meaning, that they of Judah, distrusting their own power, which was small, desired such power and riches as they saw in Syria and Israel.
23:8:7: That is, the Assyrians which dwell beyond Euphrates.
23:8:8: He speaketh this to Messiah, or Christ, in whom the faithful were comforted, and who would not suffer his Church to be destroyed utterly.
It shall be ready to drown them.
23:8:9: To wit, ye that are enemies to the Church, as the Assyrians, Egyptians, Syrians, etc.
23:8:11: To encourage me that I should not shrink for the infidelity of this people, and so neglect mine office.
23:8:12: Consent not ye that are godly, to the league and friendship that this people seek with strangers and idolaters.
Meaning, that they should not fear the thing that they feared, which have no hope in God.
23:8:13: In putting your trust only in him, in calling upon him in adversity, patiently looking for his help, and fearing to do anything contrary to his will.
23:8:14: He will defend you which are his elect, and reject all the rest, which is meant of Christ, against whom the Jews should stumble and fall, Luke 2:34; Rom. 9:33; 1 Pet. 2:7, 8.
23:8:16: Though all forsake me, yet ye that are mine, keep my word sure sealed in your hearts.
23:8:18: Meaning, them that were willing to hear and obey the word of God, whom the world hated, as though they were monsters and not worthy to live.
This was a consolation in their troubles, knowing that nothing could come unto them, but by the will of the Lord.
23:8:19: Answer the wicked thus, Should not God’s people seek succor only at him?
This is, will they refuse to be taught of the Prophet, who is the mouth of God, and seek help at the dead, which is the illusion of Satan?
23:8:20: Seek remedy in the word of God, where his will is declared.
They have no knowledge, but are blind leaders of the blind.
23:8:21: In whom afore they put their trust.
That is, in Judah, where they should have had rest, if they had not thus grievously offended God.
23:8:22: They shall think that heaven and earth and all creatures are bent against them to trouble them.
23:9:1: Wherewith Israel was punished, first by Tiglath-pilesar, which was a light scourge in respect of that which they suffered afterward by Shalmaneser, who carried the Israelites away captives.
He comforteth the Church again after these great threatenings, promising to restore them to great glory in Messiah.
Whereas the Jews and Gentiles dwelt together by reason of those twenty cites, which Solomon gave to Hiram.
23:9:2: Meaning, the comfort of their deliverance.
Which were captivity in Babylon: and the Prophet speaketh of that thing which should come to pass threescore years after, as though it were now done.
This captivity and deliverance were figures of our captivity by sin, and of our deliverance by Christ through the preaching of the Gospel, Matt. 4:15, 16.
23:9:3: Their number was greater when they went into captivity, than when they returned, but their joy was greater at their return, Hag. 2:9.
23:9:4: Thou gavest them perfect joy by delivering them, and by destroying the tyrants, that had kept them in cruel bondage, as thou didst deliver them by Gideon from the Midianites, Judg. 7:21.
23:9:5: He speaketh of the deliverance of his Church, which he hath delivered miraculously from his enemies, but especially by the coming of Christ, of whom he prophesieth in the next verse.
23:9:6: The author of eternity, and by whom the Church and every member thereof shall be preserved forever, and have immortal life.
23:9:7: His singular love and care for his elect.
23:9:8: This is another prophecy against them of Samaria, which were mockers and contemners of God’s promises and menaces.
23:9:10: We were but weak, when the enemy overcame us, but we will make ourselves so strong, that we will neither care for our enemies, nor fear God’s threatenings.
23:9:11: Rezin king of Syria, who was in league with Israel, was slain by the Assyrians, after whose death Aram, that is, the Syrians were against Israel, which on the other side were assailed by the Philistines.
23:9:18: Wickedness as a bellows kindleth the fire of God’s wrath, which consumeth all his obstinate enemies.
23:9:19: Though there were no foreign enemy, yet they shall destroy one another.
23:9:20: Their greediness shall be insatiable, so that one brother shall eat up another, as though he should eat his own flesh.
23:10:1: Which write and pronounce a wicked sentence to oppress the poor: meaning, that the wicked magistrates, which were the chief cause of mischief, should be first punished.
23:10:3: Your riches and authority, that they may be safe, and that ye may receive them again.
23:10:4: Because they have forsaken me, some shall go into captivity, and the rest shall be slain.
23:10:5: God calleth for the Assyrians to be the executioners of his vengeance.
23:10:6: That is, the Assyrians against the Jews, which are but hypocrites: and in the sixth and seventh verse is declared the difference of the work of God, and of the wicked in one very thing and act: for God’s intention is to chastise them for their amendment, and the Assyrians’ purpose is to destroy them to enrich themselves: thus in respect of God’s justice, it is God’s work, but in respect of their own malice, it is the work of the devil.
23:10:9: Seeing that I have overcome as well one city as another, so that none could resist, shall Jerusalem be able to escape mine hands?
23:10:12: When he hath sufficiently chastised his people (for he beginneth at his own house) then will he burn the rods.
23:10:15: Here we see that no creature is able to do anything, but as God appointeth him, and that they are all but his instruments to do his work, though the intentions be divers, as verse 6.
23:10:17: Meaning, that God is a light to comfort his people, and a fire to burn his enemies.
23:10:18: To wit, body and soul utterly.
When the battle is lost and the standard taken.
23:10:20: This is the end of God’s plagues toward his, to bring them to him, and to forsake all trust in others.
23:10:22: This small number which seemed to be consumed, and yet according to God’s decree is saved, shall be sufficient to fill all the world with righteousness.
23:10:23: God will destroy this land as he hath determined, and after save a small portion.
23:10:24: As the Egyptians did punish thee.
23:10:26: When the Israelites passed through by the lifting up of Moses’ rod, and the enemies were drowned, Exod. 14:28.
23:10:27: Because of the promise made to that kingdom, whereby Christ’s kingdom was prefigured.
23:10:28: He describeth by what way the Assyrians should come against Jerusalem, to confirm the faithful, when it should come to pass, that as their plague was come, so should they be delivered.
23:10:33: Fear and destruction shall come upon Judah for the princes and the people shall be all led away captives.
23:11:1: Because the captivity of Babylon was a figure of the spiritual captivity under sin, he showeth that our true deliverance must come by Christ: for as David came out of Jesse a man without dignity, so Christ should come of a poor carpenter’s house as out of a dead stock, Isa. 53:2.
23:11:4: All these properties can agree to none, but only unto Christ: for it is he that toucheth the hearts of the faithful, and mortifieth their concupiscences: and to the wicked he is the savor of death, and to them that shall perish: so that all the world shall be smitten with his rod, which is his word.
23:11:6: Men because of their wicked affections are named by the names of beasts, wherein the like affections reign: but Christ by his Spirit shall reform them, and work in them such mutual charity, that they shall be like lambs, favoring and loving one another, and cast off all their cruel affections, Isa. 65:25.
23:11:9: It shall be in as great abundance as the waters in the sea.
23:11:10: That is, the Church, which he also calleth his rest, Ps. 132:14.
He prophesieth of the calling of the Gentiles.
23:11:11: For God first delivered his people out of Egypt, and now promiseth to deliver them out of their enemies’ hands as from the Parthians, Persians, Chaldeans, and them of Antiochia, among whom they were dispersed: and this is chiefly meant of Christ, who calleth his people being dispersed through all the world.
23:11:13: Here he describeth the consent that shall be in his Church, and their victory against their enemies.
23:11:15: Meaning, a corner of the sea, that entereth into the land, and hath the form of a tongue.
To wit, Nile, the great river of Egypt, which entereth into the sea with seven streams.
23:12:1: He showeth how the Church shall praise God, when they are delivered from their captivity.
23:12:2: Our salvation standeth only in God, who giveth us an assured confidence, constancy, and occasion, to praise him for the same.
23:12:3: The graces of God shall be so abundant, that ye may receive them in as great plenty, as waters out of a fountain that is full.
23:12:6: Ye that are of the Church.
23:13:1: That is, the great calamity, which was prophesied to come on Babel, as a most grievous burden, which they were not able to bear. In these twelve chapters following, he speaketh of the plagues wherewith God would smite the strange nations (whom they knew) to declare that God chastised the Israelites as his children, and these others as his enemies: and also if that God spare not these that are ignorant, that they must not think strange, if he punish them which have knowledge of his Law, and keep it not.
23:13:2: To wit, the Medes and Persians.
23:13:3: That is, prepared and appointed to execute my judgments.
Which willingly go about to the work whereunto I appoint them, but how the wicked do this, read Isa. 10:6.
23:13:5: The army of the Medes and the Persians against Babylon.
23:13:8: The Babylonians’ anger and grief shall be so much, that their faces shall burn as fire.
23:13:10: They that are overcome shall think that all the powers of heaven and earth are against them, Ezek. 32:7; Joel 3:15; Matt. 24:29.
23:13:11: He compareth Babylon to the whole world, because they so esteemed themselves by reason of their great empire.
He noteth the principal vice, whereunto they are most given, as are all that abound in wealth.
23:13:12: He noteth the great slaughter that shall be, seeing the enemy shall neither for gold, or silver spare a man’s life, as verse 17.
23:13:14: Meaning, the power of Babylon with their hired soldiers.
23:13:16: This was not accomplished when Cyrus took Babylon, but after the death of Alexander the great.
23:13:20: Who useth to go from country to country to find pasture for their beasts, but there shall they find none.
23:13:21: Which were either wild beasts, or fowls, or wicked spirits, whereby Satan deluded man, as by the fairies, goblins, and such like fantasies.
23:14:1: Meaning, that the Gentiles shalt be joined with the Church, and worship God.
He showeth why God will haste to destroy his enemies, to wit, because he will deliver his Church.
23:14:2: Signifying, that the Jews should be superiors to the Gentiles, and that they should be brought under the service of Christ by the preaching of the Apostles, whereby all are brought to the subjection of Christ, 2 Cor. 10:5.

23:15:1: The chief city, whereby the whole country was meant.

For as in the west parts the people used to let their hair grow long, when they mourned, so in the East part they cut it off.

Meaning, that it was a city that ever lived in pleasure, and never felt sorrow.
23:15:7: To hide themselves, and their goods there.
23:15:9: So that by no means they should escape the hand of God: thus will God punish the enemies of his Church.
23:16:1: That is, offer a sacrifice, whereby he derideth their long delay, which would not repent when the Lord called them, showing them that it is now too late, seeing the vengeance of God is upon them.

That is, the Assyrians and other enemies.

He showeth that their plague was so great, that it would have moved any man to lament with them, as Ps. 141:5.
23:16:12: They shall use all means to seek help of their idols, and all in vain: for Chemosh their great god shall not be able to help them.
23:16:14: Who will observe justly the time for the which he is hired, and serve no longer, but will ever long for it.
He appointed a certain time to punish the enemies in.

It seemeth that the Prophet would comfort the Church in declaring the destruction of these two kings of Syria and Israel, when as they had conspired the overthrow of Judah.
23:17:4: Meaning, of the ten tribes, which boasted themselves of their nobility, prosperity, strength and multitude.

23:17:13: He addeth this for the consolation of the faithful which were in Israel.
23:17:14: He compareth the enemies the Assyrians to a tempest, which riseth overnight, and in the morning is gone.

23:18:3: When the Lord prepared to fight against the Ethiopians.

23:18:6: Not only men shall contemn them, but the brute beasts.
23:18:7: Meaning, that God will pity his Church, and receive that little remnant as an offering unto himself.
23:19:1: Because the Egyptians trusted in the defense of their country, in the multitude of their idols, and in the valiantness of their men, the Lord showeth that he will come over all their munitions in a swift cloud, and that their idols shall tremble at his coming and that men’s hearts shall faint.

23:19:21: By these ceremonies he comprehendeth the spiritual service under Christ.
