They seek shifts to cloak their doings, and not godly means.
23:30:4: The chief of Israel went into Egypt in embassy to seek help, and abode at these cities.
23:30:6: That is, a heavy sentence or prophecy against the beasts that carried their treasures into Egypt, by the wilderness, which was south from Judah, signifying that if the beasts should not be spared, the men should be punished much more grievously.
23:30:7: And not to come to and fro to seek help.
23:30:8: That it may be a witness against them for all posterity.
23:30:9: He showeth what was the cause of their destruction, and bringeth also all misery to man: to wit, because they would not hear the word of God, but delighted to be flattered, and led in error.
23:30:10: Threaten us not by the word of God, neither be so rigorous, nor talk unto us in the Name of the Lord, as Jer. 11:21.
23:30:12: Meaning, in their stubbornness against God and the admonitions of his Prophets.
23:30:14: Signifying, that the destruction of the wicked shall be without recovery.
23:30:15: Ofttimes by his Prophets he put you in remembrance of this, that you should only depend on him.
23:30:16: We will trust to escape by our horses.
23:30:17: Whereas all the trees are cut down save two or three to make masts.
23:30:18: Not only in punishing, but in using moderation in the same, as Jer. 10:24 and 30:11.
He commendeth the great mercies of God, who with patience waiteth to call sinners to repentance.
23:30:21: God shall direct all thy ways, and appoint thee how to go either hither or thither.
23:30:22: Showing, that there can be no true repentance, except both in heart and deed we show ourselves enemies to idolatry.
Ye shall cast away your idols, which you have made of gold, and silver, with all that belongeth unto them, as a most filthy thing, and polluted.
23:30:25: By these divers manners of speech he showeth that the felicity of the Church shall be so great, that none is able sufficiently to express it.
23:30:26: When the Church shall be restored, the glory thereof shall pass seven times the brightness of the Sun: for by the Sun and Moon, which are two excellent creatures, he showeth what shall be the glory of the children of God in the kingdom of Christ.
23:30:27: This threatening is against the Assyrians the chief enemies of the people of God.
23:30:28: To drive thee to nothing: and thus God consumeth the wicked by that means, whereby he cleanseth his.
23:30:29: Ye shall rejoice at the destruction of your enemies, as they that sung for joy of the solemn feast, which began in the evening.
23:30:32: Against Babel: meaning the Assyrians and Babylonians.
With joy and assurance of the victory.
23:30:33: By these figurative speeches he declareth the condition of the wicked after this life.
Here it is taken for hell, where the wicked are tormented, read 2 Kings 23:10.
So that their estate or degree cannot exempt the wicked.
23:31:1: Meaning, that they forsake the Lord, that put their trust in worldly things: for they cannot trust in both.

There were two special causes, why the Israelites should not join amity with the Egyptians: first, because the Lord had commanded them never to return thither, Deut. 17:16 and 28:68, lest they should forget the benefit of their redemption: and secondly, lest they should be corrupted with the superstition and idolatry of the Egyptians, and so forsake God, Jer. 2:18.
23:31:2: And knoweth their crafty enterprises, and will bring all to naught.
23:31:3: Meaning, both the Egyptians and the Israelites.
23:31:4: He showeth the Jews, that if they would put their trust in him, he is so able, that none can resist his power: and so careful over them, as a bird over her young, which ever flieth about them for their defense: which similitude the scripture useth in divers places, as Deut. 32:11; Matt. 23:37.
23:31:6: He toucheth their conscience, that they might earnestly feel their grievous sins, and so truly repent, forasmuch as now they are almost drowned and past recovery.
23:31:7: By these fruits your repentance shall be known, as Isa. 2:20.
23:31:9: This was accomplished soon after when Sennacherib’s army was discomfited, and he fled to his castle in Nineveh for succor.
23:32:1: This prophecy is of Hezekiah, who was a figure of Christ, and therefore it ought chiefly to be referred to him.
By judgment and justice is meant an upright government, both in policy, and religion.
23:32:2: Where men are weary with traveling for lack of water.
23:32:3: He promiseth to give the true light, which is the pure doctrine of God’s word, and understanding, and zeal of the same, are contrary to the threatenings against the wicked, Isa. 6:9 and 29:10.
23:32:5: Vice shall no more be called virtue, nor virtue esteemed by power and riches.
23:32:9: He prophesieth of such calamity to come, that they will not spare the women and children, and therefore willeth them to take heed and provide.
23:32:10: Meaning, that the affliction should continue long, and when one year were past, yet they should look for new plagues.
God will take from you the means and occasions, which made you to contemn him: to wit, abundance of worldly goods.
23:32:12: By the teats he meaneth the plentiful fields, whereby men are nourished as children with the teat: or, the mothers for sorrow and heaviness shall lack milk.
23:32:15: The field which is now fruitful, shall be but as a barren forest in comparison of that it shall be then, as Isa. 29:17, which shall be fulfilled in Christ’s time, for then they that were before as the barren wilderness, being regenerate shall be fruitful, and they that had some beginning of godliness, shall bring forth fruits in such abundance, that their former life shall seem but as a wilderness where no fruits were.
That is, when the Church shall be restored: thus the Prophets, after they have denounced God’s judgments against the wicked, used to comfort the godly, lest they should faint.
23:32:19: They shall not need to build it in high places for fear of the enemy: for God will defend it, and turn away the storms from hurting of their commodities.
23:32:20: The fields shall be so rank, that they shall send out their cattle to eat up the first crop, which abundance shall be signs of God’s love and favor toward them.
That is, upon fat ground and well watered, which bringeth forth in abundance, or in places which before were covered with waters, and now made dry for your uses.
23:33:1: The Chaldeans shall do like to the Assyrians, as the Assyrians did to Israel, and the Medes and Persians shall do the same to the Chaldeans.
Meaning, the enemies of the Church, as were the Chaldeans and Assyrians, but chiefly of Sennacherib, but not only.
When thine appointed time shall come that God shall take away thy power: and that which thou hast wrongfully gotten, shall be given to others, as Amos 5:11.
23:33:2: Which helped our fathers so soon as they called upon thee.
He declareth hereby what is the chief refuge of the faithful, when troubles come, to pray, and seek help of God.
23:33:3: When thou, O Lord, didst lift up thine arm to punish thine enemies.
That is, the Assyrians fled before the army of the Chaldeans, or the Chaldeans for fear of the Medes and Persians.
23:33:4: Ye that as caterpillars destroyed with your number the whole world, shall have no strength to resist your enemies the Chaldeans: but shall be gathered on an heap and destroyed.
Meaning, the Medes and Persians against the Chaldeans.
23:33:6: That is, in the days of Hezekiah.
23:33:7: Whom they of Jerusalem sent to entreat of peace.
23:33:8: These are the words of the ambassadors, when they returned from Sennacherib.
23:33:9: Which was a plentiful country, meaning, that Sennacherib would destroy all.
23:33:10: To help and deliver my Church.
23:33:11: This is spoken against the enemies, who thought all was their own: but he showeth that their enterprise shall be in vain, and that the fire which they had kindled for others, should consume them.
23:33:13: His vengeance shall be so great, that all the world shall talk thereof.
23:33:14: Which do not believe the words of the Prophet, and the assurance of their deliverance.
23:33:16: Meaning, that God will be a sure defense to all them that live according to his word.
23:33:17: They shall be no more shut in as they were of Sennacherib, but go where it pleaseth them.
They shall see Hezekiah delivered from his enemies, and restored to honor and glory.
23:33:18: Before that this liberty cometh thou shalt think that thou art in great danger: for the enemy shall so sharply assail you, that one shall cry, where is the clerk that writeth the names of them that are taxed? another, Where is the receiver? another shall cry for him that valueth the rich houses, but God will deliver you from this fear.
23:33:21: Let us be content with this small river of Shiloah and not desire the great streams and rivers, whereby the enemies may bring in ships and destroy us.
23:33:23: He derideth the Assyrians and enemies of the Church, declaring their destruction as they that perish by shipwreck.
He comforteth the Church, and showeth that they shall be enriched with all benefits both of body and soul.
23:34:1: He prophesieth of the destruction of the Edomites and other nations which were enemies to the Church.
23:34:2: God hath determined in his counsel, and hath given sentence for their destruction.
23:34:4: He speaketh this in respect of man’s judgment, who in great fear and horrible troubles, thinketh that heaven and earth perisheth.
23:34:5: They had an opinion of holiness, because they came of the Patriarch Isaac, but in effect were accursed of God, and enemies unto his Church, as the Papists are.
I have determined in my secret counsel, and in the heavens to destroy them till my sword be weary with shedding of blood.
23:34:6: That is, both of young and old, poor and rich of his enemies.
That famous city shall be consumed as a sacrifice burnt to ashes.
23:34:7: The mighty and rich shall be as well destroyed as the inferiors.
23:34:9: He alludeth to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Gen. 19:24.
23:34:11: In vain shall any man go about to build it again.
23:34:12: Meaning, here shall be neither order nor policy, nor state of commonweal.
23:34:15: Signifying, that Edom should be an horrible desolation and barren wilderness.
23:34:16: That is, the mouth of the Lord.
That is, in the Law where such curses are threatened against the wicked.
23:34:17: He hath given the beasts and fowls Edom for an inheritance.
23:35:1: He prophesieth of the full restoration of the Church both of the Jews and Gentiles under Christ, which shall be fully accomplished at the last day: albeit as yet it is compared to a desert and wilderness.
23:35:2: The Church which was before compared to a barren wilderness shall by Christ be made most plenteous and beautiful.
He showeth that the presence of God is the cause that the Church doth bring forth fruit and flourish.
23:35:3: He willeth all to encourage one another, and specially the ministers to exhort and strengthen the weak, that they may patiently abide the coming of God, which is at hand.
23:35:5: When the knowledge of Christ is revealed.
23:35:6: They that were barren and destitute of the graces of God, shall have them given by Christ.
23:35:8: It shall be for the Saints of God and not for the wicked.
God shall lead and guide them, alluding to the bringing forth of Egypt.
23:35:9: As he threateneth to the wicked to be destroyed hereby, Isa. 30:6.
23:35:10: Whom the Lord shall deliver from the captivity of Babylon.
23:36:1: When he had abolished superstition, and idolatry, and restored religion, yet God would exercise his Church to try their faith and patience.

This history is rehearsed because it is as a seal and confirmation of the doctrine afore, both for the threatenings and promises: to wit, that God would suffer his Church to be afflicted, but at length would send deliverance.
23:36:3: For he was now restored to his office, as Isaiah had prophesied, Isa. 22:20.
This declareth that there were few godly to be found in the king’s house, when he was driven to send this wicked man in such a weighty matter.
23:36:5: He speaketh this in the person of Hezekiah, falsely charging him that he put his trust in his wit and eloquence, whereas his only confidence was in the Lord.
23:36:6: Satan labored to pull the godly King from one vain confidence to another: to wit, from trust in the Egyptians, whose power was weak and would deceive them, to yield himself to the Assyrians, and so not to hope for any help of God.
23:36:9: He reproacheth to Hezekiah his small power, which is not able to resist one of Sennacherib’s least captains.
23:36:10: Thus the wicked to deceive us, will pretend the Name of the Lord: but we must try the spirits, whether they be of God or no.
23:36:11: They were afraid, lest by his words, he should have stirred up the people against the King, and also pretended to grow to some appointment with him.
23:36:12: Hebrew, the water of their feet.
23:36:16: The Hebrew word signifieth blessing, whereby this wicked captain would have persuaded the people, that their condition should be better under Sennacherib than under Hezekiah.
23:36:19: That is, of Antioch in Syria, of the which these two other cities also were: whereby we see how every town had his peculiar idol, and how the wicked make God an idol because they do not understand that God maketh them his scourge, and punisheth cities for sin.
23:36:21: Not that they did not show by evident signs that they did detest his blasphemy: for they had now rent their clothes, but they knew it was in vain to use long reasoning with this infidel, whose rage they should have so much more provoked.
23:37:1: In sign of grief and repentance.
23:37:2: To have comfort of him by the word of God, that his faith might be confirmed and so his prayer be more earnest: teaching hereby that in all dangers these two are the only remedies, to seek unto God and his ministers.
23:37:3: We are in as great sorrow as a woman that travaileth of child, and cannot be delivered.
23:37:4: That is, will declare by effect that he hath heard it: for when God deferreth to punish, it seemeth to the flesh, that he knoweth not the sin, or heareth not the cause.
Declaring that the minister’s office doth not only stand in comforting by the word, but also in praying for the people.
23:37:7: Of the Egyptians and Ethiopians, that shall come and fight against him.
23:37:8: Which was a city toward Egypt, thinking thereby to have stayed the force of his enemies.
23:37:10: Thus God would have him to utter a most horrible blasphemy before his destruction: as to call the author of all truth, a deceiver: some gather hereby that Shebna had disclosed unto Sennacherib the answer that Isaiah sent to the king.
23:37:12: Which was a city of the Medes.
Called also Charre a city in Mesopotamia, whence Abraham came after his father’s death.
23:37:16: He groundeth his prayer on God’s promise, who promised to hear them from between the Cherubims.
23:37:20: He declareth for what cause he prayed, that they might be delivered: to wit, that God might be glorified thereby through all the world.
23:37:22: Whom God had chosen to himself as a chaste virgin, and over whom he had care to preserve her from the lusts of the tyrant, as a father would have over his daughter.
23:37:23: Declaring hereby that they that are enemies to God’s Church, fight against him whose quarrel his Church only maintaineth.
23:37:25: He boasteth of his policy, in that that he can find means to nourish his army: and of his power in that that his army is so great, that it is able to dry up whole rivers, and to destroy the waters which the Jews had closed in.
23:37:26: Signifying, that God made not his Church to destroy it, but to preserve it: and therefore he saith that he formed it of old, even in his eternal counsel which cannot be changed.
23:37:27: He showeth that the state and power of most flourishing cities endureth but a moment in respect of the Church, which shall remain forever, because God is the maintainer thereof.
23:37:29: Because Sennacherib showed himself, as a devouring fish and furious beast, he useth these similitudes, to teach how he will take him and guide him.
23:37:30: God giveth signs after two sorts: some go before the thing, as the signs that Moses wrought in Egypt, which were for the confirmation of their faith, and some go after the thing, as the sacrifice, which they were commanded to make three days after their departure: and these latter are to keep the benefits of God in our remembrance: of the which sort this here is.
He promiseth that for two years the ground of itself should feed them.
23:37:31: They whom God hath delivered out of the hands of the Assyrians, shall prosper: and this properly belongeth to the Church.
23:37:35: For my promise sake made to David.
23:37:37: Which was the chiefest city of the Assyrians.
23:37:38: Who was also called Sardanapalus, in whose days ten years after Sennacherib’s death the Chaldeans overcame the Assyrians by Merodach their king.
23:38:1: Soon after that the Assyrians were slain: so that God will have the exercise of his children continually, that they may learn only to depend upon God and aspire to the heavens.
23:38:2: For his heart was touched with fear of God’s judgment, seeing he had appointed him to die so quickly after his deliverance from so great calamity, as one unworthy to remain in that estate, and also foreseeing the great change that should come in the Church, forasmuch as he left no son to reign after him: for as yet Manasseh was not born, and when he reigned, we see what a tyrant he was.
23:38:6: He doth not only promise to prolong his life, but to give him rest and quietness from the Assyrians, who might have renewed their army to revenge their former discomfiture.
23:38:7: For Hezekiah had asked for the confirmation of his faith, a sign, as verse 22, and 2 Kings 20:8, whereunto he was moved by the singular motion of God’s spirit.
23:38:9: He left this song of his lamentation and thanksgiving to all posterity, as a monument of his own infirmity and thankful heart for God’s benefits, as David did, Ps. 51.
23:38:10: At what time it was told me, that I should die.
23:38:11: I shall no more praise the Lord here in this Temple among the faithful: thus God suffereth his dearest children to want his consolation for a time, that his grace afterward may the more appear when they feel their own weakness.
23:38:12: That is, in one day, or shortly.
By my sin I have provoked God to take my life from me.
23:38:13: Over night I thought that I should live till morning, but my pangs in the night persuaded me the contrary: he showeth the horror that the faithful have when they apprehend God’s judgment against their sin.
23:38:14: To wit, sorrow and grief both of the body and mind.
I was so oppressed with sorrow, that I was not able to utter my words, but only to groan and sigh.
23:38:15: I shall have no release, but continual sorrows while I live.
God hath declared by his Prophet that I shall die and therefore I will yield unto him.
23:38:16: They that shall overlive the men that are now alive, and all they that are in these years shall acknowledge this benefit.
That after that thou hadst condemned me to death thou restoredst me to life.
23:38:17: He esteemeth more the remission of his sins, and God’s favor than a thousand lives.
Whereas I thought to have lived in rest and ease being delivered from mine enemy, I had grief upon grief.
23:38:18: Forasmuch as God hath placed man in this world to glorify him, the godly take it as a sign of his wrath, when their days were shortened, either because that they seemed unworthy for their sins to live longer in his service, or for their zeal to God’s glory, seeing that there are so few in earth that do regard it, as Ps. 6:5; 115:17.
23:38:19: All posterity shall acknowledge, and the fathers according to their duty toward their children shall instruct them in thy graces, and mercies toward me.
23:38:20: He showeth what is the use of the Congregation and Church, to wit, to give the Lord thanks for his benefits.
23:39:1: Partly moved with the greatness of the miracle, partly because he showed himself enemy to his enemies, but chiefly because he would join with them whom God favored, and have their help, if occasion served.
This was the first king of Babylon, which overcame the Assyrians in the tenth year of his reign.
23:39:4: He asketh him of the particulars, to make him understand the craft of the wicked, which he before being overcome with their flattery and blinded with ambition, could not see.
23:39:6: By the grievousness of the punishment is declared how greatly God detested ambition and vain glory.
23:40:1: This is a consolation for the Church, assuring them, that they shall be never destitute of Prophets whereby he exhorteth the true ministers of God that then were, and those also that should come after him, to comfort the poor afflicted, and to assure them of their deliverance both of body and soul.
23:40:2: Meaning, sufficient, as Isa. 61:7, and full correction, or double grace, whereas she deserved double punishment.
23:40:3: That is, in Babylon and other places, where they were kept in captivity, and misery.

Meaning Cyrus and Darius which should deliver God’s people out of captivity, and make them a ready way to Jerusalem: and this was fully accomplished, when John the Baptist brought tidings of Jesus Christ’s coming, who was the true deliverer of his Church from sin and Satan, Matt. 3:3.
23:40:4: Whatsoever may let or hinder this deliverance, shall be removed.
23:40:5: This miracle shall be so great, that it shall be known through all the world.
23:40:6: Meaning, all man’s wisdom and natural powers, James 1:10; 1 Pet. 1:24.
The voice of God which spake to the Prophet Isaiah.
23:40:7: The spirit of God shall discover the vanity in all that seem to have any excellency of themselves.
23:40:8: Though considering the frailty of man’s nature many of the Jews should perish, and so not be partakers of this deliverance, yet God’s promise should be fulfilled, and they that remained, should feel the fruit thereof.
23:40:9: He showeth at one word the perfection of all man’s felicity, which is to have God’s presence.
To publish this benefit through all the world.
23:40:10: His power shall be sufficient without help of any other, and shall have all means in himself to bring his will to pass.
23:40:11: He shall show his care and favor over them that are weak and tender.
23:40:12: Declaring that as God only hath all power, so doth he use the same for the defense and maintenance of his Church.
23:40:13: He showeth God’s infinite wisdom for the same.
23:40:17: He speaketh all this to the intent that they should neither fear man nor put their trust in any, save only in God.
23:40:18: Hereby he armeth them against the idolatry, wherewith they should be tempted in Babylon.
23:40:20: He showeth the rage of the idolaters, seeing that the poor that have not to suffice their own necessities, will defraud themselves to serve their idols.
23:40:21: Can you not learn by the visible creatures whom God hath made to observe your use, that you should not serve them nor worship them?
Have ye not the word of God, which plainly condemneth idolatry?
23:40:24: So that his power appeareth in every place wheresoever we turn our eyes.
23:40:26: Who hath set in order the infinite number of the stars.
23:40:27: He rebuketh the Jews, because they did not rest on the providence of God, but thought that he had forsaken them in their troubles.
23:40:28: Showing that men must patiently abide, and not curiously seek out the cause of God’s delay in our afflictions.
And therefore all power is in his hand to deliver when his time cometh.
23:40:30: They that trust in their own virtue, and do not acknowledge that all cometh of God.
23:41:1: That is, gather all their power and supports.
God as though he pleaded his cause with all nations, requireth silence, that he may be heard in his right.
23:41:2: Who called Abraham (who was the pattern of God’s justice in delivering his Church) from the idolatry of the Chaldeans to go to and fro at his commandment, and placed him in the land of Canaan.
23:41:4: Who hath created man and maintained his succession.
Though the world set up never so many gods, yet they diminish nothing of my glory: for I am all one, unchangeable, which have ever been, and shall be forever.
23:41:5: Considering mine excellent works among my people.
They assembled themselves and conspired against me to maintain their idolatry.
23:41:6: He noteth the obstinacy of the idolaters to maintain their superstitions.
23:41:8: And therefore oughtest not to pollute thyself with the superstition of the Gentiles.
23:41:10: That is, by the force of promise, in the performance whereof I will show myself faithful and just.
23:41:14: Thus he calleth them because they were contemned of all the world, and that they considering their own poor estate, should seek unto him for help.
23:41:15: I will make thee able to destroy all thine enemies, be they never so mighty: and this chiefly is referred to the kingdom of Christ.
23:41:17: That is, they that shall be afflicted in the captivity of Babylon.
23:41:18: God will rather change the order of nature than they should want anything, that cry to him by true faith in their miseries: declaring to them hereby that they shall lack nothing by the way, when they return from Babylon.
23:41:20: That is, hath appointed and determined that it shall come so to pass.
23:41:21: He biddeth the idolaters to prove their religion, and to bring forth their idols, that they may be tried whether they know all things, and can do all things: which if they cannot do, he concludeth that they are no gods, but vile idols.
23:41:24: So that a man cannot make an idol, but he must do that which God detesteth and abhoreth: for he chooseth his own devices and forsaketh the Lord’s.
23:41:25: Both of the Chaldeans and others.
That is, Cyrus, who shall do all things in my name and by my direction: whereby he meaneth that both their captivity and deliverance shall be ordered by God’s providence and appointment.
23:41:26: Meaning, that none of the Gentile gods can work any of these things.
23:41:27: To wit, a continual succession of Prophets and ministers.
That is, the Israelites which return from the captivity.
23:41:28: When I looked whether the idols could do these things, I found that they had neither wisdom nor power to do anything: therefore he concludeth that all are wicked, that trust in such vanities.
23:42:1: He shall declare himself governor over the Gentiles, and call them by his word, and rule them by his Spirit.

That is, Christ, who in respect of his manhood is called here servant. The Prophets used to make mention of Christ after that they have declared any great promise, because he is the foundation whereupon all the promises are made and ratified.
For I have committed all my power to him, as to a most faithful steward: Some read, I will establish him: to wit, in his office by giving him the fullness of my Spirit.
He only is acceptable to me, and they that come unto me by him: for there is no other means of reconciliation, Matt. 12:18; Eph. 4:1.
23:42:2: His coming shall not be with pomp and noise, as earthly princes.
23:42:3: Meaning, the wick of a lamp, or candle which is almost out, but he will cherish it and snuff it, that it may shine brighter.
He will not hurt the weak and feeble, but support and comfort them.
Although he favor the weak, yet will he not spare the wicked, but will judge them according to truth and equity.
23:42:4: Till he have set all things in good order.
The Gentiles shall be desirous to receive his doctrine.
23:42:6: Meaning, unto a lawful and just vocation.
As him, by whom the promise made to all nations in Abraham shall be fulfilled.
23:42:8: I will not suffer my glory to be diminished: which I should do if I were not faithful in performing the same, and the idolaters thereby would extol their idols above me.
23:42:9: As in time past I have been true in my promises, so will I be in time to come.
23:42:11: Meaning, the Arabians, under whom he comprehendeth all the people of the East.
23:42:13: He showeth the zeal of the Lord, and his power in the conservation of his Church.
23:42:14: I will haste to execute my vengeance, which I have so long deferred as a woman that desireth to be delivered, when she is in travail.
23:42:16: That is, my poor people, which are in perplexity and care.
23:42:19: The Priest to whom my word is committed, which should not only hear it himself, but cause others to hear it.
To wit, Israel, which should have most light because of my Law.
As the Priests and Prophets that should be lights to others?
23:42:22: Because they will not acknowledge this benefit of the Lord, who is ready to deliver them, he suffereth them to be spoiled of their enemies through their own fault and incredulity.
There shall be none to succor them, or to will the enemy to restore that which he hath spoiled.
23:43:1: After these threatenings he promiseth deliverance to his Church, because he hath regenerated them, adopted them, and called them.
When thou seest dangers and conspiracies on all sides, remember this benefit and the love of thy God, and it shall encourage thee.
23:43:2: By water and fire he meaneth all kind of troubles and perils.
23:43:3: I turned Sennacherib’s power against these countries, and made them to suffer that affliction which thou shouldest have done, and so were as the payment of thy ransom, Isa. 37:9.
23:43:4: I will not spare any man, rather than thou shouldest perish, for God more esteemeth one of his faithful than all the wicked in the world.
23:43:5: He prophesieth of their deliverance from the captivity of Babylon, and so of the calling of the universal Church, alluding to that which is written, Deut. 30:3.
23:43:7: Meaning, that he could not be unmindful of them, except he would neglect his own Name and glory.
23:43:9: Showing, that the malice of the wicked hindereth them in the knowledge of the truth, because they will not hear when God speaketh by his word.
Signifying, that no power can resist him in doing this miraculous work, nor all their idols are able to do the like, as Isa. 41:22.
To prove that the things which are spoken of them, are true.
23:43:10: Meaning specially Christ, and by him all the faithful.
The Prophets and people to whom I have given my Law.
23:43:14: They shall cry when they would escape by my water, seeing that the course of Euphrates is turned another way by the enemy.
23:43:16: When he delivered Israel from Pharaoh, Exod. 14:22.
When the Israelites passed through Jordan, Josh. 3:17.
23:43:17: When he delivered his people out of Egypt.
23:43:19: Meaning, that their deliverance out of Babylon should be more famous than that from Egypt was, Jer. 23:7; Hag. 2:10; 2 Cor. 5:17; Rev. 21:5, 7.
23:43:20: They shall have such abundance of all things as they return home, even in the dry and barren places, that the very beasts shall feel my benefits, and shall acknowledge them: much more men ought to be thankful for the same.
23:43:22: Thou hast not worshipped me as thou oughtest to have done.

Because thou hast not willingly received that which I did command thee, thou didst grieve me. Whereby he showeth that his mercies were the only cause of their deliverance, forasmuch as they had deserved the contrary.
23:43:23: Meaning, in true faith and obedience.
23:43:24: Either for the composition of the sweet ointment, Exod. 30:34, or for the sweet incense, Exod. 30:7.
Thou hast made me to bear an heavy burden by thy sins.
23:43:26: If I forget anything that may make for thy justification, put me in remembrance and speak for thyself.
23:43:28: That is, rejected, abhorred, and destroyed them in the wilderness and at other times.
23:44:2: He treated and chose thee from the beginning of his own mercy, and before thou couldest merit anything.
Whom God accepteth as righteous: or which haddest occasion thereunto because of the Law, and of thine holy vocation.
23:44:3: Because man of himself is as the dry and barren land, he promiseth to moisten him with the waters of his holy Spirit, Joel 2:28; John 7:38; Acts 2:17.
23:44:4: That is, thy children and posterity shall increase wonderfully after their deliverance from Babylon.
23:44:5: By this diversity of speech he meaneth one thing, that is, that the people shall be holy, and receive the true religion of God, as Ps. 87:5.
23:44:6: I am always like myself, that is, merciful toward my Church, and most able to maintain it, as Isa. 41:4 and 48:12; Rev. 1:17 and 22:13.
23:44:7: And appoint them that shall deliver the Church.
That is, declare unto me how I ought to proceed herein.
God calleth the Israelites ancient, because he preferred them to all others in his eternal election.
23:44:9: Whatsoever they bestow upon their idols, to make them to seem glorious.
That is, the idolaters seeing their idols blind, most needs be witnesses of their own blindness, and feeling that they are not able to help them, must confess that they have no power.
23:44:10: Meaning, that whatsoever is made by the hand of man, if he be esteemed as God, is most detestable.

Whereby appeareth their blasphemy, which call images the books of the laity, seeing that they are not only here called unprofitable, but Isa 41:24 abominable, and Jeremiah calleth them the work of errors, Jer. 10:15; Habakkuk, a lying teacher, Hab. 2:18.
23:44:11: Signifying, that the multitude shall not then save the idolaters, when God will take vengeance, although they excuse themselves thereby among men.
That is, which by any way consent either to the making or worshipping.
23:44:12: He describeth the raging affection of the idolaters, which forget their own necessities to set forth their devotion toward their idols.
23:44:13: To place it in some Temple.
23:44:15: He setteth forth the obstinacy and malice of the idolaters, which though they see by daily experience that their idols are no better than the rest of the matter whereof they are made, yet they refuse the one part, and make a god of the other, as the Papists make their cake god, and the rest of their idols.
23:44:16: That is, he either maketh a table or trenchers.
23:44:18: The Prophet giveth here an answer to all them that wonder how it is possible that any should be so blind to commit such abomination, saying, that God hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their hearts.
23:44:20: He is abused as one that would eat ashes, thinking to satisfy his hunger.
23:44:21: Showing that man’s heart is most inclined to idolatry, and therefore he warneth his people by these examples, that they should not cleave to any but to the living God, when they should be among the idolaters.
23:44:23: He showeth that the work of the Lord toward his people shall be so great, that the insensible creatures shall be moved therewith.
23:44:25: He armeth them against the soothsayers of Babylon, which would have borne them in hand, that they knew by the stars, that God would not deliver them, and that Babylon should stand.
23:44:26: Of Isaiah and the rest of his Prophets, which did assure the Church of God’s favor and deliverance.
23:44:27: He showeth that God’s work should be no less notable in this their deliverance, than when he brought them out of Egypt, through the sea.
23:44:28: To assure them of their deliverance, he nameth the person by whom it should be, more than an hundred years before he was born.
23:45:1: To assure the Jews of their deliverance against the great tentations that they should abide, he nameth the person and the means.
To guide him in the deliverance of my people.
Because Cyrus should execute the office of a deliverer, God called him his anointed for a time, but after another sort than he called David.
23:45:2: I will take away all impediments and lets.
23:45:3: Not that Cyrus did know God to worship him aright, but he had a certain particular knowledge as profane men may have of his power, and so was compelled to deliver God’s people.
23:45:4: Not for any thing that is in thee, or for thy worthiness.
23:45:5: I have given thee strength, power and authority.
23:45:7: I send peace and war, prosperity and adversity, as Amos 3:6.
23:45:8: I have appointed Cyrus to this use and purpose.

He comforteth the Jews, as if he would say, Though when ye look to the heavens and earth for succor, ye see nothing now but signs of God’s wrath, yet will cause them to bring forth most certain tokens of your deliverance, and of the performance of my promise: which is meant by righteousness.
23:45:9: That is, it is not perfectly made.
Hereby he bridleth their impatience, which in adversity and trouble murmur against God, and will not tarry his pleasure: willing that man should match with his like, and not contend against God.
23:45:11: Instead of murmuring, humble yourselves, and ask what ye will for the consolation of my children, and you shall be sure of it, as ye are of these things which are at your commandment. Some read it with an interrogation, and make it the application of the similitude.
23:45:13: To wit, Cyrus, that I may show by him the faithfulness of my promise in delivering my people.
Meaning, freely and without ransom, or any grievous condition.
23:45:14: These people were tributaries to the Persians, and so king Artaxerxes gave this money toward the building of the Temple, Ezra 7:27.
Whereas to fore they were thine enemies, they shall now honor thee, and thou shalt rule them: which was accomplished in the time of Christ.
23:45:15: Hereby he exhorteth the Jews to patience, though their deliverance be deferred for a time: showing that they should not repent their long patience, but the wicked and idolaters shall be destroyed.
23:45:18: To wit, of men, but chiefly of his Church.
23:45:19: As do the false gods, which give uncertain answers.
23:45:20: All ye idolaters which though you seem to have never so much worldly dignity, yet in God’s sight you are vile and abject.
23:45:22: He calleth the idolaters to repentance, willing them to look unto him with the eye of faith.
23:45:23: That is, that the thing which I have promised shall be faithfully performed.

The knowledge of God and the true worshipping shall be through all the world, Rom. 14:11; Phil. 2:10, whereby he signifieth that we must not only serve God in heart, but declare the same also by outward profession.
23:45:24: Meaning, the faithful shall feel and confess this.
23:46:1: These were the chief idols of Babylon.
Because they were of gold and silver, the Medes and Persians carried them away.
23:46:2: He derideth the idols, which had neither soul nor sense.
The beasts that carried the idols, fell down under their burden.
23:46:3: He showeth the difference between the idols and the true God: for they must be carried of others, but God himself carrieth his, as Deut. 32:11.
23:46:4: Seeing I have begotten you, I will nourish and preserve you forever.
23:46:5: The people of God, setting their own calamity, and the flourishing estate of the Babylonians, should be tempted to think that their God was not so mighty as the idols of their enemies: therefore he describeth the original of all the idols to make them to be abhorred of all men: showing that the most that can be spoken in their commendation, is but to prove them vile.
23:46:8: Become wise, meaning, that all idolaters are without wit or sense, like mad men.
23:46:11: That is, Cyrus, which shall come as swift as a bride, and fight against Babylon.
Him by whom I have appointed to execute that which I have determined.
23:46:12: Which by your incredulity would let the performance of my promise.
23:46:13: He showeth that man’s incredulity cannot abolish the promise of God, Rom. 3:3.
23:47:1: Thy government shall be taken from thee.
Which hast lived in wealth and wantonness, and hast not yet been overcome by any enemy.
23:47:2: Thou shalt be brought to most vile servitude: for to turn the mill was the office of slaves.
The things wherein she setteth her greatest pride, shall be made vile, even from the head to the foot.
23:47:3: I will use no humanity nor pity toward thee.
23:47:4: The Israelites shall confess that the Lord doeth this for his Church’s sake.
23:47:5: For very shame, and hide thyself.
23:47:6: They abused God’s judgments, thinking that he punished the Israelites, because he would utterly cast them off, and therefore instead of pitying their misery, thou didst increase it.
23:47:9: So that thy punishment shall be so great, as is possible to be imagined.
23:47:10: Thou didst think that thine own wisdom and policy would have saved thee.
23:47:12: He derideth their vain confidence, that put their trust in anything but in God, condemning also such vain sciences, which serve to no use, but to delude the people, and to bring them from depending only on God.
23:47:14: They shall utterly perish, and no part of them remain.
23:47:15: They shall flee everyone to that place, which he thought by his speculations to be most sure: but that shall deceive them.
23:48:1: He detecteth their hypocrisy which vaunteth themselves to be Israelites, and were not so indeed.
23:48:2: They make a show, as though they would have none other God.
23:48:3: He showeth that they could not accuse him in anything, forasmuch as he had performed whatsoever he had promised.
23:48:4: I have done for thee more than I promised, that thy stubbornness and impudence might have been overcome.
23:48:5: How thou shouldest be delivered out of Babylon.
23:48:6: Will ye not acknowledge this my benefit, and declare it unto others?
23:48:7: Showing that man’s arrogance is the cause why God doth not declare all things at once, lest they should attribute this knowledge to their own wisdom.
23:48:8: From the time that I brought thee out of Egypt: for that deliverance was as the birth of the Church.
23:48:9: As it was my free mercy that I did choose thee: so it is my free mercy that must save thee.
23:48:10: For I had respect to thy weakness and infirmity: for in silver there is some pureness, but in us there is nothing but dross.
I took thee out of the furnace where thou shouldest have been consumed.
23:48:11: God joineth the salvation of his with his own honor: so that they cannot perish, but his glory should be diminished, as Deut. 32:27.
23:48:13: To obey me, and to do whatsoever I command them.
23:48:14: Meaning, Cyrus, whom he had chosen to destroy Babylon.
23:48:16: Thus the Prophet speaketh for himself, and to assure them of these things.
Since the time that I declared myself to your fathers.
23:48:17: What things shall do thee good.
23:48:19: That is, the prosperous estate of Israel.
23:48:20: After that he had forewarned them of their captivity, and of the cause thereof, he showeth them the great joy that shall come of their deliverance.
23:48:21: He showeth that it shall be as easy to deliver them, as he did their fathers out of Egypt.
23:48:22: Thus he speaketh that the wicked hypocrites should not abuse God’s promise, in whom was neither faith nor repentance, as Isa. 57:21.
23:49:1: This is spoken in the person of Christ, to assure the faithful that these promises should come to pass: for they were all made in him, and in him should be performed.
This is meant of the time that Christ should be manifested to the world, as Ps. 2:7.
23:49:2: God hath taken me to his protection and defense: this chiefly is meant of Christ, and may also be applied to the ministers of his word.
By the sword and shaft, he signifieth the virtue and efficacy of Christ’s doctrine.
23:49:3: By Israel is meant Christ, and all the body of the faithful, as the members, and their head.
23:49:4: Thus Christ in his members complaineth, that his labor and preaching take none effect, yet he is contented that his doings are approved of God.
23:49:5: Though the Jews refuse my doctrine, yet God will approve my ministry.
23:49:6: To declare my Gospel, to the Gentiles, Isa. 42:6; Acts 13:47; Luke 2:32.
23:49:7: The benefit of their deliverance shall be so great, that great and small shall acknowledge it, and reverence God for it.
Meaning, the Jews, whom tyrants kept in bondage.
23:49:8: Signifying, that before Christ renew the earth by his word, there is nothing but confusion and disorder.
Thus he speaketh of his Church when he would show his mercy toward it, 2 Cor. 6:2.
23:49:9: Being in Christ’s protection, they shall be safe against all dangers, and free from the fear of the enemies.
To them that are in the prison of sin and death.
23:49:10: Meaning, that there should be nothing in their way from Babylon that should hinder or hurt them: but this is accomplished spiritually.
23:49:12: Meaning, the South country, so that Christ shall deliver his from all the parts of the world.
23:49:14: He objecteth what the faithful might say in their long affliction, and answereth thereunto to comfort them, with a most proper similitude, and full of consolation.
23:49:16: Meaning, the good order of policy, and discipline.
Because I would not forget thee.
23:49:17: I have continual care to build thee up again, and to destroy thine enemies.
23:49:18: He showeth what are the ornaments of the Church: to have many children, which are assembled by the word of God, and governed by his Spirit.
23:49:22: He showeth that Christ will not only gather this great number of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles.
23:49:23: Being joined with the Church, they shall humble themselves to Christ their head, and give him all honor.
Meaning, that Kings shall be converted to the Gospel, and bestow their power and authority for the preservation of the Church.
23:49:24: He maketh this as an objection, as though the Chaldeans were strong, and had them in just possession.
23:49:25: This is the answer to their objection, that none is stronger than the Lord, neither hath a more just title unto them.
23:49:26: I will cause them to destroy one another, as Judg. 7:22; 2 Chron. 20:22; Isa. 19:2.
23:50:1: Signifying, that he sold them not for any debt or poverty, but that they sold themselves to sins to buy their own lusts and pleasures.
Meaning, that he hath not forsaken her, but through her own occasion, as Hos. 2:2.
Which should declare that I have cut her off: meaning, that they could show none.
23:50:2: He came by his Prophets and ministers, but they would not believe their doctrine and convert.
Am I not able to help you, as I have helped your fathers of old, when I dried up the red Sea, and killed the fish in the rivers, and also afterward in Jordan?
23:50:3: As I did in Egypt in token of my displeasure, Exod. 10:21.
23:50:4: To him that is oppressed by affliction and misery.
The Prophet doth represent here the person and charge of them that are justly called to the ministry of God’s word.
As they that are taught, and made meet by him.
23:50:6: I did not shrink from God for any persecution or calamity. Whereby he showeth that the true ministers of God can look for none other recompense of the wicked, but after this sort, and also what is their comfort.
23:50:10: Showing that it is a rare thing that any should obey aright God’s true ministers, though they labor to bring them from hell to heaven.
23:50:11: You have sought consolation by your own devices, and have refused the light, and consolation which God hath offered: therefore ye shall remain in sorrow, and not be comforted.
23:51:1: That is, to Abraham, of whom ye were begotten, and to Sarah, of whom we were born.
He comforteth the Church, that they should not be discouraged for their small number.
23:51:4: I will rule and govern my Church by my word and doctrine.
23:51:5: The time that I will accomplish my promise.
23:51:6: He forewarneth them of the horrible changes and mutations of all things, and how he will preserve his church in the midst of all these dangers.
23:51:9: He putteth them in remembrance of his great benefit for their deliverance out of Egypt, that thereby they might learn to trust in him constantly.
23:51:14: He comforteth them by the short time of their banishment: for in seventy years they were restored, and the greatest empire of the world destroyed.
23:51:16: That all things may be restored in heaven and earth, Eph. 1:10.
Meaning, of Isaiah, and of all true ministers, who are defended by his protection.
23:51:17: Thou hast been justly punished and sufficiently as Isa. 40:2, and this punishment in the elect is by measure, and according as God giveth grace to bear it: but in the reprobate it is the just vengeance of God to drive them to an insensibleness and madness, as Jer. 25:15, 16.
23:51:19: Whereof the one is outward, as of the things that come to the body, as war, and famine, and the other is inward, and appertaineth to the mind: that is, to be without comfort: therefore he saith, How shalt thou be comforted?
23:52:1: No wicked tyrant, which shall subvert God’s true religion, and oppress the conscience.
23:52:2: Put off the garments of sorrow and heaviness, and put on the apparel of joy and gladness.
23:52:3: The Babylonians paid nothing to me for you: therefore I will take you again without ransom.
23:52:4: When Jacob went thither in time of famine.

The Egyptians might pretend some cause to oppress my people because they went thither, and remained among them, but the Assyrians have no title to excuse their tyranny by, and therefore will I punish them more than I did the Egyptians.
23:52:5: To wit, by the wicked, which think that I have no power to deliver them.
23:52:7: Signifying, that the joy and good tidings of their deliverance should make their affliction in the mean time more easy: but this is chiefly meant of the spiritual joy, as Nah. 1:15; Rom. 10:15.
23:52:8: The Prophets which are thy watchmen shall publish this thy deliverance: this was begun under Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah, but was accomplished under Christ.
23:52:10: As ready to smite his enemies, and to deliver his people.
23:52:11: He warneth the faithful not to pollute themselves with the superstitions of the Babylonians, as Isa. 48:20; 2 Cor. 6:17.

For the time is at hand that the Priests and Levites chiefly (and so by them all the people, which shall be as the Levites in this office) shall carry home vessels of the Temple which Nebuchadnezzar had taken away.
23:52:12: As your fathers did out of Egypt.
23:52:13: Meaning, Christ, by whom our spiritual deliverance should be wrought, whereof this was a figure.
23:52:14: In the corrupt judgment of man, Christ in his person was not esteemed.
By the preaching of the Gospel.
In sign of reverence, and as being astonished at his excellency.
He shall spread his word through many nations.
23:53:1: Meaning, that none can believe, but whose hearts God toucheth with the virtue of his holy Spirit.
The Prophet showeth that very few shall receive this their preaching of Christ, and of their deliverance by him, John 12:38; Rom. 10:16.
23:53:2: The beginning of Christ’s kingdom shall be small and contemptible in the sight of man, but it shall grow wonderfully, and flourish before God.
23:53:3: Which was by God’s singular providence for the comfort of sinners, Heb. 4:15.
23:53:4: We judgeth evil, thinking that he was punished for his own sins, and not for ours.
That is, the punishment due to our sins: for the which he hath both suffered and made satisfaction, Matt. 8:17; 1 Pet. 2:24.
23:53:5: He was chastised for our reconciliation, 1 Cor. 15:3.
23:53:6: Meaning, the punishment of our iniquity, and not the fault itself.
23:53:7: But willingly and patiently obeyed his father’s appointment, Matt. 26:63; Acts 8:32.
23:53:8: From the cross and grave, after that he was condemned.
Though he died for sin, yet after his resurrection he shall live forever and this his death is to restore life to his members, Rom. 6:9.
23:53:9: God the Father delivered him into the hands of the wicked, and to the powers of the world to do with him what they would.
23:53:10: Christ by offering up himself shall give life to his Church, and so cause them to live with him forever.
23:53:11: That is, the fruit and effect of his labor, which is the salvation of his Church.
Christ shall justify by faith through his word, whereas Moses could not justify by the law.
23:53:12: That is, of all that believe in him.
Because he humbled himself, therefore he shall be extolled to glory, Phil. 2:7-12.
23:54:1: The Church in this her affliction and captivity shall bring forth more children, than when she was at liberty: or this may be spoken by admiration, considering the great number that should come of her. Her deliverance under Cyrus was as her childhood, and therefore this was accomplished, when she came to her age, which was under the Gospel.

After that he hath declared the death of Christ, he speaketh to the Church, because it should feel the fruit of the same, and calleth her barren, because that in the captivity she was a widow without hope to have any children.
23:54:2: Signifying, that for the great number of children that God should give her, she should seem to lack room to lodge them.
23:54:4: The afflictions which thou suffered at the beginning.
When as thou wast refused for thy sins, Isa. 50:1.
23:54:5: His glory shall shine through the whole World, which seemed before to be shut up in Judea.
That did regenerate thee by his holy Spirit.
23:54:6: As a wife which wast forsaken in thy youth.
23:54:9: As sure as the promise that I made to Noah, that the waters should no more overflow the earth.
23:54:11: Hereby he declareth the excellent estate of the Church under Christ.
23:54:13: By the hearing of his word and inward moving of his Spirit.
23:54:14: In stability and sureness, so that it shall stand forever.
23:54:15: Meaning, the domestical enemies of the Church, as are the hypocrites.
23:54:16: Signifying hereby, that man can do nothing, but so far as God giveth power: for seeing that all are his creatures, he must needs govern and guide them.
23:55:1: Signifying, that God’s benefits cannot be bought for money.
By waters, wine, milk and bread, he meaneth all things necessary to the spiritual life, as these are necessary to this corporal life.

Christ by proposing his graces and gifts to his Church, exempteth the hypocrites which are full with their imagined works, and the Epicureans, which are full with their worldly lusts, and so thirst not after these waters.
23:55:2: He reproveth their ingratitude, which refuse those things that God offereth willingly, and in the meantime spare neither cost nor labor to obtain those which are nothing profitable.
23:55:3: The same covenant which through my mercy I ratified and confirmed to David, that it should be eternal, 2 Sam. 7:13; Acts 13:34.
23:55:4: Meaning Christ, of whom David was a figure.
23:55:5: To wit, the Gentiles, which before thou didst not receive to be thy people.
23:55:6: When he offereth himself by the preaching of his word.
23:55:7: Hereby he showeth that repentance must be joined with faith, and how we cannot call upon God aright, except the fruits of our faith appear.
23:55:8: Although you are not soon reconciled one to another and judge me by yourselves, yet I am most easy to be reconciled, yea, I offer my mercies to you.
23:55:11: If these small things have their effect, as daily experience showeth, much more shall my promise which I have made and confirmed, bring to pass the things which I have spoken for your deliverance.
23:55:13: Of God’s deliverance, and that he will never forsake his Church.
23:56:1: Which I will declare toward you, and pour into your hearts by my Spirit.
God showeth what he requireth of them after that he hath delivered them: to wit, the works of charity whereby true faith is declared.
23:56:2: Under the Sabbath he comprehendeth the whole service of God and true religion.
23:56:3: Let none think himself unmeet to receive the graces of the Lord: for the Lord will take away all impediments, and will forsake none which will keep his true religion, and believe in him.
23:56:5: They shall be called after my people, and be of the same religion: yea, under Christ the dignity of the faithful shall be greater than the Jews were at that time.
23:56:7: Not only for the Jews, but for all others, Matt. 21:13.
Hereby he meaneth the spiritual service of God, to whom the faithful offer continual thanksgiving, yea themselves and all that they have, as a lively and acceptable sacrifice.
23:56:9: Meaning, the enemies of the Church, as the Babylonians, Assyrians, etc., thus he speaketh to fear the hypocrites and to assure the faithful that when this cometh, they may know it was told them before.
23:56:10: He showeth that this affliction shall come through the fault of the governors, prophets, and pastors, whose ignorance, negligence, avarice and obstinacy provoked God’s wrath against them.
23:56:12: We are well yet, and tomorrow shall be better: therefore let us not fear the plagues before they come: thus the wicked contemned the admonitions and exhortations which were made them in the Name of God.
23:57:1: From the plague that is at hand, and also because God will punish the wicked.
23:57:2: The soul of the righteous shall be in joy, and their body shall rest in the grave unto the time of the resurrection, because they walked before the Lord.
23:57:3: He threateneth the wicked hypocrites, who under the pretence of the name of God’s people, derided God’s word and his promises: boasting openly that they were the children of Abraham, but because they were not faithful and obedient as Abraham was, he calleth them bastards, and the children of sorcerers, which forsook God, and fled to wicked means for succor.
23:57:6: Meaning, every place was polluted with their idolatry: or every fair stone that they found, they made an idol of it.
In the sacrifices which you offering before these idols, thought you did serve God.
23:57:7: To wit, thine altars in an open place, like an impudent harlot, that careth not for the sight of her husband.
23:57:8: That is, didst increase thine idolatry more and more.
Instead of setting up the word of God in the open places on the posts and doors to have it in remembrance, Deut. 6:9 and 27:1, thou hast set up signs and marks of thine idolatry in every place.
23:57:9: Thou didst seek the favor of the Assyrians by gifts and presents to help thee against the Egyptians: and when they failed thou soughtest to the Babylonians, and more and more didst torment thyself.
23:57:10: He derideth their unprofitable diligence, which thought to have made all sure, and yet were deceived.
Although thou sawest all thy labors to be in vain, yet wouldest thou never acknowledge thy fault, and leave off.
23:57:11: Meaning, that the wicked abuse God’s lenity, and grow to further wickedness.
23:57:12: That is, thy naughtiness, idolatries, and impieties which the wicked call God’s service: thus he derideth their obstinacy.
23:57:13: Meaning, the Assyrians and others, whose help they looked for.
23:57:14: God shall say to Darius and Cyrus.
23:57:16: I will not use my power against frail man, whose life is but a blast.
23:57:17: That is, for the vices and faults of the people, which is meant here by covetousness.
23:57:18: Though they were obstinate, yet I did not withdraw my mercy from them.
23:57:19: As well to him that is in captivity as to him that remaineth at home.
That is, I frame the speech and words of my messengers which shall bring peace.
23:57:20: Their evil conscience doth ever torment them, and therefore they can never have rest, read Isa. 48:22.
23:58:1: The Lord thus speaketh to the Prophet, willing him to use all diligence and severity to rebuke the hypocrites.
23:58:2: They will seem to worship me and have outward holiness.
23:58:3: He setteth forth the malice and disdain of the hypocrites, which grudge against God, if their works be not accepted.
Thus he convinceth the hypocrites by the second table, and by their duty toward their neighbor, that they have neither faith nor religion.
23:58:4: So long as you use contention and oppression, your fasting and prayers shall not be heard.
23:58:6: That you leave off all your extortions.
23:58:7: For in him thou seest thyself as in a glass.
23:58:8: The Testimony of thy goodness shall appear before God and man.
That is, the prosperous estate wherewith God will bless thee.
23:58:9: Whereby is meant all manner of injury.
23:58:10: That is, have compassion on their miseries.
Thine adversity shall be turned into prosperity.
23:58:12: Signifying, that of the Jews should come such as should build again the ruins of Jerusalem and Judea: but chiefly this is meant of the spiritual Jerusalem, whose builders were the Apostles.
23:58:13: If thou refrain thyself from thy wicked works.
23:59:4: According to their wicked devices, they hurt their neighbors.
All men wink at the injuries and oppressions, and none go about to remedy them.
23:59:5: They are profitable to no purpose.
Whatsoever cometh from them is poison, and bringeth death.
23:59:9: That is, God’s vengeance to punish our enemies.
23:59:10: We are altogether destitute of counsel, and can find no end of our miseries.
23:59:11: We express our sorrows by outward signs, some more, some less.
23:59:12: This confession is general to the Church to obtain remission of sins, and the Prophets did not exempt themselves from the same.
23:59:14: There is neither justice nor uprightness among men.
23:59:16: Meaning, to do justice, and to remedy the things that were so far out of order.
That is, his Church or his arm did help itself, and did not seek aid of any other.
23:59:17: Signifying, that God hath all means at hand to deliver his Church and to punish their enemies.
23:59:18: To wit, your enemies, which dwell in divers places, and beyond the sea.
23:59:19: He showeth that there shall be great affliction in the Church, but God will ever deliver his.
23:59:20: Whereby he declareth that the true deliverance from sin and Satan belongeth to none, but to the children of God, whom he justifieth.
23:59:21: Because the doctrine is made profitable by the virtue of the Spirit, he joineth the one with the other, and promiseth to give them both to his Church forever.
23:60:1: The time of thy prosperity and felicity: whereas speaking of Babylon, he commanded her to go down, Isa. 47:1.
23:60:2: Signifying, that all men are in darkness till God give them the light of his Spirit, and that this light shineth to none, but to those that are in his Church.
23:60:3: Meaning, that Judea should be as the morning star, and that the Gentiles should receive light of her.
23:60:4: An infinite number from all countries, as Isa. 49:18.
23:60:5: For joy, as the heart is drawn in for sorrow.
23:60:6: Meaning, that everyone shall honor the Lord with what wherewith he is able: signifying, that it is no true serving of God, except we offer ourselves to serve his glory, and all that we have.
23:60:7: Because the Altar was a figure of Christ, Heb. 13:10, he showeth that nothing can be acceptable to him, which is not offered to him by this Altar, who was both the offering and the altar itself.
That is, the Arabians, that have great abundance of cattle.
23:60:8: Showing what great number shall come to the Church, and with what great diligence and zeal.
23:60:9: The Gentiles that are now enemies, shall become friends and setters forth of the Church.
23:60:10: Meaning, Cyrus and his successors, but chiefly this is accomplished in them that serve Christ, being converted by his Gospel.
23:60:12: He showeth that God hath given all power and authority here in earth for the use of his Church, and that they which will not serve and profit the same, shall be destroyed.
23:60:13: There is nothing so excellent which shall not serve the necessity of the Church.
Signifying, that God’s Majesty is not included in the Temple, which is but the place for his feet, that we may learn to rise us to the heavens.
23:60:14: To worship their head Christ, by obeying his doctrine.
23:60:16: Both high and low shall be ready to help and succor thee.
23:60:17: Thy governors shall love thee, and seek thy wealth and prosperity.
23:60:18: Meaning, not a temporal felicity, but a spiritual, which is fulfilled in Christ’s kingdom.
23:60:19: Signifying, that all worldly means shall cease, and that Christ shall be all in all, as Rev. 21:23 and 22:5.
23:60:22: Meaning, that the Church should be miraculously multiplied.
23:61:1: Thus appertaineth to all the Prophets and ministers of God, but chiefly to Christ, of whose abundant graces everyone receiveth according as it pleaseth him to distribute.
To them that are lively touched with the feeling of their sins.
Which are in the bondage of sin.
23:61:2: The time when it pleased God to show his good favor to man, which S. Paul calleth the fullness of time, Gal. 4:4.
For when God delivereth his Church, he punisheth his enemies.
23:61:3: Which was the sign of mourning.
Trees that bring forth good fruits, as Matt. 3:8.
23:61:4: That is, for a long time.
23:61:5: They shall be ready to serve you in all your necessities.
23:61:6: This is accomplished in the time of Christ, by whom all the faithful are made Priests and Kings, 1 Pet. 2:9; Rev. 1:6 and 5:10.
23:61:7: Abundant recompense, as this word is used, Isa. 40:2.
Whereas the Gentiles had dominion over the Jews in times past, now they shall have double authority over them and possess twice so much.
23:61:8: I will not receive their offerings which are extortioners, deceivers, hypocrites, or that deprive me of my glory.
23:61:10: He showeth what shall be the affection, when they feel this their deliverance.
23:62:1: The Prophet saith that he will never cease to declare unto the people the good tidings of their deliverance.
Till they have full deliverance: and this the Prophet speaketh to encourage all other ministers to the setting forth of God’s mercies toward his Church.
23:62:2: Thou shalt have a more excellent fame than thou hast had hitherto.
23:62:3: He shall esteem thee as dear and precious as a king doth his crown.
23:62:4: Thou shalt no more be contemned as a woman forsaken of her husband.
That it may be replenished with children.
23:62:5: Forasmuch as they confess one faith and religion with thee, they are in the same bond of marriage with thee, and they are called the children of the Church, inasmuch as Christ maketh her plentiful to bring forth children unto him.
23:62:6: He exhorteth the ministers never to cease to call upon God by prayer for the deliverance of his Church, and to teach others to do the same.
23:62:7: For the restoration whereof all the world shall praise him.
23:62:10: Signifying the great number that should come to the Church, and what means he would prepare for the restitution of the same, as Isa. 57:14.
23:62:11: He shall have all power to bring his purpose to pass, as Isa. 40:10.
Ye Prophets and Ministers show the people of this their deliverance: which was chiefly meant of our salvation by Christ, Zech. 9:9; Matt. 21:5.
23:62:12: That is, one over whom God hath had a singular care to recover her when she was lost.
23:63:1: God answereth them that asked this question, Who is this? etc. and saith, Ye see now performed in deed the vengeance which my Prophets threatened.

This prophecy is against the Idumeans and enemies which persecuted the Church, on whom God will take vengeance, and is here set forth all bloody after he hath destroyed them in Bozrah, the chief city of the Idumeans: for these were their greatest enemies, and under the title of circumcision and the kindred of Abraham, claimed to themselves the chief religion, and hated the true worshippers, Ps. 137:7.
23:63:2: Another question, to the which the Lord answereth.
23:63:4: Showing that when God punisheth his enemies, it is for the profit and deliverance of his Church.
23:63:5: God showeth that he hath no need of man’s help for the deliverance of his, and though men refuse to do their duty through negligence and ingratitude, yet he himself will deliver his Church, and punish the enemies, read Isa. 59:16.
23:63:6: I will so astonish them and make them so giddy, that they shall not know which way to go.
23:63:7: The Prophet speaketh this to move the people to remember God’s benefits in times past, that they may be confirmed in their troubles.
23:63:8: For I did choose them to be mine, that they should be holy, and not deceive mine expectation.
23:63:9: Which was a witness of God’s presence, and this may be referred to Christ, to whom belongeth the office of Salvation.
He bare their afflictions and griefs as though they had been his own.
23:63:11: That is, in Moses that he might well govern the people: some refer this giving of the spirit to the people.
That is, the people of Israel, being afflicted, called to remembrance God’s benefits, which he had bestowed upon their fathers in times past.
23:63:13: Peaceably and gentle, as an horse is led to his pasture.
23:63:15: Meaning, from the whole body of the Church.
Having declared God’s benefits showed to their forefathers, he turned himself to God by prayer, desiring him to continue the same graces toward them.
Thy great affection, which thou barest towards us.
23:63:16: Though Abraham would refuse us to be his children, yet thou wilt not refuse to be our father.
23:63:17: By taking away the holy Spirit from us, by whom we were governed, and so for our ingratitude didst deliver us up to our own concupiscence, and didst punish sin by sin according to thy just judgment.
Meaning, for the Covenant’s sake made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob his servants.
23:63:18: That is, in respect of the promise, which is perpetual: albeit they had now possessed the land of Canaan, a thousand and four hundred years: and thus they lament, to move God rather to remember his Covenant, than to punish their sins.
23:64:1: The Prophet continueth his prayer, desiring God to declare his love toward his Church by miracles, and mighty power, as he did in mount Sinai.
23:64:2: Meaning, the rain, hail, fire, thunder, and lightnings.
23:64:4: S. Paul useth the same kind of admiration, 1 Cor. 2:9, marveling at God’s great benefit showed to his Church, by the preaching of the Gospel.
23:64:5: That is, in thy mercies, which he calleth the ways of the Lord.
Thou wilt have pity upon us.
Thou showedst favor toward our fathers, when they trusted in thee, and walked after thy Commandments.
23:64:6: We are justly punished and brought into captivity, because we have provoked thee to anger, and though we would excuse ourselves, yet our righteousness, and best virtues are before thee as vile cloths, or (as some read) like the menstruous clothes of a woman.
23:64:8: Albeit, O Lord, by thy just judgment thou mayest utterly destroy us as the potter may his pot, yet we appeal to thy mercies, whereby it hath pleased thee to adopt us to be thy children.
23:64:9: For so the flesh judgeth when God doth not immediately send succor.
23:64:10: Which were dedicated to thy service, and to call upon thy Name.
23:64:11: Wherein we rejoiced and worshipped thee.
23:64:12: That is, at the contempt of thine own glory? though our sins have deserved this, yet thou wilt not suffer thy glory thus to be diminished.
23:65:1: Meaning, the Gentiles which knew not God, should seek after him, when he had moved their heart with his holy Spirit, Rom. 10:20.
23:65:2: He showeth that to delight in our own fantasies, is the declining from God and the beginning of all superstition and Idolatry.
He showeth the cause of the rejection of the Jews, because they would not obey him for any admonition of his Prophets, by whom he called them continually and stretched out his hand to draw them.
23:65:3: Meaning, their altars, which he thus named by contempt.
23:65:4: Which was contrary to God’s Commandment, Lev. 11:7; Deut. 14:8.
To consult with spirits, and to conjure devils, which was forbidden, Deut. 18:11.
23:65:5: Their punishment shall never have end.
He showeth that hypocrisy is ever joined with pride and contempt of others.
23:65:6: So that the remembrance thereof cannot be forgotten.
23:65:7: Shall be both punished together: and this declareth how the children are punished for their fathers’ faults, to wit, when the same faults or like are found in them.
23:65:8: That is, it is profitable: meaning, that God will not destroy the faithful branches of his vineyard, when he destroyeth the rotten stocks, that is, the hypocrites.
23:65:10: Which was a plentiful place in Judea to feed sheep, as Achor was for cattle.
23:65:11: By the multitude and number he meaneth their innumerable idols of whom they thought they could never have enough.
23:65:12: By my Prophets, whom ye would not obey.
Seeing you cannot number your gods, I will number you with the sword.
23:65:13: By these words, Eat and drink, he meaneth, the blessed life of the faithful, which have always consolation and full contentment of all things in their God, though sometimes they lack these corporal things.
23:65:15: Meaning, that he would call the Gentiles, who should abhor even the very name of the Jews for their infidelities’ sake.
Than by the name of the Jews.
23:65:16: I will no more suffer my Church to be desolate as in times past.
By blessing, and by swearing is meant the praising of God for his benefits, and the true worshipping of him, which shall not be only in Judea, but through all the world.
23:65:17: I will so alter and change the state of my church, that it shall seem to dwell in a new world.
23:65:20: Meaning, in this wonderful restoration of the Church there should be no weakness of youth, nor infirmities of age, but all should be fresh and flourishing: and this is accomplished in the heavenly Jerusalem, when all sin shall cease, and the tears shall be wiped away.
Whereby he showeth that the infidels and unrepentant sinners have no part of this benediction.
23:65:21: He proposeth to the faithful the blessings which are contained in the Law, and so under temporal things comprehendeth the spiritual promises.
23:66:1: My majesty is so great, that it filleth both heaven and earth, and therefore cannot be included in a temple like an idol: condemning hereby their vain confidence, which trusted in the Temple and sacrifices.
23:66:2: Seeing that both the Temple and the things therein, with the sacrifices, were made and done by his appointment, he showeth that he hath no need thereof, and that he can be without them, Ps. 50:10.
To him that is humble and pure in heart, which receiveth my doctrine with reverence and fear.
23:66:3: Because the Jews thought themselves holy by offering of their sacrifices, and in the mean season had neither faith nor repentance, God showeth that he doth no less detest these ceremonies than he doth the sacrifices of the heathen, who offered men, dogs, and swine to their idols, which things were expressly forbidden in the Law.
23:66:4: I will discover their wickedness and hypocrisy, wherewith they think to blind mine eyes, to all the world.
23:66:5: He encourageth the faithful by promising to destroy their enemies, which pretended to be as brethren, but were hypocrites, and hated them that feared God.
23:66:6: The enemies shall shortly hear a more terrible voice, even fire and slaughter, seeing they would not hear the gentle voice of the Prophets, which called them to repentance.
23:66:7: Meaning, that the restoration of the Church should be so sudden and contrary to all men’s opinions, as when a woman is delivered before she looked for it, and that without pain in travail.
23:66:8: This shall pass the capacity of man to see such a multitude that shall come up at once, meaning, under the preaching of the Gospel, whereof they that came up out of Babylon were a sign.
23:66:9: Declaring hereby, that as in his power and providence women travailed and delivered, so he giveth the power to bring forth the Church at his time appointed.
23:66:11: That is, may rejoice for all the benefits that God bestoweth upon his Church.
23:66:12: I will give her felicity and prosperity in great abundance.
Ye shall be cherished as her dearly beloved children.
23:66:14: Ye shall have new strength and new beauty.
23:66:15: This vengeance God began to execute at the destruction of Babylon, and hath ever continued it against the enemies of his Church, and will do till the last day, which shall be the accomplishment thereof.
23:66:17: Whereby are meant them that did maliciously transgress the Law, by eating beasts forbidden, even to the mouse, which nature abhoreth.
23:66:18: The Gentiles shall be partakers of that glory, which before I showed to the Jews.
23:66:19: Meaning, the Apostles, Disciples, and others, which he did first choose of the Jews to preach unto the Gentiles.
To wit, Lydia, or Asia minor.
I will make these that I chose, that they perish not with the rest of the infidels: whereby he alludeth to the marking of the posts of his people, whom he preserved, Exod. 12:7.
I will scatter the rest of the Jews, which escaped destruction, into divers nations.
23:66:20: That is, the Gentiles, which by faith shall be made the children of Abraham as you are.
Whereby he meaneth that no necessary means shall want, when God shall call the Gentiles to the knowledge of the Gospel.
23:66:21: To wit, of the Gentiles, as he did Luke, Timothy, and Titus first, and others after to preach his word.
23:66:22: Hereby he signifieth the kingdom of Christ wherein his Church shall be renewed, and whereas before there were appointed seasons to sacrifice, in this there shall be one continual Sabbath, so that all times and seasons shall be meet.
23:66:24: Meaning, a continual torment of conscience, which shall ever gnaw them, and never suffer them to be at rest, Mark 9:44.
As he that declared the felicity that shall be within the Church for the comfort of the godly, so doth he show what horrible calamity shall come to the wicked, that are out of the Church.
This is the just recompense for the wicked, which contemning God and his word, shall be by God’s just judgment abhorred of all his creatures.
